[headline] Pottery, Crafts, and a Full Fredas Across the Holds

[dateline] Friday, November 13, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, guest of the Hearth, and a fine grey Fredas to you — the clouds hang low over the Rim, the air is cool at sixty-two, and the Holds have filled this Friday with honest making. Potters open their festival at D.A. Ranch in Cornville, Santa’s craft fair fills the Elks Lodge in Show Low, holiday crafts spread out in Prescott, and here in Payson an estate sale and a cozy women’s gathering bookend the day. Wrap up warm, by the Nine, and go see what your neighbors’ hands have made.

[hero_caption] Potters, crafters, and treasure hunters turn out across the Holds — clay on the wheel in the Verde Valley and holiday crafts in every hall.

[weather] Overcast high 62 low 45 rain 23% sunrise 6:56 AM sunset 5:22 PM tomorrow Light rain, 50/41

[weather_caption] Gandy holds court under the dry eaves while Maevy bats at a leaf the breeze keeps stealing.

[today Payson] Estate Sale — 703 N Manzanita Dr, Payson, today from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM, and again Saturday. Everything must go: furniture, Christmas decorations, wall art, camping equipment, and more, from a house full of Rim Country living. Treasure hunters should come early, for the good pieces walk out first. Bring cash, a truck if you can, and a hunter’s eye. This is the kind of sale that furnishes a cabin in one morning. | Jesus & Jammies — 1100 W Lake Dr, Payson, today at 6:00 PM, $5 tickets or donations, and no one turned away for hardship. A women’s slumber-party gathering with pajamas, childhood snacks, friendship bracelets, games, and sweet conversation about faith and friendship. You do not need to know anyone to come — you are welcome exactly as you are. Bring your inner little girl and a friend who could use a night of joy. Cozy is the whole point, and this Hold does cozy well.

[today Camp Verde] Verde Valley Pottery Festival — First Pick Friday — D.A. Ranch Vineyards, 1900 Dancing Apache Rd, Cornville, today from 4:00 to 6:00 PM, $25. The festival’s early-access preview gives guests first choice of handmade ceramic work, with D.A. Ranch wine, local food trucks, craft beer, and live music along Oak Creek. Arizona potters bring bowls, mugs, and sculpture to over a hundred acres of cottonwood-shaded farmland. Saturday and Sunday are free, but Friday is when the best pieces still stand on the tables. Makers and collectors, this is your hour.

[today Sedona] Gabriel & Co. Holiday Trunk Show — Renee Taylor Jewelry, Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village, 336 State Route 179, Sedona, today from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM, running November 13–15. Three festive days of jewelry sparkle to open the gift season, with Gabriel & Co. experts on hand for custom designs and festive refreshments while you shop. Bring the gift list and find the piece they will treasure for years. Tlaquepaque in the fall light is half the gift already. | Lil Fish with Govinda at Humankind — Humankind, 1730 W State Route 89A, Sedona, today from 5:00 PM to 1:00 AM. Frequency Friday opens the evening from 5:00 to 7:00 PM, Lady Merkaba opens the concert at 8:00 PM, Govinda plays live violin over deep bass at 9:15 PM, and Lil Fish closes from 10:45 PM. Tickets run $33 to $55, with the full Frequency Friday plus concert bundle at $55 ahead and $77 at the door. An intimate, full-body night of music under the red rocks — plan the drive home before the first set.

[today Show Low] Santa’s Winter Wonderland Craft Fair — Elks Lodge, 805 E. Whipple St, Show Low, today and Saturday, November 14, from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM each day. As many as 47 merchandise and craft vendors fill the lodge for the first great holiday shopping weekend on the mountain. Santa himself appears on Saturday, candy canes in hand for the children. Come start the holiday list early and support the makers of the White Mountains. A warm hall on a grey day — exactly right. | Live Music on the Mountain — Show Low, today in the evening. The Thirsty Band plays AZTEX Coffee and Taproom at 5:00 PM, and Ashley Westcott plays Charlie Clark’s Steakhouse at 6:00 PM. Two rooms, two sounds, one small mountain town that knows how to end a Friday. Pick the taproom for a lively set or the steakhouse for dinner with a song. Either way, the White Mountains will sing you into the weekend.

[today Prescott] Yavapai Hills 31st Annual Holiday Craft Show — 4975 Hornet Dr, Prescott, today and Saturday, November 14, from 9:00 AM. Thirty-one years running, this hometown craft show is handmade and local to its bones — gifts, decorations, and the first real taste of Arizona’s Christmas City season. Go in the daytime, take your time at the tables, and talk to the makers. Holiday shows like this one are where a town shows its hands. Bring the list; you will finish more of it than you expect. | Flag Retirement Ceremony — Embry-Riddle, 3700 Willow Creek Rd, Prescott, today from 5:00 to 6:30 PM. A solemn, fitting close to Veterans Week: worn flags retired with ceremony and honor, at the hour the light goes down. The city’s own notice lists the gathering, and all are welcome to stand respectfully. After a week of parades and wreaths, this quiet rite says the last word well. Arrive a little early and dress for the evening cool.

[week Sat, Nov. 14] 2nd Annual Pasta Night — Elks Lodge, 1206 N Beeline Hwy, Payson, Saturday at 4:00 PM. Pasta night returns to the Elks for its second year, and the Payson Lions hold the tickets — they will also sell them Saturday morning at Noley’s alongside their bake sale. Expect a hall full of neighbors and heaped plates of the good stuff. Lodge suppers in this Hold do not stay secret long, so get tickets before the weekend. Write the Lions at paysonlionsfoundation@gmail.com if you need a hand. | Verde Valley Pottery Festival — Free Weekend — D.A. Ranch Vineyards, Cornville, Saturday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Sunday from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM, admission free. The full festival weekend brings live pottery demonstrations, hands-on clay activities for children, local food, live music, and estate-grown wine along Oak Creek. What began in Camp Verde in 2022 has grown into a regional gathering of makers and collectors. A handmade mug to bring home is a quest worth taking. Valley Dwellers up for the weekend pass nearly by the gate. | 3rd Annual GET LOUD Community Celebration — 3250 White Bear Rd, Sedona, Saturday from 2:00 PM. Sedona’s community celebration returns for its third year — an afternoon of neighbors, music, and good noise in a good cause. Community celebrations are where a Hold shows its heart, and this one has earned its annual place on the calendar. Bring the family and a little volume. The red rocks will provide the echo, free of charge.

[week Sun, Nov. 15] Alice Cooper in Concert — Findlay Toyota Center, Prescott Valley, Sunday at 7:00 PM. The godfather of shock rock brings his show to Prescott Valley, a short drive from downtown Prescott. It is the loudest booking of the week by a considerable margin, and Rim Country rock fans will fill the arena. A bard of a very different school, to be sure — but every mead hall honors a legend. Get tickets ahead; this one will not wait at the door.

[week Mon, Nov. 16] Banner Payson Cancer Center Groundbreaking — 807 S Ponderosa St, Payson, Monday at 10:00 AM, on the south side of the main building. Shovels turn for the new Banner Payson Cancer Center — changing the landscape of cancer treatment in Payson, one shovel at a time, as the hosts put it. For Rim Country families, care closer to home means fewer long drives down the Beeline at the hardest times. Come stand with the town for a hopeful morning. This is the week’s biggest good news, and it is ours.

[week Tue, Nov. 17] The Dreamboats — 301 S McLane, Payson, Tuesday at 7:00 PM. The Dreamboats bring a revival of the golden age of rock and roll — Elvis, Chuck Berry, the Beatles, Buddy Holly — played with heartthrob shine that has audiences falling in love with the old tunes all over again. It is a school night, yes, but some music is worth the yawns tomorrow. Bring someone who remembers when these songs were new. The hall will be humming by the second chorus. | Festival of Trees — A Christmas City Gala — Sam Hill Warehouse, 232 N Granite St, Prescott, opening Tuesday at 5:30 PM, tickets $100 for the gala. The gala opens Festival of Trees week in Arizona’s Christmas City: decorated trees and wreaths, Santa, and vendors under one roof, with proceeds benefiting the Eric Marsh Foundation. The public festival follows Thursday through Saturday, November 19–21, from 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM at $10 for adults. Go early in the run for the full forest. Prescott wears this season better than any town in the Holds.

[week Wed, Nov. 18] Rim Country Camera Club Meeting and Rally Around the Flag Dedication — Payson Library Large Meeting Room, 328 N McLane Rd, Payson, Wednesday from 4:30 to 6:30 PM. The camera club gathers to share the month’s work — members sending photos for the 2027 calendar contest should note submissions were due Friday, November 13. The same morning at 10:00 AM, the Rally Around the Flag memorial is dedicated at its complex, flags raised in ceremony. Two gatherings, one theme: this town remembers, and it keeps the pictures to prove it.

[week Thu, Nov. 19] Festival of Trees Prescott — Sam Hill Warehouse, 232 N Granite St, Prescott, Thursday through Saturday, November 21, from 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM, adults $10 and kids $2. Decorated trees and wreaths to see, shop, and vote on, with live entertainment, hot cocoa, ornament-making for children, and visits with Santa. Net proceeds benefit the Eric Marsh Foundation, honoring the Granite Mountain Hotshots. It is the first great hall of the Christmas season — go in the daytime with the family. By the Nine, bring cocoa money.

[merchant name] Mamajoe’s Italian Grill

[merchant town] Strawberry

[merchant blurb] A cozy Italian grill right on AZ-87 in Strawberry, serving the classics that keep locals and road-trippers coming back — legendary spaghetti, homemade meatballs, chicken parmesan, lobster ravioli, and wood-fired pizzas, all conjured in a small pine-country kitchen as if by a slow-simmered sauce spell. The signature thing to try is the spaghetti with homemade meatballs, the dish travelers cross Arizona to taste. Dinner only, Thursday through Sunday — plan for it like a quest, because it is one.

[merchant review] Pack your patience, this isn’t Scottsdale and the food is fantastic.

[merchant review_src] Review quoted in We3Travel

[merchant why] The Hearth sends guests here because a tiny Strawberry kitchen whose spaghetti folks drive across the state for is the very definition of a Rim Country treasure — great praise is great!

[merchant visit] 5076 AZ-87, Strawberry, AZ 85544. Hours: Thu 4–7 PM, Fri–Sun 4–8 PM; closed Mon–Wed. Phone (928) 476-3910. Prices: moderate. Good to know: it is a small restaurant and service runs at mountain pace — call ahead and do not be in a hurry.

[merchant image caption] The legendary spaghetti — worth the whole winding road to Strawberry.

[tale title] The Pinecones That Kept Vanishing

[tale] Fredas dawned grey and cool over the Hearth, the clouds hanging low, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) declared a grey day wanted brightening. He painted a dozen pinecones gold, hid them about the clearing, and announced a treasure hunt with a prize of Gus’s lemonade.

Henny (the Hearth’s plump chicken) won without moving. She had settled, early and unbothered, directly on top of the finest golden pinecone, and no clue Jethro read aloud could shift her. Earl (an elk) carried the collecting basket on his antlers with enormous dignity, gathering cone after cone, while Mabel (a wood elf) kept the tally and sighed only twice.

At eleven cones found, Jethro searched high and low for the last, until Henny stood up for a drink of water — and there it gleamed beneath her, warm as a fresh-laid egg. The hunt declared her champion, the lemonade was shared all round, and Henny, professional to the end, sat back down on her trophy.

[tale image caption] Eleven cones hunted, one sat upon — Henny wins the grey-day hunt without moving.

text:
[headline] The Holds Honor Their Veterans Under a Bright Sun

[dateline] Wednesday, November 11, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, wayfarer, and a bright Middas to you — the sun is climbing over the Rim, the pines are lit gold, and this is Veterans Day in the Holds. Here in Payson the dentists open their doors free to veterans from 9:00 AM, Prescott steps off its great parade at 11:00 AM, and Sedona gathers at the Heritage Museum for its tribute at the same hour. The week rolls merrily on from there — a pottery festival in Cornville, pasta night at the Elks, Alice Cooper in Prescott Valley, and the Dreamboats in Payson — so raise a mug to those who served, by the Nine, and step out into the sunshine.

[hero_caption] The Holds turn out under a bright sun to honor their veterans — parades, tributes, and thanks in every town.

[weather] Sunny high 67 low 45 rain 0% sunrise 6:54 AM sunset 5:23 PM tomorrow Overcast, 65/44

[weather_caption] Gandy basks half-asleep in the sun while Maevy chases a butterfly clean across the deck.

[today Payson] Payson Dentists Salute Our Veterans — today starting 9:00 AM, at dental offices around Payson. Four local practices offer veterans a free basic cleaning, an extraction, or a filling — all you need is your VA ID. Space is limited, so call ahead: Payson Premier Dental at 928-472-8400 for fillings, Center Point Dental at 928-472-2500 for extractions, Anderson Dental Group at 928-474-4581, and Mountain Family Dentistry at 928-363-4149, whose offer runs all month. This is the Hold at its best — skill offered freely, with thanks, to those who served.

[today Sedona] Sedona Heritage Museum Veterans Day Tribute — Sedona Heritage Museum, 735 Jordan Rd, Sedona, today at 11:00 AM, free. The annual tribute fills the historic Apple Shed: a flag ceremony, patriotic music, veteran dignitaries, and a parade of American flags at the entrance assembled by the Daughters of the American Revolution. Shondra Jepperson emcees and Col. Judith Patton gives the keynote. A warm, unhurried hour of thanks among the red rocks. | Drum and Sound Experience — Cultural Park, Sedona, today at 4:00 PM. An afternoon of rhythm and sound under the red rocks, in Sedona’s open-air cultural park. Bring a blanket, settle on the grass, and let the drums carry the day’s thanks into the evening light. It is the merry end of a solemn day — music, community, and that famous Sedona sky. Guests who love a sound bath with scenery will feel right at home.

[today Show Low] Coffee and Chair Massage — 100 N White Mountain Rd, Suite 104, Show Low, today at 9:00 AM. A gentle Veterans Day morning on the mountain: coffee in hand and a chair massage to loosen the shoulders. It is a small, kind offering in the middle of a busy week of remembrance. Come as you are, stay for a cup, and leave walking taller. White Mountain mornings were made for exactly this pace.

[today Prescott] Prescott Veterans Day Parade — downtown Prescott, today. Opening ceremonies begin at 10:30 AM at Cortez and Union streets and the parade steps off at 11:00 AM from the Courthouse Plaza ground where yesterday’s wreath was laid. This year’s theme honors veteran first responders — “Protecting Our Country, Serving Our Communities.” Come early, for downtown fills fast and the plaza is the best seat in the Hold. A grand, flag-bright morning in Arizona’s Christmas City. | Veterans Day Military Ball — Touchmark Blvd, Prescott, today at 5:00 PM. After the parade, the day turns dressy: a military ball to close Veterans Day in style. Expect an evening of ceremony, music, and dancing in honor of those who served. It is the formal bookend to a morning of flags on Cortez Street. Polish the boots, wayfarer — Prescott knows how to finish a day of honor.

[week Thu, Nov. 12] Mingle with a Veteran — Northland Pioneer College White Mountain Campus, 1001 W. Deuce of Clubs, Show Low, Thursday 7:00–10:00 AM. The college invites students, staff, and the whole community to an informal morning of conversation with local veterans — hear their stories, share a coffee, and say thank you in person. Everyone is welcome and no program stands between you and the talking. The best kind of Veterans Week event: simple, early, and human.

[week Fri, Nov. 13] Verde Valley Pottery Festival — D.A. Ranch, Cornville, Friday through Sunday, November 13–15. Three days of clay in the Verde Valley: Friday evening is the ticketed opening, and Saturday and Sunday are free. Potters from across the region bring bowls, mugs, and sculpture to a working ranch setting, with wine tasting and live demonstrations. Hearth guests headed to Sedona pass nearly by the gate. A handmade mug to bring home is a quest worth taking. | Lil Fish with Govinda at Humankind — Humankind, 1730 W State Route 89A, Sedona, Friday 5:00 PM–1:00 AM. A long, layered night of electronic music in Sedona’s intimate conscious-event venue: Frequency Friday opens the evening, Govinda plays 9:15–10:45 PM, and Lil Fish closes from 10:45 PM. Travelers who like their music with red-rock air will find their hall. Tickets are on the event page — plan the drive home before the first set.

[week Sat, Nov. 14] 2nd Annual Pasta Night — Elks Lodge, 1206 N Beeline Hwy, Payson, Saturday at 4:00 PM. Pasta night returns to the Elks Lodge for its second year, and the Lions have the tickets. Expect a hall full of neighbors, heaped plates, and the particular merriment of a small-town lodge supper. Last year’s first helping made it an annual — that tells you how the pasta was. Get tickets before the weekend; lodge suppers in this Hold do not stay secret long. | 3rd Annual GET LOUD Community Celebration — 3250 White Bear Rd, Sedona, Saturday at 2:00 PM. Sedona’s community celebration returns for its third year — an afternoon gathering of neighbors, music, and good noise in a good cause. Community celebrations are where a Hold shows its heart, and this one has earned its annual place. Bring the family and a little volume. Valley Dwellers up for the weekend are honored guests, as always.

[week Sun, Nov. 15] Alice Cooper in Concert — Findlay Toyota Center, Prescott Valley, Sunday at 7:30 PM. The godfather of shock rock brings his show to Prescott Valley, about twenty minutes from downtown Prescott. It is the loudest booking of the week by a considerable margin, and the arena will be full of Rim Country rock fans. A bard of a very different school, to be sure — but every mead hall honors a legend. Get tickets ahead; this one will not wait at the door.

[week Mon, Nov. 16] Banner Payson Cancer Center Groundbreaking — 807 S Ponderosa St, Payson, Monday at 10:00 AM. Shovels turn for the new Banner Payson Cancer Center — changing the landscape of cancer treatment in Payson, one shovel at a time, as the hosts put it. For Rim Country families, cancer care closer to home means fewer long drives down the Beeline at the hardest times. Come stand with the town for a hopeful morning. This is the week’s biggest good news, and it is ours.

[week Tue, Nov. 17] The Dreamboats — 301 S McLane, Payson, Tuesday at 7:00 PM. The Dreamboats bring a revival of the golden age of rock and roll to Payson — classic tunes played with the kind of shine that has audiences falling in love with them all over again. It is a school night, yes, but some music is worth the yawns tomorrow. Bring someone who remembers when these songs were new. The hall will be humming by the second chorus. | Festival of Trees Prescott — Sam Hill Warehouse, 232 N Granite St, Prescott, opening Tuesday, November 17 and running to November 21. Five days of beautifully decorated Christmas trees and wreaths, holiday vendors, live entertainment, visits with Santa, and children’s crafts. It is the first great trumpet blast of the Christmas season in the Holds. Go early in the run for the full forest, before the crowds find it. Downtown Prescott wears the season well.

[merchant name] Tiny’s Family Restaurant

[merchant town] Payson

[merchant blurb] A big, friendly family diner on Highway 260 pouring out the classics from 6:00 AM — blueberry pancakes with whipped cream, an open-face steak sandwich, hand-breaded shrimp, and a meatball sandwich regulars swear by, with a separate lounge for a quieter meal. The signature thing to try is that meatball sandwich, conjured to legendary size as if by a generous portion spell. Come hungry; the plates do not believe in half measures.

[merchant review] Best meatball sandwich in the USA!! Very friendly staff! 100 stars!

[merchant review_src] Restaurantji review

[merchant why] The Hearth sends guests here because a hometown diner with a meatball sandwich folks rate at a hundred stars is exactly where a Rim Country morning should start — great praise is great!

[merchant visit] 600 E AZ-260, Payson, AZ 85541. Hours: Mon and Sun 6 AM–3 PM, Tue–Sat 6 AM–8 PM. Phone (928) 474-5429. Prices: moderate, with generous portions. Good to know: breakfast is served from opening, and the lounge gives grown-ups a separate room when the dining room fills.

[merchant image caption] The famous meatball sandwich — a hundred stars’ worth, served in Payson.

[tale title] The Thank-You Parade That Went in a Circle

[tale] Middas dawned sunny and mild over the Hearth, sixty-seven degrees by afternoon, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) declared the forest owed its old soldiers a thank-you parade. Henny (the Hearth’s plump chicken) took the front, as is her right. Earl (an elk) marched behind with enormous dignity, and Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) flew above, scattering ice crystals that sparkled in the sun.

The trouble was the route. Flurry flies in zigzags, on account of the kink in his tail, and Jethro — banner held high — followed him faithfully. Left, right, left again. By the third lap of the clearing, Earl stopped, looked about, and announced that he had now been thanked in every direction the compass owns.

Mabel (a wood elf) sighed, stepped into the circle, and pointed the whole parade at the porch, where Gus (an orc baker) waited with lemonade. The parade arrived in perfect order, having marched a mile and traveled forty feet, and everyone agreed it was the finest thank-you the Hold has ever given.

[tale image caption] A mile marched, forty feet traveled — the thank-you parade arrives in perfect order.

headline: A Week of Thanks: Wreaths, Parades, and a Groundbreaking
greeting: PAYSON — Hail, traveler, and a fair Tirdas to you — the sun is up over the Rim, the pines stand gold in the morning light, and the whole country is turning its mind to thanks. Volunteers are already lacing their boots for a trail-building morning in Pine, Prescott lays its wreath at the All-Service Members Memorial at 10:00 AM to open the Veterans Day observances, and tomorrow the Holds honor their veterans in earnest — free dental care here in Payson, a parade in Prescott, and a tribute in Sedona. The week then rolls merrily on to a pottery festival in Cornville, pasta night at the Elks, and, come Monday, the groundbreaking for the new Banner Payson Cancer Center — good news worth raising a mug to, by the Nine.

[headline] A Week of Thanks: Wreaths, Parades, and a Groundbreaking

[dateline] Tuesday, November 10, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, traveler, and a fair Tirdas to you — the sun is up over the Rim, the pines stand gold in the morning light, and the whole country is turning its mind to thanks. Volunteers are already lacing their boots for a trail-building morning in Pine, Prescott lays its wreath at the All-Service Members Memorial at 10:00 AM to open the Veterans Day observances, and tomorrow the Holds honor their veterans in earnest — free dental care here in Payson, a parade in Prescott, and a tribute in Sedona. The week then rolls merrily on to a pottery festival in Cornville, pasta night at the Elks, and, come Monday, the groundbreaking for the new Banner Payson Cancer Center — good news worth raising a mug to, by the Nine.

[hero_caption] Trail crews take to the pines at first light while Prescott lays its wreath — a week of thanks begins in the Holds.

[weather] Mostly sunny high 66 low 45 rain 0% sunrise 6:53 AM sunset 5:24 PM tomorrow Sunny, 67/45

[weather_caption] Gandy basks half-asleep in the sun while Maevy chases a butterfly clean across the deck.

[today Payson] PPRC Committee Meeting — today 6:30–7:30 PM. The committee behind Payson’s rodeo doings opens its doors to the public this evening, and newcomers are genuinely welcome. The group runs on committee members, volunteers, and rodeo fans, and the meeting is the plainest way to see how the Hold’s biggest weekends get built. Come curious, lend a hand later, or just listen in. If you have ever wondered who hangs the banners, tonight is your night.

[today Pine-Strawberry] Trail Day Volunteer Build — Highway 87, Pine, today at 7:00 AM. “Don’t just use the trail — help build it” is the call from Pine-Strawberry Fuel Reduction, inviting hikers, bikers, runners, and neighbors to keep building the trails below the Mogollon Rim. Expect real outdoor work side by side with the community, not a guided hike. Bring work clothes, water, and a willing back. This is Rim Country looking after its own trails, one bright morning at a time.

[today Camp Verde] Defensive Long Gun Fundamentals — The Compass Training Center AZ, Camp Verde, today at 9:00 AM. A fundamentals class for folks who want their long-gun skills taught properly, step by step, by instructors rather than by guesswork. Training days like this draw students from all over the Verde Valley. If marksmanship is your craft, this is a serious, structured way to practice it. Check the event page for what to bring and how to reserve a spot.

[today Sedona] Creative Aging Class for 55+: The Gift of Fruits & Florals with Patricia Saxton — 15 Art Barn Rd, Sedona, today 10:00 AM–12:00 PM, and Tuesdays through December 8. A beginner-friendly art class made for folks 55 and better: paint, draw, or make collages inspired by fruits and flowers, on everything from paper and canvas to boxes and trays. Materials are included, image prompts are provided, and the guidance is generous. Small works worth keeping — or giving as gifts. A gentle, colorful way to spend a red-rock morning. | Restorative & Yin Yoga — Intimate Small-Group Session — Sundara Sacred Arts, 1785 W. State Route 89A, Sedona, today at 6:00 PM. A small-group evening practice in the slow, deep-stretch yin style, made for unwinding rather than working up a sweat. Sedona does quiet evenings beautifully, and this is one of its calmest hours. Mats down, lights low, red rocks fading outside. A fine way for guests to close a day of hiking.

[today Prescott] Wreath Laying Ceremony — All-Service Members Memorial, west side of the Yavapai County Courthouse Plaza, Prescott, today at 10:00 AM. Prescott opens its Veterans Day observances with the ceremonial laying of the wreath, and cadets from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University’s Air Force and Army ROTC stand a 24-hour Guard of the Memorial. It is a solemn, beautiful start to the two days of honor. Arrive a little early and stand with the town. Tomorrow’s parade begins on this same ground. | Line Dance Lessons — 214 S. Montezuma St, Prescott, today at 6:00 PM. When the wreath is laid and the day turns merry, Whiskey Row answers with dancing: an evening of line dance lessons a short stroll from the Courthouse Plaza. Beginners are the whole point of a lesson night, so no partner and no experience are required. Boots help, enthusiasm helps more. A joyful Prescott evening after a day of remembrance. | Raskin’s Jewelers Buying Event — Raskin’s Jewelers, 110 W. Gurley St, Prescott, starting today at 10:00 AM and running November 10–12. The downtown jeweler’s three-day buying event takes over the Gurley Street shop, a block from the Courthouse Plaza. If a drawer at home holds pieces you have meant to have looked at, this is the week the experts are in. Combine it with the wreath ceremony and make a full Prescott day of it. The plaza is lovely in this weather.

[week Wed, Nov. 11] Payson Dentists Salute Our Veterans — Payson, Wednesday starting 9:00 AM. Four local dental offices offer veterans a free basic cleaning, an extraction, or a filling — just bring your VA ID. Space is limited, so call ahead: Payson Premier Dental (928-472-8400, fillings), Center Point Dental (928-472-2500, extractions), Anderson Dental Group (928-474-4581), and Mountain Family Dentistry (928-363-4149, whose offer runs all month). This is the Hold at its best — skill offered freely to those who served. | Prescott Veterans Day Parade — Downtown Prescott, Wednesday. Opening ceremonies begin at 10:30 AM at Cortez and Union streets, the parade steps off at 11:00 AM, and it pauses at 11:11 AM to mark the Armistice that ended World War I. This year’s theme is “Remember the Past. Serve the Present. Inspire the Future.” The route runs south on Cortez to Goodwin, west to Montezuma, and on to Sheldon. Come early — downtown streets close at 8:00 AM and the plaza fills fast. | Sedona Heritage Museum Veterans Day Tribute — Sedona Heritage Museum, 735 Jordan Rd, Sedona, Wednesday at 11:00 AM, free. The annual tribute fills the historic Apple Shed: a flag ceremony, patriotic music, veteran dignitaries, and a parade of American flags at the entrance assembled by the Daughters of the American Revolution. Shondra Jepperson emcees, and Col. Judith Patton gives the keynote. A warm, unhurried hour of thanks among the red rocks.

[week Thu, Nov. 12] Mingle with a Veteran — Northland Pioneer College White Mountain Campus, Learning Center Lobby, 1001 W. Deuce of Clubs, Show Low, Thursday 7:00–10:00 AM. The college invites students, staff, and the whole community to an informal morning of conversation with local veterans — hear their stories, share a coffee, and say thank you in person. Everyone is welcome and no program stands between you and the talking. The best kind of Veterans Week event: simple, early, and human.

[week Fri, Nov. 13] Verde Valley Pottery Festival — D.A. Ranch, Cornville, Friday through Sunday, November 13–15. Three days of clay in the Verde Valley: Friday evening is the ticketed opening, and Saturday and Sunday are free. Potters from across the region bring bowls, mugs, and sculpture to a working ranch setting — the kind of festival where you meet the maker at the wheel. Hearth guests headed to Sedona pass nearly by the gate. A sweet roll for the road and a handmade mug to bring home: a fine Friday indeed. | Jesus & Jammies — 1100 W Lake Dr, Payson, Friday at 6:00 PM. The WELL women’s gathering brings back the classic girls’ sleepover — favorite pajamas, childhood snacks, friendship bracelets, silly games, and talk until late — with faith and friendship at its heart. Tickets are $5 as a donation, and if that is a hardship you are still welcome. You do not have to know anyone to come. A cozy, laughing Friday night on the Payson side of the Rim.

[week Sat, Nov. 14] 2nd Annual Pasta Night — Elks Lodge, 1206 N Beeline Hwy, Payson, Saturday at 4:00 PM. Pasta night returns to the Elks Lodge for its second year, and tickets are already out. Expect a hall full of neighbors, heaped plates, and the particular merriment of a small-town lodge supper. Last year’s first helping made it an annual — that tells you how the pasta was. Get tickets before the weekend; lodge suppers in this Hold do not stay secret long.

[week Mon, Nov. 16] Banner Payson Cancer Center Groundbreaking — 807 S Ponderosa St, Payson, Monday at 10:00 AM. Shovels turn on the south side of the main building for the new Banner Payson Cancer Center — “changing the landscape of cancer treatment in Payson, one shovel at a time,” as the hosts put it. For Rim Country families, cancer care closer to home means fewer long drives down the Beeline at the hardest times. Come stand with the town for a hopeful morning. This is the week’s biggest good news, and it is ours.

[merchant name] Arizona Mountain Coffee Co.

[merchant town] Show Low

[merchant blurb] A veteran-owned coffee house on White Mountain Road — fitting for Veterans Week — pouring organic-style mountain coffee, hazelnut and salted-caramel lattes, breakfast burritos, sandwiches, and pastries, with a dog-friendly patio and a cozy room to linger in. The signature thing to try is the cinnamon roll, a swirled sweet roll of the very kind sung about in every mead hall from here to Whiterun, kept warm as if by a kindly warming spell. Order the roll and a Han Solo Hazelnut Latte and settle in.

[merchant review] Travel all over the world and still the best cinnamon rolls in the World are right here as Arizona Mountain Coffee.

[merchant review_src] Google review

[merchant why] The Hearth sends guests here because a veteran-owned coffee house with the best cinnamon rolls on the mountain is exactly the stop a Rim road trip deserves — great praise is great!

[merchant visit] 151 N White Mountain Rd, Show Low, AZ. Hours: Mon–Sat 7 AM–4 PM, Sun 7 AM–2 PM. Phone (928) 892-2326. Prices: inexpensive. Good to know: it is veteran-owned, the patio welcomes dogs, and the cinnamon rolls are famous enough to plan a morning around.

[merchant image caption] The famous cinnamon roll — a sweet roll worthy of song, served warm in Show Low.

[tale title] The Antler Sled

[tale] Tirdas dawned bright and mostly sunny over the Hearth, a full sixty-six degrees by afternoon, and Henny (the Hearth’s plump chicken) announced that sledding weather had arrived. It had not. There was no snow anywhere in the Hold.

Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) fixed that the only way he knows how. He frosted a short lane of flat stones across the clearing, smooth and sparkling, while Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) tied a little wooden sled between Earl’s (an elk’s) antlers like a parade float. Earl stood very still, wearing his best offended dignity.

Henny climbed aboard, Jethro pushed, and away they went — six glorious feet — before the sun, doing its honest work, melted the last of the lane and the sled stopped dead in the warm grass. Henny rode the whole six feet like a queen in procession and has dined out on it since. Mabel (a wood elf) sighed, fetched a lemonade, and declared it the finest sled run in Hold history, distance notwithstanding.

[tale image caption] Six glorious feet — Henny rides the Antler Sled like a queen in procession.

headline: A New Pantry, Pine Music, and Veterans Week Across the Holds

text:
[headline] A New Pantry, Pine Music, and Veterans Week Across the Holds

[dateline] Monday, November 9, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, wayfarer, and a bright Morndas to you — morning light is spilling over the Rim, the pines stand still in clear air, and a kind week is opening in every Hold. Here at home a brand-new Neighbor’s Pantry food distribution rolls out at the Payson Warming Center this morning, Pine lifts its voice at open mic tonight, and by Wednesday the Holds turn out in full thanks for Veterans Day in Prescott, Sedona, and Camp Verde. Add a free documentary screening in Show Low, sourdough in Prescott, and warm hand pies up the road in Strawberry, and there is good cheer enough for the whole road, by the Nine.

[hero_caption] Volunteers load the pantry cart, bards tune up in Pine, and the Holds look toward Veterans Day.

[weather] Sunny high 65 low 44 rain 0% sunrise 6:52 AM sunset 5:25 PM tomorrow Overcast, 67/45

[weather_caption] Gandy basks half-asleep in the sun while Maevy chases a butterfly clean across the deck.

[today Payson] Payson Food Distribution — Neighbor’s Pantry Launch — Payson Warming Center, 601 AZ-260, today 9:00–11:00 AM. A brand-new monthly mobile food distribution from United Food Bank and Mercy Care kicks off this morning, drive-thru style, so empty the trunk before you come and no walk-ups, please. Volunteers will load fresh produce, pantry staples, and bakery goods at no cost. It is open to the public and aimed at neighbors in need — a fine, practical piece of good news to start the week. Arrive early in the window while the crates are full.

[today Pine-Strawberry] Open Mic Night: Music with a Purpose — THAT Brewery & Pub, 3270 N Highway 87, Pine, today at 4:00 PM. Open mic returns to the pub in the pines, hosted this season by rotating members of the Pine-Strawberry Fuel Reduction crew, where community, music, and giving back come together. Local singers, pickers, and brave first-timers are welcome to take a turn while the crowd listens kindly. It is a relaxed Monday-evening stop for Hearth guests. Good pours, live local voices, and a good cause behind it all.

[today Sedona] Wild Grace Retreat — In Session — Sky Ranch Lodge, Sedona, running November 8–13 and in session today. This is a registered, intimate-group retreat, not a drop-in event, billed as a joyful gathering of movement, rest, renewal, ceremony, and nourishing meals attuned to Sedona’s red-rock and vortex country. Guests already booked will find the red rocks at their calmest on a Monday. Travelers not booked should take it as a sign of the season: Sedona’s retreat weeks are in full swing. Watch for the hosts’ special 11/11 gathering later this week.

[today Show Low] NPC Special Screening: People of the West, Episodes 3 & 4 — Northland Pioneer College White Mountain Campus, 1001 W. Deuce of Clubs, Show Low, today 5:00–7:00 PM, free. The college’s Community Connections Subcommittee invites everyone to this special screening in its five-evening series. Episodes 3 and 4 of the ten-part documentary explore California’s history through the voices and perspectives of Indigenous peoples. Everyone is welcome and there is no cost. A thoughtful, quiet Monday-night option for guests headed to the White Mountains.

[today Prescott] Sourdough Bread Demonstration — University of Arizona Yavapai County Cooperative Extension, Prescott, today at 10:00 AM, a two-hour session. Using pre-made dough, the guide walks through every stage: starter basics, mixing and fermenting, shaping, and baking tips with troubleshooting. It is made for home bakers who have a starter on the counter and questions to go with it. Practical, friendly food learning from the county Extension service. Bring your best starter questions and leave with a plan for the next loaf. | Stefani Savage — Live Music — Peacock Room, Hassayampa Inn, 122 E Gurley St, Prescott, today 5:00–8:00 PM. Monday nights rarely sound this nice: a local singer fills the historic inn’s Peacock Room while dinner and drinks are served around her. The setting is warm, the hour is kind, and downtown is an easy stroll before or after. Prescott lists dozens of live-music nights this week, and this is Monday’s gentle pick. A fine early-evening plan for Valley Dwellers up for the week. | Xtreme Bar Bingo — Jersey Lilly Saloon, 116 S Montezuma St, Prescott, today at 6:00 PM. Free-to-play bingo takes over the Whiskey Row saloon for Monday night, with a cash jackpot advertised up to $15,000, weekly giveaways, and deluxe prizes. All-day happy hour is part of the pitch, and the room is loud, social, and glad to see new faces. It is the merry opposite of the quiet Peacock Room set across town. Pick your pace — Prescott offers both tonight.

[week Tue, Nov. 10] Trail Day Volunteer Build — Highway 87, Pine, Tuesday at 7:00 AM. “Don’t just use the trail — help build it” is the call from Pine-Strawberry Fuel Reduction, inviting hikers, bikers, runners, and neighbors to continue work on the trails below the Mogollon Rim. Expect real outdoor work side by side with the community, not a guided hike. Bring work clothes, water, and a willing back. This is Rim Country looking after its own trails, one morning at a time.

[week Wed, Nov. 11] Prescott Veterans Day Parade — Downtown Prescott, Wednesday, November 11. Opening ceremonies begin at 10:30 AM at Cortez and Union streets, and the parade steps off at 11:00 AM around Courthouse Square. This year’s theme is “Protecting Our Country – Serving Our Communities – Honoring Our Veteran First Responders.” It is the region’s biggest Veterans Day observance this week. Arrive early — downtown draws a large, proud crowd. | Sedona Veterans Day Tribute — Sedona Heritage Museum, 735 Jordan Road, Uptown Sedona, Wednesday 11:00 AM–1:00 PM, free. Sedona’s official observance, hosted with the City of Sedona, gathers neighbors for a flag ceremony, dignitaries, a tribute to veterans, and music in Jordan Historical Park. Free food and entertainment follow the ceremony. Every veteran and active-duty service member is invited to be honored. Open to anyone who wishes to stand and give thanks. | Veterans Day Appreciation Program — Cliff Castle Casino, Camp Verde, Wednesday 11:00 AM–12:00 noon. The Yavapai-Apache Nation and Cliff Castle Casino honor all veterans with presentation of colors, a flag folding ceremony, remarks, and an honor song. Gifts for veterans are part of the program, and the casino offers a free lunch for veterans. It is a warm, one-hour midday tribute. A fitting stop on the road between the Holds. | Payson Dentists Salute Our Veterans — 409 W Main Street, Payson, Wednesday at 9:00 AM. Local dentists offer a free basic cleaning, extraction, or filling for veterans with VA ID, with space limited, so reserve ahead. It is a practical thank-you, given chair by chair, right here at home. Veterans, call early to claim a spot. Neighbors, spread the word to a veteran who could use it.

[week Thu, Nov. 12] Mingle with a Veteran — Northland Pioneer College White Mountain Campus, Learning Center Lobby, 1001 W. Deuce of Clubs, Show Low, Thursday morning. Join the college for conversation, community, and appreciation for the veterans who have served. Students, staff, and community members are all invited — this is a meet-and-talk gathering, not a formal ceremony. It is a good day-after way to sit down and hear a veteran’s story. Come with time to listen.

[week Fri, Nov. 13] Verde Valley Pottery Festival — First Pick Friday — D.A. Ranch Vineyards, 1900 Dancing Apache Road, Cornville, Friday 4:00–6:00 PM, $25 early access. The festival’s fifth year opens with first choice of handmade ceramic work by Arizona potters, plus D.A. Ranch wine, local food trucks, craft beer, and live music along Oak Creek. The free festival weekend follows on Saturday and Sunday. The finest pots go to those who come Friday. Book the evening if a handmade bowl is calling your name.

[week Sat, Nov. 14] Verde Valley Pottery Festival — Free Festival Day — D.A. Ranch Vineyards, Cornville, Saturday 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, free. Arizona potters show and sell their work with live demonstrations, hands-on activities, local food, estate wine, and live music across the ranch grounds. What began as a grassroots gathering in Camp Verde has grown into a regional favorite for makers and collectors. Bring a bag and a careful hand. Nobody leaves empty-handed. | Get Loud Community Celebration — Community Library Sedona, 3250 White Bear Drive, Sedona, Saturday 2:00–5:00 PM, free. Sedona’s big community party returns with an obstacle slide, inflatable maze, bungee run, and baseball speed-pitch, plus face painting and balloon animals. Free tacos, popcorn, and cotton candy are served until they run out. Park free at Red Rock High School and ride the free trolley. Last year more than 1,500 neighbors came — come be counted.

[week Sun, Nov. 15] Sedona Symphony: Simple Gifts — Sedona Performing Arts Center, 995 Upper Red Rock Loop Road, Sedona, Sunday — pre-concert talk 2:00 PM, concert 3:00–5:00 PM. The Sedona Symphony’s American music celebration closes with Aaron Copland’s Appalachian Spring, built on the Shaker melody that gives the afternoon its name. Violinist Rachel Lee Priday is the featured soloist in a new concerto written for her. Tickets are sold through the Sedona Symphony. A gratitude-filled soundtrack under Sedona’s big sky.

[merchant name] PIEbar AZ

[merchant town] Strawberry

[merchant blurb] In a tiny red-and-yellow carryout shop in the pines — just 329 square feet, with picnic tables under the trees and no dining room at all — PIEbar AZ bakes hand pies and empanadas sealed in golden pastry, each one three days in the making. The menu runs long and rotates weekly, from Green Chile Pork and Philly Cheese Steak to Strawberries & Cream and Molten Chocolate, with coffee, bubble tea, and sodas beside them. Try The Mountain Man first — sausage, potato, gravy, and cheese, ideally with the habanero chimichurri — a pocket pie any Dragonborn would carry in his satchel, kept warm as if by a kindly spell.

[merchant review] Great pies! We loved the variety and the opportunity to eat them under the trees on site. They were served still warm - we should have gotten more to take home with us!

[merchant review_src] TripAdvisor review

[merchant why] The Hearth sends guests here because warm hand pies under the ponderosas are perfect trail food on the road to Tonto Natural Bridge — and great praise is great!

[merchant visit] 5096 AZ-87, Strawberry, AZ 85544. Hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun 9 AM–5 PM; closed Wednesdays. Phone (602) 882-1442. Prices: moderate, about $10–$20 per person. Good to know: carryout and outdoor tables only, the menu varies weekly, and popular flavors sell out — go earlier in the day.

[merchant image caption] Warm hand pies under the pines — the sweet-roll rival of the Rim.

[tale title] The Sun Tea That Would Not Warm

[tale] Morndas dawned bright and clear over the Hearth, and Gus (an orc baker) set a row of glass jars on the deck rail to make sun tea, the way any sensible baker does on a sunny day. “Sun does the work,” he said proudly. “We just wait.”

Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) could not bear it. Warm jars looked wrong to him, so every time Gus turned away, Flurry breathed one careful puff of ice mist over the rail, frosting the jars rim to rim. Henny (the Hearth’s plump chicken) sat guard beside them, unbothered, warming herself in the very sunshine the tea was trying to catch.

Mabel (a wood elf) arrived, looked at the frosted jars, and sighed her best sigh. “Flurry, love, sun tea cannot brew in a snowbank.” Flurry zigzagged sadly — then brightened, and shaded the picnic table with one wing so the whole crew could drink yesterday’s tea, properly cold, while today’s jars finally warmed in peace. By noon the tea was gold, the ice was gone, and Gus declared it the first sun tea in Hold history brewed by argument.

[tale image caption] Sun tea, brewed by argument — gold by noon.

headline: Riders, Red Rocks, and a College Win Fill a Bright Sundas

Here at home the dual-sport riders ride their second day of Howlin’ at the Moon out of the Payson Elks Lodge, while Sedona closes its Mountain Bike Festival under the red rocks and Show Low settles in for a Sunday song at AZTEX. And there is good news worth a cheer in the mead hall: voters gave Gila Community College an overwhelming vote of confidence, approving Proposition 425 by about 67 percent to lift the college’s outmoded spending limit — a win for every student in Rim Country, by the Nine.
text:
[headline] Riders, Red Rocks, and a College Win Fill a Bright Sundas

[dateline] Sunday, November 8, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, traveler, and a fair Sundas to you — the pines stand gold in the morning light, the sky is clear from the Rim to the valley road, and the Holds are wide awake. Here at home the dual-sport riders ride their second day of Howlin’ at the Moon out of the Payson Elks Lodge, while Sedona closes its Mountain Bike Festival under the red rocks and Show Low settles in for a Sunday song at AZTEX. And there is good news worth a cheer in the mead hall: voters gave Gila Community College an overwhelming vote of confidence, approving Proposition 425 by about 67 percent to lift the college’s outmoded spending limit — a win for every student in Rim Country, by the Nine.

[hero_caption] Riders take the forest roads, gem stalls glitter, and red-rock trails call — a bright Sundas in every Hold.

[weather] Sunny high 66 low 45 rain 0% sunrise 6:51 AM sunset 5:25 PM tomorrow Sunny, 65/45

[weather_caption] Gandy basks half-asleep in the sun while Maevy chases a butterfly clean across the deck.

[today Payson] 2026 Howlin’ at the Moon — Day Two — Payson Elks Lodge, 1206 N Beeline Hwy. The AMA/Beta National Dual Sport riders head out again today on fresh 50–60 mile loops through the forest around Payson, different roads from Saturday’s long run. Check-in runs 6:30–8:30 AM over the same hearty breakfast, and GPS track logs and a thank-you gift round out the day. Registration closed in October, so today belongs to the registered riders — and to everyone who loves the sound of the Hold’s trails humming till evening.

[today Sedona] 2026 Sedona Mountain Bike Festival — Final Day — Posse Grounds Park, 525 Posse Grounds Rd, running Friday through today, Sunday, November 8. The year’s great gathering of mountain bikers closes today with the expo, bike demos, shuttled rides on Sedona’s famous red singletrack, gear vendors, a beer garden, food trucks, skills clinics, and live bands. Passes are sold at the festival registration booth, so a traveler can still join the fun. Go early — the red rocks and the singletrack are at their best in the morning light. | Sedona Community Farmers Market — 2201 W State Route 89A, Sedona, today from 8:00 AM. The Sunday market fills its lot with local growers, bakers, and makers — fresh produce, bread, and small treasures to carry home to the Hearth. It is the gentle start to a Sedona day: shop the stalls first, then walk the town while the air is still cool. Valley Dwellers up for the weekend will find it an easy, friendly stop.

[today Show Low] The Thirsty Band at AZTEX Coffee and Taproom — Show Low, today at 1 PM. An easygoing Sunday set at the taproom: coffee, a cold pour, and live music to close the weekend at a civilized hour. The room is friendly, the hour is kind to travelers, and the drive over from Payson runs through some of the prettiest pine country in the Holds. A good excuse for the scenic run while the sun is still high.

[today Prescott] CoffeeHouse Concert: John Coinman — Prescott Public Library, 215 E Goodwin St, today 2:00–3:30 PM. The award-winning Tucson singer-songwriter brings his Southwest-inspired songs to the library’s quiet hall, drawing on his solo work, film and television soundtracks, and his time with Kevin Costner & Modern West. Library hush, live songs, and the rare chance to clap indoors among the books. Arrive a little early for a good seat. | A Tribute to the Ole’ Cherokee Cowboy — Elks Theatre, 117 E Gurley St, Prescott, today at 3 PM. Billy Mata & The Texas Tradition honor the legendary Ray Price with classic hits, western swing, and stories from his long career, with Prescott fiddler Jordan Brambila joining the band. The historic Elks stage was made for music like this — warm, well-played, and full of heart. A fine way to spend a Sunday afternoon on the square. | 251st Marine Corps Birthday Ball — Prescott Resort, today, Sunday, November 8. Copper State Detachment 906 of the Marine Corps League hosts the ball with the traditional birthday ceremony and cake cutting, dinner, dancing, a guest speaker, and music. It honors the Marine Corps’ proud tradition and service, in the company of Marines, families, and friends. Dress fine, come proud, and raise a glass to 251 years.

[week Mon, Nov. 9] Daryl Felsberg at Hon-Dah Resort Hotel — near Show Low, Monday at 7 PM. A Monday-night stand-up set at the resort hotel — an uncommon treat in the White Mountains and a merry way to start the week. Travelers staying over after the weekend will find dinner and a show under one roof. Check the hotel for ticket word before you set out.

[week Tue, Nov. 10] PAWS for Reading — Prescott Public Library, 215 E Goodwin St, Prescott, Tuesday at 3:30 PM. A calm therapy dog, a picture book, and a young reader who forgets to be nervous — that is the whole kind magic of this library hour for youth and school-age kids. Children read aloud to a patient, four-legged listener, and confidence grows page by page. Free, gentle, and well loved by local families.

[week Wed, Nov. 11] Prescott Veterans Day Parade — Downtown Prescott, Wednesday, November 11. Opening activities begin at 10:30 AM at Cortez and Union streets, the parade steps off at 11:00 AM, and it pauses at 11:11 AM to mark the Armistice that ended the First World War. This year’s theme is “Remember the Past, Serve the Present, Inspire the Future.” Come stand with the Hold, wave a flag, and give thanks — downtown streets close from 8 AM, so arrive early. | Veterans Day Tribute — Sedona Heritage Museum, Uptown Sedona, Wednesday, November 11. The town’s official Veterans Day observance, hosted with the City of Sedona, gathers neighbors at the museum to honor those who served. It is a quiet, fitting stop in the middle of the week, under the red rocks. Come, stand with the Hold, and give thanks.

[week Fri, Nov. 13] Verde Valley Pottery Festival — First Pick Friday — D.A. Ranch Vineyards, 1900 Dancing Apache Rd, Cornville, Friday 4–6 PM, $25 early access. The festival’s fifth year opens with a ticketed first look: first choice of handmade ceramic work by Arizona potters, plus D.A. Ranch wine, local food trucks, craft beer, and live music along Oak Creek. The free festival weekend follows Saturday and Sunday — but the finest pots go to those who come Friday. | Bully-Proof Your Child: Free Kids Workshop — 501 W Main St, Payson, Friday, November 13. A free 45-minute workshop that gives children plain, practical tools to stand tall and stay safe, taught in a friendly room where questions are welcome. Parents looking for one useful thing to do with the young ones this week need look no further. Check the listing for the start time before you go.

[week Sat, Nov. 14] Verde Valley Pottery Festival — Free Festival Day — D.A. Ranch Vineyards, 1900 Dancing Apache Rd, Cornville, Saturday 10 AM–5 PM, free admission. Fifteen Arizona potters show and sell their work, with live demonstrations, hands-on activities, local food, estate wine, and live music across the ranch grounds. The festival is now a nonprofit in its fifth year, and Saturday is its biggest day. Bring a bag — nobody leaves empty-handed. | Honoring Prescott’s Heroes — Sharlot Hall Museum, Prescott, Saturday, November 14. The museum’s Living History Adventure explores the roles Fort Whipple and Fort Verde played in Arizona’s territorial history, while honoring the soldiers who served across the years and the heroes of today. Costumed interpreters, real stories, and a walk through Prescott’s own past. A worthy Saturday outing for the whole household.

[merchant name] Creekside Tavern

[merchant town] Payson

[merchant blurb] Up Christopher Creek way, where the pines lean over the water, stands a rustic mountain tavern terraced along the banks of the creek itself — steaks, ribs, prime rib, fish and chips, burgers, pizza, and the famous Firehouse Buffalo Chicken Sandwich, with a full bar beside it. A small helpful enchantment seems to hang over the kitchen: order the prime rib and it arrives as if a banquet spell had been cast just for your table. Start with the Creekside Sampler Platter, save room for the 20-oz King Ribeye if you are feeling heroic, and take dessert on the patio while the creek talks below.

[merchant review] The prime rib was superb!!

[merchant review_src] Google review

[merchant why] The Hearth sends guests here because a meal beside a real creek, under real pines, is Rim Country on a plate — and this tavern earns its praise. Great praise is great!

[merchant visit] 1520 East Christopher Creek Loop, Payson, AZ 85541. Hours: Mon 11 AM–7 PM, Tue–Wed 4–7 PM, Thu 11 AM–7 PM, Fri 11 AM–9 PM, Sat 10 AM–9 PM, Sun 10 AM–5 PM. Phone (928) 478-4557. Prices: moderate. Good to know: Tuesday and Wednesday open at 4 PM only, so plan a dinner visit on those days.

[merchant image caption] The tavern by the creek, where the prime rib arrives like a banquet spell.

[tale title] The Sunrise Roll Call

[tale] Sundas dawned clear and gold over the Hearth, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) decided the sunrise deserved a proper welcome. He stood on the deck with a parchment roster and called the roll like a town crier: “Earl! Henny! Flurry! Mabel! Present yourselves for the sun!”

Earl (an elk) presented himself beautifully — and fell asleep standing up, antlers swaying like a metronome. Henny (the Hearth’s plump chicken) pecked the roster twice, which Jethro recorded as “present, and in charge.” Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) tried to salute with a wing, zigzagged, and breathed one small swirl of ice crystals that caught the first light and threw a tiny rainbow clean across the deck.

Mabel (a wood elf) arrived last, with mugs for everyone, and sighed the sigh of the only responsible adult in the forest. “The sun,” she said, “has risen every day without a roll call.” Jethro nodded gravely and wrote it down anyway: Sun — present. It was, travelers, the best-attended sunrise in Hold history.

[tale image caption] Sun — present. The best-attended sunrise in Hold history.

headline: Gems, Riders, and Red Rocks Fill a Bright Loredas
greeting: PAYSON — Hail, wayfarer, and good Loredas to you — the sun is up over the Rim, the air is cool and bright, and every road out of the Hearth leads somewhere merry today. Down in Miami, the Gila County Gem and Mineral Society spreads its Fall Show and Sale across the Bullion Plaza yard from 9 AM to 2 PM, free for all who love a sparkling stone. Here at home, two hundred dual-sport riders roar out of the Payson Elks Lodge for Howlin’ at the Moon, and tonight the Rim Country Marine Corps Ball fills the Mazatzal with ceremony and dancing. West in Sedona, the Mountain Bike Festival takes over Posse Grounds Park, Prescott opens its zoo gates for a one-dollar day, and the Verde Valley gathers for its first Wellness Festival — by the Nine, a finer Saturday is hard to picture.
text:
[headline] Gems, Riders, and Red Rocks Fill a Bright Loredas

[dateline] Saturday, November 7, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, wayfarer, and good Loredas to you — the sun is up over the Rim, the air is cool and bright, and every road out of the Hearth leads somewhere merry today. Down in Miami, the Gila County Gem and Mineral Society spreads its Fall Show and Sale across the Bullion Plaza yard from 9 AM to 2 PM, free for all who love a sparkling stone. Here at home, two hundred dual-sport riders roar out of the Payson Elks Lodge for Howlin’ at the Moon, and tonight the Rim Country Marine Corps Ball fills the Mazatzal with ceremony and dancing. [hero_caption] Gem stalls glitter in the pines while riders take the forest trails toward the red rocks.

[weather] Sunny high 62 low 45 rain 1% sunrise 6:50 AM sunset 5:26 PM tomorrow Sunny, 66/46

[weather_caption] Gandy basks half-asleep in the sun while Maevy hunts a butterfly clean across the deck.

[today Payson] 2026 Howlin’ at the Moon — AMA/Beta National Dual Sport Series — Payson Elks Lodge, 1206 N Beeline Hwy. Two hundred riders take to the forest today and tomorrow, rain or shine. Check-in runs 6:00–8:00 AM today over a full breakfast of eggs, bacon, sausage, biscuits and gravy, and coffee, then riders head out on a 110–120 mile loop with a lunch stop near the midpoint. Registration closed October 26, so today belongs to the registered riders — and to everyone who enjoys the sight and sound of the Hold’s roads full of adventure. | 2026 Rim Country Marine Corps Ball — Mazatzal Hotel & Casino, Payson, $50 per person. The evening opens with a VIP early check-in at 4 PM and a social hour at 5 PM, followed by the formal ceremony at 6 PM — no admittance during the ceremony itself — then dinner at 7 PM, a raffle, and the famous money tornado. A band and dancing follow directly after, and the whole Hold is welcome to honor the Marines in fine style.

[today Miami] Gila County Gem & Mineral Society Fall Show and Sale — Bullion Plaza Cultural Center & Museum Yard, 150 Plaza Circle, Miami, today only, 9 AM–2 PM, free admission. Vendors fill the yard with gems, minerals, jewelry, and rocks of every stripe, and rockhounds and jewelry makers stand ready to talk shop with travelers. Popcorn and water are sold on site, and the Taqueria La Familia and Grindhead Coffee trucks keep everyone fed — a perfect short ride down the road from the Hearth, and it ends at 2 PM, so go early.

[today Camp Verde] Verde Valley Wellness Festival — Verde Valley Fairgrounds, 800 E Cherry St, Cottonwood, today 11 AM–4 PM, free admission. The first annual gathering of its kind in the Verde Valley brings holistic health practitioners, fitness professionals, local businesses, and wellness educators together for mini sessions, talks, shopping, food trucks, and family activities. It is an easy drive from Camp Verde, and a gentle way to spend the middle of a sunny Saturday.

[today Sedona] 2026 Sedona Mountain Bike Festival — Posse Grounds Park, 525 Posse Grounds Rd, Sedona, running Friday through Sunday, November 6–8. The must-visit mountain bike gathering of the year fills the park with an expo, bike demos, shuttled rides on Sedona’s famous red singletrack, gear vendors, a beer garden, food trucks, skills clinics, and live bands. Passes are sold at the festival registration booth, and today is the festival’s biggest day — arrive ready for crowds of happy riders under the red rocks.

[today Prescott] Dollar Day at Heritage Park Zoo — Heritage Park Zoological Sanctuary, 1403 Heritage Park Rd, Prescott, today 10 AM–4 PM, admission just $1. The sanctuary throws its gates open for the cheapest wild day in the Hold: stroll the grounds, meet the animals, and make a family outing of it for less than the price of a sweet roll. Dollar days draw a crowd, so the wise traveler goes in the morning and lingers. | Hike for Hounds Fall Festival — United Animal Friends Rescue Ranch, 2600 Heckethorn Rd, Prescott, today 9 AM–1 PM, entry $25. Hikers check in between 9 and 10:30 AM and walk as much of the neighboring Peavine Trail as they like, then a grilled picnic lunch is served on the ranch lawn from 11 AM to 1 PM with vendors, dog activities, face painting, raffles, music, and games. Every dollar raises money for the rescue’s animals — a good walk for a good cause. | Cosmic Coyote — a Tribute to the Grateful Dead — Elks Theatre, 117 E Gurley St, Prescott, tonight at 7 PM. A Phoenix band of professional musicians, formed in 2020, brings the Dead’s songs to the historic Elks stage with high energy, wide dynamic range, and long stretches of improvisation. Tie-dye is optional; swaying is not. Prices are shown at seat selection, and a Saturday night on Whiskey Row needs no further excuse.

[week Sun, Nov. 8] Howlin’ at the Moon, Day Two — Payson Elks Lodge, 1206 N Beeline Hwy, Payson. The dual-sport riders ride again on Sunday with fresh 50–60 mile loops through the forest around Payson, different routes from Saturday’s long run. Check-in is 6:30–8:30 AM with the same hearty breakfast, and GPS track logs and a thank-you gift are part of the day. Registered riders only — but the Hold’s trails will hum till evening. | The Thirsty Band at AZTEX Coffee and Taproom — Show Low, Sunday at 1 PM. An easygoing Sunday set at the taproom: coffee, a cold pour, and live music to close the weekend at a civilized hour. A good excuse for the scenic run over to Show Low while the sun is still high.

[week Wed, Nov. 11] Veterans Day Tribute — Sedona Heritage Museum, Uptown Sedona. The town’s official Veterans Day observance, hosted with the City of Sedona, gathers neighbors at the museum to honor those who served. It is a quiet, fitting stop in the middle of the week — come, stand with the Hold, and give thanks.

[week Fri, Nov. 13] Verde Valley Pottery Festival — First Pick Friday — D.A. Ranch Vineyards, 1900 Dancing Apache Rd, Cornville, Friday 4–6 PM, $25 early access. The festival’s fifth year opens with a ticketed first look: first choice of handmade ceramic work by Arizona potters, plus D.A. Ranch wine, local food trucks, craft beer, and live music along Oak Creek. The free festival weekend follows Saturday and Sunday — but the finest pots go to those who come Friday. | Santa’s Winter Wonderland Craft Fair — Elk’s Lodge, 805 E. Whipple St, Show Low, Friday and Saturday, November 13–14, 10 AM–4 PM each day. As many as 47 merchandise and craft vendors fill the lodge for early holiday shopping, and Santa himself appears on Saturday. Bring the young ones for a candy cane and a word with the old elf, and come home with gifts made by local hands.

[merchant name] Ace Hardware

[merchant town] Camp Verde

[merchant blurb] Every Hold needs a smithy, and Camp Verde’s wears a red Ace sign: a full hardware and home-and-garden store carrying tools, plumbing, paint, grills, and garden goods, with services a traveler actually uses — Stihl power equipment repair, propane refill or exchange, paint color matching, pipe cutting and threading, and screen repair. A little enchantment of the helpful kind seems to hang over the aisles: name the broken thing, and the right bolt, board, or fitting turns up as if summoned. This is the place that saves a project — and a weekend — in a single stop.

[merchant review] Reviewers return again and again to one word for this store: helpful — the kind of place where the staff walk you to the right aisle, know their stock cold, and send you home with exactly what the job needs.

[merchant review_src] Google reviews (paraphrased)

[merchant why] The Hearth sends guests here because no quest survives a broken fitting — and this smithy has never yet failed to arm a traveler for the repair at hand. Great praise is great, and this place earns it!

[merchant visit] 285 S Main St, Camp Verde, AZ 86322. Hours: Mon–Fri 7 AM–7 PM, Sat 8 AM–5 PM, Sun 9 AM–3 PM. Phone (928) 567-4172. Prices: moderate. Good to know: Saturday hours end at 5 PM, so make it a morning stop on a weekend project run.

[merchant image caption] The smithy of Camp Verde, where every broken thing finds its mending.

[tale title] The List That Rode the Wind

[tale] Loredas dawned bright and cool over the Hearth, with a steady breeze combing the pines — fine weather, unless you were Gus (a friendly orc baker) with a market list. Gus had written it fair and careful: flour, honey, apples, and one bag of the good cinnamon. He set it on the deck rail for one moment to tie his apron, and the breeze, that dang ol’ breeze, took it like it had been waiting all morning.

Henny (the Hearth’s plump chicken) gave chase at a professional’s trot, and Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) launched after it in his best zigzag, frosting the corners to slow it down, which only made it sail the prouder. Three laps of the clearing it led them, over the woodpile and clean through Mabel’s washing line, while Gus lumbered behind calling, “Not the cinnamon page!”

At last the list settled, gentle as a leaf, across the antlers of Earl (an elk), who had been standing in the sun minding his own dignified business. Earl did not shake it off. Earl carried it, head high, straight to Gus at the bakery door, like a herald delivering a royal decree. Gus read it, nodded once, and said the Hold’s highest praise: “Delivered in full.” Henny got a crumb for her trouble, and the cinnamon, travelers, was saved.

[tale image caption] Earl delivers the market list in full, antlers high, as is proper for a royal decree.
