By the Nine, there is plenty to do before the early 5:27 sunset — choose your adventure below.
text:
[headline] Fish Fries, Fast Bikes, and a Hold Full of Friday Merry-Making

[dateline] Friday, November 6, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, wayfarer, and pull your cloak close — Fredas dawns grey and cool over the Rim, with the pines standing quiet under a blanket of cloud and a fair breeze to hurry you along the road. The Holds are in fine Friday fettle: fish fries sizzle in Payson and Pine, Sedona’s red rocks ring with the great Mountain Bike Festival all weekend, and Show Low serves soup in hand-made bowls for a good cause. Word from the road brings glad tidings, too — the first North Inch Renaissance Faire at the Payson Golf Course last month was such a success that its organizers are already planning next year’s. By the Nine, there is plenty to do before the early 5:27 sunset — choose your adventure below.

[hero_caption] Riders, market stalls, and merry folk gather under a grey Rim sky — the Holds open a full Friday of doings.

[weather] Overcast high 57 low 45 rain 12% sunrise 6:49 AM sunset 5:27 PM tomorrow Overcast, 61/45

[weather_caption] Gandy holds the dry deck in lordly gloom while Maevy duels a runaway pine needle.

[today Payson] Payson Elks Lodge Friday Fish Fry — 5:30–7:30 PM at the Payson Elks Lodge, 1206 N Beeline Hwy. The Lodge opens the big Howlin’ at the Moon dual-sport weekend with its weekly Friday fish fry, and riders and locals alike are welcome at the table. Expect a home-style fried-fish supper in good company before Saturday’s forest loops roll out. It is the easy way for Hearth guests to meet the rider crowd without throwing a leg over a bike. Come hungry and come early — lodge suppers fill fast on event weekends. | Band of Fools at The Roadhouse — live music Friday night, 8:00 PM to midnight, at The Roadhouse in Payson. After the fish fry, the town keeps its Friday going with a late set of live band fare for folks who like their evenings with a tune in them. Dinner first, then music — the classic small-town Friday, done properly. Check the Bandsintown listing or the venue for cover and seating before you head out. A fine nightcap for guests not ready for an early bed. | GrannyCore Christmas Sale — an early Christmas sale running Friday and Saturday, Nov. 6–7, here in Payson (from the Hold’s yard-and-estate-sales sheet). Think cozy, handmade, and vintage-leaning holiday goods — the kind of sale where the best treasures go to the early birds. It pairs nicely with Saturday’s Noel Christmas Market at Noley’s for a full weekend of gift hunting. If your hearth needs trimming before the season crowds arrive, this is your opening move. No web page stands for it — ask around town and follow the sale signs.

[today Pine-Strawberry] First Friday Fish Fry and Bingo — at the Pine Strawberry Community Center, 3916 AZ-87, Pine. Fish is served from 4:30 PM (plates $7/$12/$15, with homemade pie at $5), and bingo follows at 6:00 PM. This is the twin villages’ social anchor of the month — neighbors, winter visitors, and Hearth guests all at the long tables together. Expect a community-center supper, bingo cards, and small-town prizes rather than a commercial show. Come for the fish, stay for the bingo, and bring a little cash for the pie.

[today Sedona] Sedona Mountain Bike Festival — Friday through Sunday, Nov. 6–8, 9:00 AM–7:00 PM, at Posse Grounds Park, 525 Posse Grounds Rd. One of the nation’s premier mountain-bike festivals, with more than 90 vendors and more demo bikes than any other festival of its kind. Three days of demos, shuttled rides to 250-plus miles of red-rock singletrack, guided rides, and skills clinics for beginners through experts. Add live entertainment, food trucks, and a beer garden, and the whole park hums all weekend. New this year: a Shuttle-Only Pass for riders who just want maximum trail time. | 1st Friday in the Galleries — Friday, 4:00–7:00 PM, at galleries across Sedona, including Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village, 336 State Route 179. Sedona’s galleries open together with new exhibitions, artist receptions, music, and treats — free and open to everyone. At Tlaquepaque, Mountain Trails Galleries launches a small-works show, and Creative Gateways paints live from a blank canvas. The Village Gallery in the Village of Oak Creek hosts its own reception from 5:00–8:00 PM. An easy, walkable evening — come and go from gallery to gallery as you please. | FAMoS First Friday Reception — Curt Walters: A Lifetime of Art — Friday, 5:00–8:00 PM at the Sedona Heritage Museum, with a live interview at 5:45 PM. The Fine Art Museum of Sedona hosts this free reception for the Grand Canyon plein-air master, whose show gathers works painted after he moved to Sedona in 1979. Admission is free and refreshments are served. It is a quieter, sit-down counterpoint to the gallery stroll. Guests who love landscape painting should not miss it.

[today Show Low] NPC Empty Bowls — Friday, 11:00 AM–2:00 PM, at Northland Pioneer College’s Show Low campus, Aspen Center Room 103, 1001 W. Deuce of Clubs. For a suggested $10 donation, you pick a hand-crafted ceramic bowl, fill it with soup donated by Persnikkity’s plus fresh bread — and keep the bowl. Every dollar goes to the RE:center, a local nonprofit working on health, safety, and self-sufficiency. This year adds a plant and art sale for student scholarships. No reservations — first come, first served, cash or check at the door. | Fiber Arts Gathering at NPC — Friday on the same Show Low campus, 1001 W. Deuce of Clubs. The college calendar invites one and all: “Interested in the fiber arts? Join us!” A drop-in makers’ circle for knitters, weavers, and stitchers of every level. Pair it with the Empty Bowls luncheon for a full and friendly campus visit. Check the NPC calendar for the room and hour before you go.

[today Prescott] Anthony Mazzella — Legends of Guitar — Friday, 7:00 PM, at the Prescott Elks Theatre, 117 E. Gurley St. The acclaimed virtuoso plays every note live in a high-energy tribute to the world’s iconic guitarists. Expect Hendrix, Clapton, Page, Gilmour, Harrison, Van Halen, and even Segovia in one solo show. The historic Elks Theatre on Gurley Street is half the pleasure — arrive early and soak it in. A strong Friday-night anchor for music lovers willing to make the Prescott drive. | Prescott History Tour — Friday, 10:00 AM–12:00 PM, downtown Prescott, from Whiskey Row to Nob Hill. A guided two-hour walk through the landmarks of Arizona’s original territorial capital, with the people and stories that shaped it. Daytime, outdoors, and easy-paced — a fine first introduction to Prescott for new visitors. The tour is run by Freaky Foot Tours; check the Signals AZ listing for the meeting point. Sturdy shoes and a curious mind are all you need.

[week Sat, Nov. 7] Howlin’ at the Moon Dual Sport Ride — Saturday and Sunday at the Payson Elks Lodge, 1206 N Beeline Hwy. Arizona Trail Riders’ two-day rally rides a 110–120 mile forest loop Saturday (check-in 6:00–8:00 AM) and shorter 50–60 mile loops Sunday, with breakfast at the Lodge both mornings and a home-cooked Elks dinner Saturday at 5:30 PM. Registration closed Oct. 26 and the listing marks it sold out — so print this as a spectacle, not a sign-up. The town will buzz with bikes all weekend, and the Lodge is the place to watch it gather. Rain or shine, the riders ride. | Gila County Gem & Mineral Society Fall Show & Sell — Saturday, 9:00 AM–2:00 PM, free admission, at Bullion Plaza, 150 Plaza Circle, Miami. Vendors sell gems, minerals, jewelry, and rough rock, with rockhounds and jewelry makers on hand to visit with — a small, friendly one-day show. Popcorn and water are sold on site, with food and coffee trucks alongside. Mind the early 2:00 PM close if you are driving down from Payson. A perfect Saturday prize for anyone who loves what the Rim is made of. | Rim Country Marine Corps Ball — Saturday evening at the Mazatzal Hotel & Casino, Payson. Marine Corps League Detachment #928’s formal birthday ball: social hour at 5:00 PM, ceremony at 6:00 PM (no admittance during the ceremony), dinner at 7:00 PM, then a raffle and dancing. Tickets are $50 per person on the reservation form at rimcountrymarines.org. It anchors Payson’s Veterans-week season in full dress style. Late ticket availability is not confirmed — call ahead before dressing up. | Don’t Sweat It, Shred It! — Free Shred Event — Saturday, 9:00 AM–1:00 PM, at Camp Verde Town Hall, 473 S. Main St. AARP’s free secure-shredding stop: sensitive papers do not belong in the recycling bin, so bring them for safe on-site shredding. It is a practical errand that protects against fraud, and it costs nothing. Pair it with a Camp Verde morning — Montezuma Castle or Fort Verde — and lunch after. Drive up, shred, and leave lighter. | Noel Christmas Market at Noley’s — Saturday at Noley’s Books, Art & Whatnot, 103 E. State Hwy 260, Payson. An early-season Christmas market at Payson’s beloved book-bar and gathering place, carried from the Hold’s own listings. Expect local makers, books, art, and holiday goods in Noley’s cozy rooms. It makes a fine Saturday pair with Friday’s GrannyCore sale for gift hunters. No web page stands for the market — check Noley’s own page or just come by and see.

[week Sun, Nov. 8] The Thirsty Band at AZTEX Coffee and Taproom — Sunday, 1:00 PM, in Show Low. A relaxed Sunday-afternoon live set at a coffee-and-taproom — the gentle end of a busy weekend. The band returns to the same room Friday, Nov. 13, so locals get two chances. Good low-key fare for guests overnighting in the White Mountains. Check the Bandsintown listing for cover and updates before going.

[week Mon, Nov. 9] United Food Bank — Payson Food Distribution — Monday, 9:00–11:00 AM, at 601 AZ-260, Payson. A drive-through distribution of produce and pantry staples, listed in the Holiday Helpings roundup for families getting ready for Thanksgiving. The listing notes a turkey is not guaranteed at this stop — come for the groceries, not a promise. This is a know-where-to-send-folks item: pass the word to any neighbor who could use a hand. Volunteers and donations are the other way to take part.

[week Wed, Nov. 11] Prescott Veterans Day Parade — Wednesday in downtown Prescott; opening ceremonies 10:30 AM at Cortez and Union, parade at 11:00 AM around Courthouse Plaza. This year’s theme, from the City itself: “Remember the Past. Serve the Present. Inspire the Future.” Entries compete in seven categories plus Best Overall, and the whole community is invited, free. Arrive before 10:30 for the ceremony and a good spot on Cortez Street. A worthy midweek drive for every guest who honors those who served.

[merchant name] Ruby Road Vintage Mall

[merchant town] Camp Verde

[merchant blurb] Eight thousand square feet of treasure just off Highway 260 — more than 60 vendor booths of vintage and repurposed furniture, home décor, clothing, hand-poured candles, locally crafted jewelry, gourmet treats, and artisan goods. The furniture room is the signature hunt: hundreds of pieces, and the house rule is plain — drawers glide, hinges work, no holes. A whisper of an Appraisal enchantment hangs over the place, the regulars swear, for the right piece seems to find its traveler the moment he walks in.

[merchant review] It’s really fun to look around, plus it’s clean, and it doesn’t have that musky odor that some resale shops have

[merchant review_src] Flagstaff Business News, quoting customer and local artist Sheri Morris

[merchant why] The Hearth sends guests here on the Camp Verde day — Montezuma Castle and Fort Verde in the morning, then one great treasure hunt where every traveler finds something to carry home.

[merchant visit] 851 E Howards Rd, Camp Verde — open seven days, 10 AM–5 PM; phone (928) 567-5759; $$ (moderate). Good to know: new furniture lands daily in the shop and online — call before driving down for a piece you spotted on their website.

[merchant image caption] Inside Ruby Road: sixty booths of treasures, and the furniture room is the stuff of legend.

[quest] Build the Mogollon’s Hearth shield Due Oct. 17 — laser-cut layered plywood shield, troll relief mounted on top, spar urethane finish.

[quest] Mount the shield by the front door Due Oct. 24 — hang on a French cleat beside the front door, best view from the walkway.

[quest] Finish & install the torches Due Oct. 10 — wire the sockets into the door-light boxes, mount both torches, test at dusk.

[quest] Doors — Mogollon Hearth Due Oct. 24 — the Hearth’s door work stands ready on the quest board.

[tale title] Mittens for the Antlers

[tale] Fredas dawned grey and cool, and Mabel (a wood elf) looked out at the cloud blanket and declared it a knitting day. By mid-morning she had finished two tiny mittens — and then, eyeing Earl (an elk), she kept right on knitting.

“For the antler tips,” she said, tying the first one on while Earl stood very still and tried to look like this was normal. “A dignified elk should not have cold antlers.” Earl, who takes himself more seriously than any creature in the forest, bore it with enormous dignity, which is to say he pretended not to notice the mittens, the onlookers, or Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) following him around making soft, impressed noises.

Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) wanted in, of course. There were not enough mittens for a monster, so he wore the spares as socks — one on each great foot — and paraded the clearing with his toes wiggling in striped wool. Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) offered to chill the mittens “for authenticity,” and was voted down by everyone, including the mittens.

By evening Earl was still wearing his, purely, he said, because removing them would be undignified. Mabel has orders for six more pairs. The forest has never been warmer, or prouder.

[tale image caption] Earl endures his antler mittens with enormous dignity; Jethro takes the spares as socks.

headline: Grey Skies, Full Tables: The Holds Tune Up for a Festival Weekend
greeting: Hail, traveler, and pull your cloak close — Turdas dawns grey and cool over the Rim this Thursday, November 5, with a high of 60, overcast skies, light winds, and no rain in it at all. The Holds spend the day well anyway: a farmers market down in Cornville at 2:00 PM, tai chi in Pinetop-Lakeside at 10:00 AM, and Prescott keeping its courthouse lit with a live auction from 4:00 PM. And the whole week is gathering behind today like riders at a trailhead — the great Sedona Mountain Bike Festival opens Friday, November 6, a Pine fish fry fries the same night, and a star party, an open mic, and a veterans concert follow close behind. By the Nine, a grey sky is no excuse at all: the mead is warm, the tables are full, and the road is calling.
text:
[headline] Grey Skies, Full Tables: The Holds Tune Up for a Festival Weekend

[dateline] Thursday, November 5, 2026

[lead] Hail, traveler, and pull your cloak close — Turdas dawns grey and cool over the Rim this Thursday, November 5, with a high of 60, overcast skies, light winds, and no rain in it at all. The Holds spend the day well anyway: a farmers market down in Cornville at 2:00 PM, tai chi in Pinetop-Lakeside at 10:00 AM, and Prescott keeping its courthouse lit with a live auction from 4:00 PM. And the whole week is gathering behind today like riders at a trailhead — the great Sedona Mountain Bike Festival opens Friday, November 6, a Pine fish fry fries the same night, and a star party, an open mic, and a veterans concert follow close behind. By the Nine, a grey sky is no excuse at all: the mead is warm, the tables are full, and the road is calling.

[hero_caption] Iron steeds gather under the red rocks — the great Sedona ride opens tomorrow.

[weather] Overcast high 60 low 42 rain 0% sunrise 6:49 AM sunset 5:28 PM tomorrow Overcast, 60/45

[weather_caption] Gandy dozes under the grey Turdas sky while Maevy chases one brave leaf.

[today Payson] “Got Sneakers” Recycle and Fundraiser runs all day today, Thursday, November 5, in the Payson Unified School District, and continues through November 19. Old sneakers that might have gone to the midden instead get a second road to run, and the drive raises funds along the way. It is an easy good deed for guests with a spare pair in the wagon — ask at a school office where the collection stands. A small quest, honestly, but the best kind: one anybody can finish before supper.

[today Camp Verde] Windmill Park Farmers Market sets up today, Thursday, November 5, from 2:00 PM at Windmill Park, 9950 E. Cornville Road in Cornville, down the Verde road from Camp Verde. Local growers and makers bring produce, baked goods, and handmade wares to an easy afternoon market in the valley. It is a fine excuse for a scenic ride and a full basket. Valley Dwellers climbing up for Rim Country air will find the valley itself in a generous mood.

[today Sedona] Sedona Mountain Bike Festival Robbers Roost Overnighter rolls out today, Thursday, November 5, from 10:00 AM at Cultural Park in Sedona. It is a group bikepacking trip tied to this weekend’s great festival — riders load their iron steeds, ride out under the red rocks, and camp like proper wayfarers. A fine warm-up for the festival crowds gathering tomorrow. If you meet them on the road, give them the wide side and a hail.

[today Show Low] Tai Chi meets today, Thursday, November 5, at 10:00 AM at the Community Center, 1594 Johnson Drive in Pinetop-Lakeside, just down the road from Show Low, and the first time is free. Slow, steady movement in good company — the sort of morning practice that leaves a traveler loose-limbed and clear-headed for the road. Newcomers are welcome at the back of the hall. Wear soft shoes and bring your patience; both will be used gently. | Intro to West Coast Swing steps out today, Thursday, November 5, at 6:40 PM at 640 E. White Mountain Blvd. in Pinetop-Lakeside, near Show Low. A beginner-friendly evening of swing dancing, where the first steps are taught plainly and nobody is left counting alone for long. Partners and solo travelers alike are welcome on the floor. By the Nine, even a bard needs a rest from the lute now and then — dancing will do it.

[today Prescott] Live Auction — Courthouse Christmas Lighting Fundraiser Kick-Off Party runs today, Thursday, November 5, from 4:00 to 8:00 PM at the Jersey Lilly Saloon, 116 S. Montezuma Street in Prescott. Friends of the Jersey Lilly raise funds to keep Prescott’s famous courthouse lighting shining, with live and silent auction lots and a hall full of neighbors. Bid on something fine, or simply cheer the bidding on. Either way, the lights you enjoy in December start with nights like this one. | The Beauty of Granite Mountain is presented today, Thursday, November 5, at 7:00 PM at the Natural History Institute, 126 North Marina Street in Prescott. An evening given to the great granite shoulder that watches over the town — its stone, its trails, and the creatures that call it home. Lovers of the high country will feel right at home in the audience. Come learn why the Hold’s own Rim has a worthy cousin to the west.

[week Fri, Nov. 6] Sedona Mountain Bike Festival opens Friday, November 6, at 9:00 AM at Posse Grounds Park, 525 Posse Grounds Road in Sedona, and runs through Sunday, November 8. Riders descend on Sedona’s famous red singletrack for demo rides, shuttles, and guided group rides, with food trucks, a beer garden, and live music between runs. The festival site says tickets will be sold daily at the registration booth during the event. By the Nine, it is the biggest wheel-show in the Holds this week. | First Friday Fish Fry and Bingo returns Friday, November 6, at the Pine Strawberry Community Center, 3916 AZ-87 in Pine. Fish is served from 4:30 PM at $7, $12, or $15, with homemade pie at $5, and bingo starts at 6:00 PM. The hall fills with neighbors, the fryers sing, and somebody always goes home hoarse from cheering a card. Arrive hungry and early — the pie has a way of vanishing first. | GrannyCore Christmas Sale opens Friday, November 6, in Payson and runs through Saturday, November 7, the Hold’s yard-and-estate-sales sheet reports. Early Christmas treasures, handmade and homey goods, and the sort of finds that start a season right — all gathered for two days. Treasure hunters should come with a list and leave with a story. Check the sales sheet on the Hearth’s table for the address before you ride out.

[week Sat, Nov. 7] Noel Christmas Market at Noley’s fills Saturday, November 7, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM at Noley’s Books, Art & Whatnot, 103 E. State Hwy 260 in Payson. Books, art, gifts, and Christmas goods crowd the shelves and tables of the Hold’s beloved bookshop for one merry market day. It is the easiest early gift quest in town. Come for one present and leave, as everyone does, with three and a book for yourself. | Star Party at Red Rock State Park begins Saturday, November 7, at 5:30 PM at 4050 Red Rock Loop Road in Sedona. Telescopes come out as the light goes down, and the red rocks turn to silhouettes under a sky full of cold, bright stars. Guides help visitors find planets and constellations, so no star-lore is required — only warm layers. A clear desert night sky is pure mead for the eyes.

[week Sun, Nov. 8] A Tribute to the Ol’ Cherokee Cowboy plays Sunday, November 8, at 3:00 PM at the Elks Theatre, 117 E. Gurley Street in Prescott. An afternoon of song and story in honor of a western legend makes a fine Sunday outing for music lovers. Expect warm harmonies, tall tales told straight-faced, and a room full of folks who know the choruses. Get there a little early for a good seat.

[tale title] The Sun Jethro Painted

[tale] Turdas dawned grey from rim to rim, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) declared the sky had forgotten its job. So he fetched a bowl of golden paint Gus (an orc baker) had mixed for honey cakes, knelt by the big flat rock in the Hearth clearing, and set about painting the sun back himself — one great round face, with rays as long as Earl’s antlers.

Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) inspected the work the proper way: she walked straight through the paint bowl, then proudly around the rock, then across the deck, leaving a trail of small golden footprints for the whole Hold to admire. Earl (an elk) stood over the painted sun with enormous dignity and announced that it was, at least, warmer than the real one had managed all morning.

Mabel (a wood elf) sighed, fetched a brush, and painted one small grey cloud in the rock’s corner, for honest measure. By supper the painted sun was the cheeriest thing in the clearing, Henny’s footprints led three guests straight to the front door, and that dang ol’ Jethro was taking full credit for the weather — which, being overcast still, belonged to nobody at all.

[tale image caption] The painted sun was warmer than the real one managed all morning.

[tale title] The Loaf That Followed the Sun

[tale] Middas dawned bright and cool, and Gus (an orc baker) set his sourdough bowl on the Hearth deck to rise in the sunbeam, declaring that sunshine was the only leavening a wise baker truly trusts. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) took one look at the warm bowl, climbed up, and sat on the rim like a queen on a throne, which the dough did not mind and Gus did.

Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) worried the sun would spoil it and helpfully shaded the bowl with one wing, so Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) took up the bowl and solemnly carried it three steps west, following the sunbeam as it slid across the deck boards. Earl (an elk) stood perfectly still as the official sundial, announced the hour by the shadow of his antlers, and was correct twice.

All morning the procession shuffled — bowl, chicken, dragon-wing parasol, and one dang ol’ monster timekeeper — until the loaf had risen clear to the bowl’s brim. Mabel (a wood elf) sighed, baked it, and served it warm, and even Henny agreed the sun had done fine work, once it finally sat still in the oven.

[tale image caption] The official sundial was correct twice — and the loaf rose anyway.

[tale] Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) declared the first Great Cloud-Watching Championship on Tirdas, spread a blanket in the Hearth clearing, and flopped onto his back with great ceremony. The sky, being overcast from rim to rim, offered the contestants exactly one cloud, and it was the size of the whole Hold.

Earl (an elk) stared upward with enormous dignity and announced he could see a noble elk in it. Mabel (a wood elf) sighed and said she could see a grey blanket, because it was a grey blanket, and the judging was rigged. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) walked across Jethro’s face mid-deliberation, which the rules apparently allow.

Then Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) zigzagged up and breathed one small, sparkling ice-crystal cloud of his very own, shaped — he insisted — exactly like a chicken. Henny inspected it, clucked once, and claimed the trophy on the grounds that she was clearly the model. Mabel declared everybody tied for first, Jethro declared the snacks the real winner, and that dang ol’ grey sky never stood a chance.

[tale image caption] One grey cloud, five champions — and one small ice cloud shaped, allegedly, like a chicken.

[headline] Creeks Rise Over the Crossings, and the Holds Hold Fast

[dateline] Monday, November 2, 2026

[lead] Hail, wayfarer, and mind the crossings — Morndas dawns grey and cool over the Rim, and the waters are still up after Sunday’s storm. The National Weather Service in Flagstaff kept a Flood Warning in force until 8:00 AM today, Monday, November 2, for parts of Gila, Coconino, and Yavapai counties, after 2 to 5 inches of rain fell across the warned country. Flooding was reported around Payson, Pine, Strawberry, and the Tonto Creek country, roads were closed at low-water crossings, and on Sunday afternoon parts of Gisela and Tonto Basin were told to evacuate to higher ground. Northland Pioneer College said all its campuses would not open until 11:00 AM today because of the flooding. So the Hearth’s counsel is plain and warm: stay off the crossings, never drive around a barricade, and let the creeks settle — the mead hall is dry, the cats are dry, and there is a full week of markets, music, trail work, and mountain bikes ahead once the water goes down.

[hero_caption] Sunday’s waters at the crossing — neighbors with lanterns guiding travelers to high, dry ground.

[weather] Overcast high 54 low 43 rain 25% sunrise 6:46 AM sunset 5:31 PM tomorrow Overcast, 60/43

[weather_caption] Gandy endures the grey under the eaves while Maevy bats at the rain that dares to fall.

[today Payson] “Got Sneakers” Recycle and Fundraiser begins today, Monday, November 2, and runs through November 19 in the Payson Unified School District. Old sneakers that might have gone to the midden instead get a second road to run, and the drive raises funds along the way. It is an easy good deed for guests with a spare pair in the wagon — ask at a school office where the collection stands. A small quest, honestly, but the best kind: one anybody can finish before supper. | A Quiet Morndas in the Hold — after Sunday’s flood waters, Payson’s verified calendar for today is deliberately light, and that is no shame in it. The creeks are still settling, the Flood Warning ran until 8:00 AM, and the wise traveler spends the day on high, dry ground. Warm up in a cafe, browse the shops on Main Street, and let the road crews do their work unhurried. The Holds will be lively again by the weekend, as The Days Ahead below can testify.

[today Show Low] Story Time at Show Low Public Library meets on Mondays in the Kids Room at the Show Low Public Library, the city’s own live feed says. Little travelers get stories read aloud in a warm, dry room while the grown folk rest their boots — a gentle way to start a grey week. It is made for young children and the people who bring them, and it costs nothing but attention. Call the library at 928-532-4070 for the day’s hour before you ride over.

[today Prescott] Prescott Farmers Market sets up today, Monday, November 2, from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM at Yavapai College, 1100 E. Sheldon Street in Prescott. Local farmers, ranchers, bakers, and makers bring fresh produce, meats, eggs, bread, and ready-to-eat treats to the tables. Entry is free, and SNAP/EBT and farmers market nutrition benefits are accepted, the market’s own word says. Valley Dwellers riding up for Rim Country air will find it a fine first stop of the week. | Fairweather Social Club gathers today, Monday, November 2, in Prescott, listed on the Prescott 365 events calendar. Expect the friendly machinery of a social club done right: drinks, company, and the easy talk of neighbors glad to see each other after a wet weekend. It is a traveler-friendly evening — come as you are, find a seat, and let somebody else pour. Check the Prescott 365 listing for the day’s hour and hall before you set out. | BINGO — Mondays at Jersey Lilly Saloon starts at 6:00 PM tonight at 116 S. Montezuma Street, Suite A, in Prescott. The cards come out, the caller warms up, and a room full of hopefuls leans over the same numbers with very different luck. It is old-fashioned, cheerful, and exactly the sort of Monday mischief a mead hall would approve of. Arrive a little early to claim a good seat and a drink before the first call.

[week Tue, Nov. 3] Trail Day Volunteer Build in Pine, Tuesday, November 3, from 7:00 AM to 12:00 PM, off Highway 87 just before Pine. Pine-Strawberry Fuel Reduction calls hikers, bikers, and runners to clear brush, move rocks, and shape a trail that will serve the Hold for years — and double as a fire-access route. Tools are provided; bring water, gloves, and sturdy shoes, and email trails@psfuelreduction.org for directions. No experience needed, only willing hands. | Snakes! Lizards! Tortoises! on Tuesday, November 3, from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM at Creative Gateways / Kuivato Gallery, Tlaquepaque North, 336 AZ-179 in Sedona, and it is free. Visitors get a hands-on hour with desert reptiles, including Riggs the desert tortoise, a creature with more patience than most jarls. It is a splendid hour for curious children and grown travelers alike. Come learn which neighbors wear scales, and why they deserve respect, not fear.

[week Wed, Nov. 4] Wildflower Walk on Wednesday, November 4, from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Highlands Center for Natural History, 1375 S. Walker Road in Prescott. A guide leads walkers through the highland woods to see what the season still offers after the rains, at a pace made for looking closely. The walk is free, and an RSVP is required, the center’s calendar says. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water — the trails will still remember the weekend’s weather.

[week Fri, Nov. 6] Sedona Mountain Bike Festival opens Friday, November 6, at 9:00 AM at Posse Grounds Park, 525 Posse Grounds Road in Sedona, and runs through Sunday, November 8. Riders descend on Sedona’s famous red singletrack for demo rides and guided group rides, with food trucks, a beer garden, and live music between runs. Even travelers who never mount a bike will enjoy the festival air. By the Nine, it is the biggest wheel-show in the Holds this week. | Small Works Show — Opening Reception on Friday, November 6, from 4:00 to 7:00 PM at Mountain Trails Gallery in Tlaquepaque, Sedona, and it is free. Paintings, sculpture, and mixed-media works by the gallery’s award-winning artists fill the walls, including new work for the holiday season. Animal artist Sarah Webber demonstrates the next day, Saturday, November 7, from noon to 4:00 PM. The show itself runs through December 31. | Anthony Mazzella — Legends of Guitar plays Friday, November 6, at 7:00 PM at the Prescott Elks Theater in Prescott. Mazzella’s fingers do the traveling — a concert of guitar legends reimagined by one of Arizona’s best-known players, in a grand old theater made for live music. Bard-work of the highest order, and a fine Friday night out for Hearth guests. Tickets are through the theater and its listings, so claim seats before the hall fills. | First Friday Fish Fry and Bingo on Friday, November 6, at the Pine Strawberry Community Center, 3916 AZ-87 in Pine. Fish is served from 4:30 PM — dinners at $7, $12, and $15, with homemade pie for $5 — and bingo starts at 6:00 PM. It is the twin villages’ own mead-hall night: hot food, sweet pie, and numbers called over a happy room. Come hungry, bring small bills, and may your card be luckier than Earl’s antlers.

[week Sat, Nov. 7] Hike for Hounds Fall Festival on Saturday, November 7, from 9:00 AM in Prescott, a fall festival built around a good hike with good dogs. Travelers and their four-legged companions get fresh air, festival company, and the satisfaction of a walk that helps animals in need. It is the sort of wholesome quest the Hearth loves to send guests on. Bring water for both ends of the leash, and check the festival listing for the trailhead before you go.

[merchant name] Merchant Coffee

[merchant town] Prescott

[merchant blurb] Inside the Founding Fathers Collective at 218 N. Granite Street, Merchant Coffee pours handcrafted, Italian-style craft coffee made with specialty beans from Provision Coffee & Roaster of Phoenix — cold brew, nitro, and lemonade made fresh in house, plus local pastries to go with them. A kindly enchantment of spaciousness seems to rest on the hall: it is the most spacious coffee shop in Prescott for leisure or a workday, with a tap wall of ales, beers, and meads in the same collective for later in the day. Start with a latte and a local pastry — that is the signature pairing the house itself recommends.

[merchant review] Had a great cup of coffee and enjoyed the live music. They have a massive tap wall with various ales, beers, meads, and more. You can also try a bloody mary or mimosa sampler. Very friendly service in a relaxing environment.

[merchant review_src] Founding Fathers Collective website — guest testimonials

[merchant why] Because a merchant named Merchant, pouring mead-adjacent cheer beside the coffee, was clearly sent to this paper by the Nine — and because Hearth guests get Prescott’s roomiest, friendliest coffee hall in one stop.

[merchant visit] 218 N. Granite St., Prescott, AZ 86301. Hours: Monday–Friday 6:00 AM–7:00 PM, Saturday–Sunday 7:00 AM–7:00 PM. Phone (928) 541-1556. Coffee-shop prices. Good to know: the collective holds several local businesses under one roof, so a coffee stop can grow into a browse — plan a little extra time.

[merchant image caption] The Merchant himself, pouring for travelers — coffee first, mead talk later.

[quest] Design & prep the torch sconces Measure the flame bulb and socket, scale the sconce model, slice in PETG — due September 26, longest waiting.

[quest] Print the torch sconces Print two torches plus the socket test piece and test-fit the bulb — due October 3.

[quest] Finish & install the torches Paint, seal against the sun, wire into the door-light boxes with the breaker off — due October 10.

[quest] Build the Mogollon’s Hearth shield Laser-cut layered plywood, 3D-print the troll relief, finish with spar urethane — due October 17.

[quest] Mount the shield by the front door Hang it on a French cleat beside the front door, where the walkway sees it best — due October 24.

[quest] Doors — Mogollon Hearth The front and side door work for the guest house — due October 24.

[due soon] Longest waiting at the bench: Design & prep the torch sconces — due September 26 and ready to start, by the Nine.

[quest caption] At the bench: a shield taking shape, torch sconces printing, and a door being fitted true.

[tale title] The Marooned Elk Breakfast Rescue

[tale] Earl (an elk) took his usual dignified morning walk on Morndas and found the garden path under grey skies turned into a shining puddle-sea, with himself standing very seriously on the one dry rock in the middle of it. He would not wet his hooves. Earl has standards, and the standards were winning.

Gus (an orc baker) arrived with a tray of warm acorn muffins and took the problem personally, as bakers do. Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) breathed a careful frost over flat stepping stones laid across the puddle, one zigzag at a time, while Mabel (a wood elf) sighed and held the tray steady and pretended she was not impressed. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) rode on the tray lid as navigator, pointing her beak at the safest stone like a tiny admiral.

The crossing took four stones, two wobbles, and one muffin sacrificed to the puddle gods. Earl ate his breakfast on his rock with enormous dignity, frost on his antlers and crumbs on his chin, and declared the rescue satisfactory. That dang ol’ puddle never stood a chance.

[tale image caption] Four stones, two wobbles, one muffin lost — breakfast reached Earl intact.

text:
[headline] A New Market Hall for Payson, and Rain Over All the Holds

[dateline] Sunday, November 1, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, guest of the Hearth, and shake the rain from your cloak by the door! Sundas comes in wet over the Rim — hard rain, a high of 57 and a low of 47, and a 100% chance of rain — and still the Holds are full of doings: Payson’s own TJ Maxx throws open its doors for its grand opening today at 400 E State Hwy 260, Sedona’s farmers market opens its winter season late this morning, and Prescott dances to flamenco guitars this afternoon. One sad note — Tlaquepaque’s Day of the Dead celebration in Sedona has been called off for the storm. By the Nine, keep your lantern lit and your cloak dry.

[hero_caption] A rainy market day under the Rim — new doors opening in Payson and lanterns lit across the Holds.

[weather] Hard rain high 57 low 47 rain 100% sunrise 6:45 AM sunset 5:32 PM tomorrow Overcast, 53/41

[weather_caption] Gandy sulks dry beneath the eaves while Maevy conducts the rain from the deck rail.

[today Payson] TJ Maxx Grand Opening, 8:00 AM–8:00 PM at 400 E State Hwy 260, Payson. A brand-new market hall for the Hold opens its doors today: the off-price favorite’s first day in Payson, with grand opening hours running the full day. Expect racks of clothing, home goods, and treasure-hunt bargains, and a crowd of neighbors doing the same happy hunting. Valley Dwellers are already trading the lowland heat for Rim Country air — and today, for first pick of the shelves. Go early for the best of it, and bring a cloak for the rain between the door and the cart.

[today Sedona] Sedona Community Farmers Market — Winter Season Opens, 11:00 AM–3:00 PM at the Wells Fargo Bank lot, 2201 W SR 89A, Sedona. The market’s winter season starts today, with later hours than summer: local growers, bakers, and makers set out fresh produce, baked goods, jams, and Rim Country flavor in every stall. Everything sold here is grown by the farmers themselves — no reselling — so what you carry home is the real harvest. A gentle late-morning outing, rain and all, with the red rocks standing guard. Come hungry and leave with a full basket. | Day of the Dead at Tlaquepaque — Called Off for the Weather. A sad note, travelers: Tlaquepaque’s Día de los Muertos celebration, planned for today at 336 State Route 179 in Sedona, has been canceled because of the storm — the village’s own page says so in plain words. The altars, marigolds, and music will have to wait for next year. If your heart was set on honoring the day, light a candle at the Hearth tonight and raise a mug to those who have gone before. The bards will sing the celebration back next autumn.

[today Prescott] Tierra Flamenca: Guitar, Dance, and Classical Roots, 3:00 PM at Ruth Street Community Theater in Prescott, tickets $28–$69. Lena Jácome dances and Chris Jácome plays, with Arizona Philharmonic strings behind them — heels striking the stage and guitar carrying the hall. A rich, warm afternoon of music to close a wet weekend, and well worth the drive over the hill. The theater crowd dresses a little fine for this one. Book ahead; seats in a hall this size go quickly. | Whole Food Plant Based Cooking Class, 1:00 PM at Prescott Seventh Day Adventist Church, Prescott. A hands-on afternoon of plant-based cooking — recipes, tastings, and kitchen wisdom for anyone curious about eating more from the garden and less from the packet. Friendly instruction and plenty of samples make it a fine rainy-day outing. Newcomers are welcome; no experience with a skillet is required. Bring your appetite and your questions.

[week Mon, Nov. 2] Prescott Farmers Market, 9:00 AM–1:00 PM at Yavapai College, 1100 E Sheldon St., Prescott. Dozens of growers and makers with fresh produce, baked goods, local honey, and ready-to-eat food, plus live entertainment — the region’s oldest farmers market, running since 1997. Free entry, SNAP and EBT welcome, and FMNP coupons accepted. A cheerful Monday-morning provision run for any guest’s kitchen. Go early for the best of the bread and greens.

[week Tue, Nov. 3] Trail Day Volunteer Build in Pine, 7:00 AM–12:00 PM off Highway 87 just before Pine. Pine Strawberry Fuel Reduction invites hikers, bikers, runners, and neighbors to clear brush, move rocks, and shape trails that will serve the Hold for years — and give fire crews better access when it matters. Tools are provided; bring water, gloves if you have them, and sturdy shoes. To volunteer, email trails@psfuelreduction.org for directions and details. Good work, good company, and a trail to be proud of. | Snakes! Lizards! Tortoises!, 11:00 AM at 336 AZ-179, Sedona. A close-up morning with the desert’s scaly neighbors — the kind of talk where the creatures are the teachers and every kid in the room leans in. Fine family fare for a school-day adventure, with handlers who know their beasts and love questions. Come with curiosity; leave with respect for the wildlife under the Rim. Arrive early — the front rows fill with small naturalists fast.

[week Wed, Nov. 4] Wildflower Walk, 10:00 AM–12:00 PM at the Highlands Center for Natural History, 1375 S. Walker Rd., Prescott. A guided walk through Lynx Creek’s highland trails to see what still blooms along the creek this late in the season, led by center naturalists who know every plant by name. Free, but an RSVP is required — sign up on the center’s calendar page. Easy walking and good company in the pines. Dress for the weather and bring your curiosity.

[week Fri, Nov. 6] Sedona Mountain Bike Festival opens at 9:00 AM at Posse Grounds, 525 Posse Grounds Rd., Sedona. Three days of red-rock riding begin: demo bikes, group rides, shuttled runs, gear vendors, food trucks, and a festival crowd of riders from every Hold and beyond. Even non-riders will enjoy the spectacle, the bands, and the food. The Rim’s trails show off their best this weekend. If you ride, bring your legs; if you watch, bring a chair. | Small Works Show opening reception, 4:00–7:00 PM at Mountain Trails Gallery in Tlaquepaque, Sedona. The gallery’s popular Small Works show opens with new pieces by Arizona artist Greg Heil and others, with animal artist Sarah Webber in attendance. Small pieces, big country — a fine First Friday evening among the galleries. The show runs through the holidays, so a gift hunt can start right here. Wine, art, and good talk in a beautiful courtyard setting. | Anthony Mazzella — Legends of Guitar, 7:00 PM at the Prescott Elks Theater. A night of guitar legends’ music played by a master of the instrument, in one of the prettiest old theaters in the territory. Expect the great riffs and melodies every traveler knows, played up close in a room built for sound. A strong close to the week’s doings. Seats in historic halls go fast — plan ahead and dress for an evening out.

[week Sat, Nov. 7] Hike for Hounds Fall Festival, 9:00 AM in Prescott. A fall morning where the dogs are the guests of honor — a group hike and festival fun with four-legged companions leading the way. Expect wagging tails, happy chaos, and a crowd that takes pup pageantry seriously. A grand outing for anyone traveling with a hound. Bring water for both ends of the leash.

[merchant name] Prescott Antiques

[merchant town] Prescott

[merchant blurb] A true treasure hall less than a mile from Courthouse Plaza: two three-story buildings brimming with antiques, classic cars, coins, toys, rocks and minerals, jewelry, vintage clothing, and mid-century décor — even vintage Star Wars figures standing guard over the aisles. A whisper of finding-magic seems to hang over the place, the way the one thing you did not know you were hunting calls out from a crowded shelf. The signature stop is downstairs: a coffee and bakehouse serving fresh-baked cookies, pies, cobbler, muffins, and egg sandwiches. They buy single items, whole estates, and classic cars too.

[merchant review] The fresh-baked cookies I tried were absolutely delicious, and there were plenty of tempting pies and pastries as well.

[merchant review_src] Google review, via Wanderlog

[merchant why] Because a guest who loves a treasure hunt deserves a whole afternoon of one — three floors of wonders, with a fresh cookie waiting at the bottom of the stairs.

[merchant visit] 915 E Gurley St, Prescott, AZ 86301. Hours: Mon–Sat 9 AM–5 PM, Sun 10 AM–4 PM. Phone (928) 800-9776. Price: moderate. Good to know: the place is handicap-friendly, with ramps and electric chair rails at every stairway — and you can happily spend a long browse in its nooks and crannies before the cookie downstairs.

[merchant image caption] Three floors of treasures, and a cookie waiting downstairs — Prescott Antiques.

[quest] Design & prep the torch sconces Measure the flame bulb and socket, then scale a wall-torch model to fit — the quest that starts them all. Due Sept. 26 — overdue.

[quest] Print the torch sconces Print two torches plus the socket test piece, and test-fit bulb and socket first. Due Oct. 3 — overdue.

[quest] Finish & install the torches Paint faux wrought iron or wood, UV seal, then wire the sockets with the breaker OFF. Due Oct. 10 — overdue.

[quest] Build the Mogollon’s Hearth shield Finalize the size for the door placement, then cut and engrave. Due Oct. 17 — overdue.

[quest] Mount the shield by the front door Hang it on a French cleat beside the front door, placed for best sight from the walkway. Due Oct. 24 — overdue.

[quest] Doors — Mogollon Hearth Front and side door work for the guest house. Due Oct. 24 — overdue.

[due soon] Longest waiting on the board: the torch sconces — their design was due back on Saturday, Sept. 26, and the torches still want lighting, by the Nine!

[quest caption] The Hearth workshop: shield, sconces, and doors waiting on the bench.

[tale title] The Great Soup Crossing

[tale] Sundas dawned wet over the Hearth, and by mid-morning the porch boards shone like a millpond. That was when Gus (the orc baker) came out of the kitchen carrying his great covered pot of pumpkin soup, bound for Mabel’s porch across the yard, where Mabel (the wood elf) waited with an empty bowl and her most patient sigh.

The puddles were too wide to step and too deep to wade, so Flurry (the young ice-breathing dragon) set to work. Stone by stone he breathed flat cakes of ice across the water, and Gus — enormous hands, delicate cargo — tiptoed over them like a dancer at a jarl’s feast, one great foot at a time.

Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) rode the whole crossing on the pot lid, unbothered as a ship’s captain in a storm. Halfway across she gave one flat cluck, which everyone agreed was navigation advice. The soup arrived hot, dry, and unspilled, and Mabel declared it the finest delivery the Treeline has ever seen. That dang ol’ Flurry has already applied for the job of ferryman, and Gus is charging him one bowl per crossing.

[tale image caption] Gus keeps the soup dry, Flurry lays the road, and Henny captains the pot.

[today Show Low] Show Low Main Street Halloween Trunk or Treat 2026, from 3:00 PM on Main Street in downtown Show Low. Rows of decorated trunks, costumed kids, and candy by the bagful in the heart of town — the White Mountains way of doing Halloween up right. Families can make an early start here and still be home before the rain gets serious. Costumes encouraged for grown-ups too.

[today Prescott] Halloween on Mt. Vernon, from 2:00 PM on Mt. Vernon Ave in the historic district, and it is free. The avenue closes for one of the most loved Halloween walks in Arizona: historic homes, big decorations, and treats handed out along the street. Tools are provided; bring water, gloves if you have them, and sturdy shoes. To volunteer, email trails@psfuelreduction.org for directions and details. | Snakes! Lizards! Tortoises!, 11:00 AM at 336 AZ-179, Sedona. A close-up morning with the desert’s scaly neighbors — the kind of talk where the creatures are the teachers and every kid in the room leans in. Fine family fare for a school-day adventure. Come with questions; leave with respect for the wildlife under the Rim.

[week Fri, Nov. 6] Sedona Mountain Bike Festival opens at 9:00 AM at Posse Grounds, 525 Posse Grounds Rd., Sedona. Three days of red-rock riding begin: demo bikes, group rides, and a festival crowd of riders from every Hold and beyond. Even non-riders will enjoy the spectacle and the food. The Rim’s trails show off their best this weekend. | Small Works Show opening reception, 4:00–7:00 PM at Mountain Trails Gallery in Tlaquepaque, Sedona. The gallery’s popular Small Works show opens with new work by Arizona artist Greg Heil and others, plus animal artist Sarah Webber in attendance. A night of guitar legends’ music played by a master of the instrument, in one of the prettiest old theaters in the territory. A strong close to the week’s doings. Seats in historic halls go fast — plan ahead.

[merchant name] Bill’s Pizza

[merchant town] Prescott

[merchant blurb] A downtown Prescott institution on Cortez Street, right across from Courthouse Square and Whiskey Row, serving sourdough-crust pizzas with fresh toppings — by the whole pie or by the slice. The signature bite is that sourdough crust itself, with named pies like the Eastwood and Nonni’s Pie leading the board; a touch of kitchen magic — call it a slow-rise enchantment — is what lets a crust come out crisp, chewy, and full of flavor every single time. Dine in or take out, lunch and dinner.

[merchant review] Bills Pizza in Prescott is THE BEST EVER!! I love the sourdough crust they make for their pizza.

[merchant review_src] TripAdvisor review

[merchant why] Because a guest who has walked Whiskey Row deserves the best slice in the Hold — and this is the pie the locals themselves swear by.

[tale title] The Great Apple-Bobbing Upset

[tale] Loredas dawned wet over the Hearth, so Mabel (a wood elf) moved the Halloween apple-bobbing barrel under the porch roof and declared fair rules: no hands, no antlers, no magic. Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) went first and came up grinning with an apple in each cheek, looking for all the world like a squirrel with secrets.

Then came Earl (an elk). Earl lowered his great dignified head, caught the barrel’s rim squarely between his antlers, and lifted the whole barrel clean off the porch boards, apples, water, and all. Rain and barrel-water poured down together while Earl stood blinking, wearing a barrel like a very surprised hat.

Henny (the Hearth’s chicken), judging from the barrel’s edge, gave one flat cluck — the official ruling. Mabel sighed the sigh of a wood elf who has seen this exact thing before, set the barrel back down, and awarded Earl the prize for Most Apples Moved at Once. That dang ol’ Jethro is still claiming he won on style.

[tale image caption] Earl wins Most Apples Moved at Once — Henny’s ruling stands.

[headline] Hard Rain, Bright Pumpkins, and a Halloween Eve Full of Music

[dateline] Friday, October 30, 2026

[lead] Hail, guest of the Hearth, and mind the puddles on the Fredas road — the rain comes down hard over the Rim today, the pines drip and shine, and Mogollon’s Hearth keeps a dry bench and a warm mug waiting for every traveler. PAYSON — Halloween eve brings live music to Payson tonight, with an acoustic set at 5 and the T-BoneZ at 7:30, while Sedona paints its Marigold Mural and Prescott opens a brand-new three-day gravel bike race, a spooky story night, and a murder-mystery dinner. Tomorrow the Holds turn full Halloween — trunk-or-treats in Camp Verde, Sedona, and Show Low — and on Sunday, Nov. 1, a brand-new TJ Maxx opens its doors right here in Payson. By the Nine, take an umbrella today and a costume tomorrow, and the weekend is yours.

[hero_caption] Pumpkins, riders, and lanterns in the rain — Halloween eve stands merry across the Holds.

[weather] Hard rain high 65 low 49 rain 94% sunrise 6:43 AM sunset 5:33 PM tomorrow Snow, 58/51

[weather_caption] Gandy endures the hard rain under the eaves while Maevy bats at the raindrops.

[today Payson] Jeordie — acoustic live music — today at 5 in the afternoon at Tox Bar in Payson, as listed on Bandsintown. An early-evening acoustic set opens Halloween weekend in the Hold — small room, close music, and an easy stop before supper in town. Guests who like live music without a late night will find this the gentlest start to the weekend. Check the Bandsintown Payson page before heading out, as small-venue times can shift. | The T-BoneZ — live music — tonight at 7:30 at Janey’s Coffee Co. & Bodega in Payson, as listed on Bandsintown. A second, later set of local music on the same evening, in a coffee-house room made for sitting and listening. No costume is required — this is simply a good local-music stop on Halloween eve. Confirm the time on the Bandsintown Payson page, and bring a raincoat for the walk back to the car.

[today Sedona] Marigold Mural Project — today from 11 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon at Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village, 336 State Route 179 in Sedona. Visitors paint a tribute to a loved one on a 26-foot community remembrance wall, leading into Sunday’s Día de los Muertos celebration. It is hands-on and open to all ages — your own marigold art joins the wall. The village patios and shops make it an easy half-day trip under the red rocks. | Frequency Friday — Meditation, BioCharger & Sound Bath — tonight at 5:45 at 1730 West State Route 89A in West Sedona, per the AllEvents Sedona listing. A quiet, indoor evening of meditation and sound — a calm counterpoint to costumes and crowds on a rainy Halloween eve. Good for guests who want to end the day restored rather than rattled. Check the AllEvents listing for booking details before going. | Sound Ceremony — Songs of the Forest — tonight at 7 at 251 Arizona 179, Suite B1, in Sedona, per AllEvents. An immersive listening and sound-healing evening rather than a stage concert — the forest sung back to you in a small room. It is a second, later wellness option for a Friday night in red rock country. Seating for these sessions is usually limited, so confirm booking on the AllEvents page first.

[today Prescott] Prescott — The Rough Rider opens today at Courthouse Square in Prescott, a brand-new three-day gravel bike race running Friday, Oct. 30 through Sunday, Nov. 1. Riders take on three stages of high-desert roads based in historic downtown, and the weekend stages finish right on North Cortez Street. Spectators get the best of it: fast starts, dusty finishes, and a square full of food and cheer. Come wave the riders home like bards greeting heroes — rain gear advised today. | Spooky Stories & S’mores — tonight from 5:30 to 7 at the Highlands Center for Natural History in Prescott, free with registration first, per Prescott Places. A marshmallow in one hand and a spooky story in your ear, out among the pines — a family-friendly Halloween-eve outing, not a haunted-house scare fest. Registration is required, so sign up before driving over. Dress warm and dry; it is an outdoor evening in high country, and today’s rain is no respecter of storytellers. | On The Chopping Block — murder mystery dinner — tonight at 6 at the Elks Performing Arts Center, Crystal Hall, 117 East Gurley Street in Prescott, $65 with dinner, per the listing. The Preskitt Mystery Company turns supper into a whodunit set at a cooking-show semi-final — six chefs, sharp judges, and clues served between courses. Guests meet the characters and help solve the mystery; it is immersive, not a sit-back stage play. It plays again Saturday night at 6 for those who miss tonight.

[week Sat, Oct. 31] Camp Verde Trunk or Treat takes over Main Street in Camp Verde on Saturday, Oct. 31, from 5 to 7 in the evening. Businesses, groups, and neighbors line the street with decorated cars and booths, handing out candy to crowds the town counts in the thousands. There are haunted houses, games, music, and a Haunted Jail for the brave, plus a decorating contest. Costumes are the order of the night — bring a bag with room to spare. | A Haunting at the Fort — Saturday, Oct. 31, from 6 to 8 in the evening at Fort Verde State Historic Park, 125 East Hollamon Street in Camp Verde. A lantern-lit, after-hours walk with ghost stories and a chance to visit with those who still call the fort home after 150 years, per Arizona State Parks. There is no extra cost beyond regular park admission. It sits a short walk from the Main Street candy line — trunk-or-treat first, then slip into the fort as darkness falls. | Uptown Trick or Treat in Sedona, Saturday, Oct. 31, from 5 to 8 in the evening along Uptown’s main street on State Route 89A. Shops stay open late handing out candy as costumed families wander door to door under the red rocks. Look for the “Thriller” flash-mob dance at Sinagua Plaza and the Fire Department’s Haunted Ambulance nearby. It is Sedona’s biggest Halloween gathering — joyful, glowing, and full of tiny dragons and knights. | Show Low Main Street Trunk or Treat — Saturday, Oct. 31, from 3 to 8 in the evening at Hatch Toyota, 1051 North Auto Mall Parkway in Show Low. Trunk-or-treating, music, food, a haunted house, and a Kids Zone, with a trunk-decorating contest offering cash prizes. Presented by Show Low Main Street, it is the town’s main Halloween gathering. Families from across the White Mountains make the trip for this one.

[week Sun, Nov. 1] TJ Maxx Grand Opening — Payson’s own brand-new TJ Maxx throws open its doors Sunday, Nov. 1, at 400 East State Highway 260, with opening-day hours from 8 in the morning to 8 at night. Off-price treasures are the house specialty — clothes, shoes, home goods, and gifts at prices to make a bard sing. Arrive early for the best pick of the racks; the whole Hold has waited for this one. Valley Dwellers riding up for the weekend can be first through the door. | Día de los Muertos at Tlaquepaque — Sunday, Nov. 1, from 11 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon at Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village in Sedona. A colorful celebration of life and remembrance fills the patios and fountains — traditional altars, large cultural installations, papel picado, music, and dance. It follows four days of the Marigold Mural Project, where visitors painted tributes on the community wall. All ages are welcome at one of Sedona’s most loved fall gatherings. | Sedona Community Farmers Market — Sunday, Nov. 1, from 8 to 11 in the morning at 2201 West State Route 89A in Sedona. Local growers and makers spread their tables under the red rocks — produce, baked goods, and handmade wares for a slow Sunday morning. Go early for the best pick of the bread, then ride on to Tlaquepaque for the afternoon. A fine, calm close to Halloween weekend.

[week Tue, Nov. 3] Trail Day Volunteer Build in Pine — Tuesday, Nov. 3, from 7 in the morning to noon, off Highway 87 just before Pine. Pine Strawberry Fuel Reduction calls hikers, bikers, runners, and neighbors to help clear brush, move rocks, and shape a trail the whole community will use for years. The work also opens better access for fire crews, so every hour given does double duty. Tools are provided and no experience is needed — bring water, gloves if you have them, and sturdy shoes, and sign up at trails@psfuelreduction.org. | Snakes! Lizards! Tortoises! — Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 11 in the morning at Tlaquepaque, 336 Arizona 179 in Sedona, free and open to the public, per the event listing. Sonoran Reptiles brings native and non-native lizards, snakes, and tortoises to see up close, with handlers glad to answer questions. A fine midweek stop for families and anyone curious about desert wildlife. Confirm the start time on the event page before the ride over.

[merchant name] The Hike Shack

[merchant town] Prescott

[merchant blurb] Prescott’s local outfitter just off Courthouse Plaza, stocked for everything from a Thumb Butte day hike to an extended trek — camping gear and apparel, sleeping bags, trail maps, climbing gear and harnesses, and hiking boots fitted by staff who actually hike. Their motto says it plain: it all starts with a good Base Camp — and by the Nine, a spell of true-fitting means those boots will not pinch a toe from here to Granite Mountain.

[merchant review] Great selection of quality gear, knowledgeable helpful staff and dog friendly store. We also really appreciate the fact that the prices are reasonable.

[merchant review_src] Wanderlog (Google review)

[merchant why] Real trail fuel for the feet — local trail knowledge and a proper boot fitting in one stop, right off Courthouse Plaza, before any Prescott trail.

[merchant visit] 104 North Montezuma Street, Prescott. Open Monday to Saturday 9 to 6, Sunday 10 to 6 — so open today, Friday, Oct. 30, 9 to 6. Phone 928-443-8565. Prices are moderate ($$). Good to know: the store is dog-friendly, and staff are trained for custom boot fittings — ask, and they will bring out several pairs to try.

[merchant image caption] Inside The Hike Shack, where the boots are fitted by folks who hike.

[quest] Finish and install the torches Paint, seal against the sun, wire into the door-light boxes with the breaker off, and test at dusk.

[quest caption] The shield, the torch sconces, and the doors wait their turn on the workshop bench.

[tale title] The Great Raincoat Fitting

[tale] Fredas dawned with the rain coming down hard, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) declared that no friend of the Hearth would go to the Halloween market wet — beginning with Earl (an elk).

The raincoat was a yellow tarp, cut generous, with holes argued over and cut again. Gus (an orc) held an oiled-cloth umbrella over the fitting like a royal canopy, and every time Jethro pulled the tarp straight, Earl’s great antlers poked out at a new and grander angle. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) watched from a dry crate and offered no help at all, which everyone agreed was her finest work.

At last the tarp stood fastened, the antlers wore two small sleeves of their own, and Earl stepped into the downpour with his dignity entirely dry. The rain, impressed, kept falling anyway — and Earl, pleased despite himself, wore the yellow tarp all the way to the porch and back, twice.

[tale image caption] Jethro fits, Gus shelters, Henny supervises — Earl stays dry.

[tale title] The Paper Bat Mix-Up

[tale] Turdas dawned grey and mild, so Mabel (a wood elf) set out to hang paper bats along the Hearth porch beam for Halloween — a string of them, each one cut neat and even, in a row any jarl would approve.

Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) helpfully frosted each knot so the strings would hold stiff in the breeze, and landed proud beside the crate. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) climbed into that crate, sat down square on the spare bats, and arranged herself like a queen on a paper throne.

Every bat Mabel hung, Henny counted with one solemn cluck — and every count came out one short, because the bat under Henny never got hung at all. At last Mabel sighed her professional sigh, cut one extra bat, and hung it right over Henny’s crate. Henny wears the honor like a banner, and tells the porch she is the best bat of the whole row.

[tale image caption] Mabel hangs, Flurry frosts, and Henny sits on the count.

[headline] Halloween Week Fills the Holds With Music, Markets, and Treats

[dateline] Wednesday, October 28, 2026

[lead] Hail, guest of the Hearth, and good Middas morning to you — the clouds hang low and kind over the pines, the air sits mild at 69 degrees, and Mogollon’s Hearth sends warm greetings under a grey Rim Country sky. PAYSON — It is a quiet day here in the Payson Hold itself, and a merry one abroad: a concert in Sedona tonight, baking and open-mic music in Prescott, and adoptable dogs introduced live from Camp Verde. Then Halloween takes the week by both hands — a remembrance mural and a farmers market on Thursday, a brand-new gravel bike race rolling into Prescott on Friday, and trunk-or-treats from Camp Verde to Show Low on Saturday. One sad note, told plainly: Sedona’s Día de los Muertos celebration on Sunday, Nov. 1 is canceled, by the Nine — the venue’s own page says so — though its Marigold Mural Project still opens Thursday as planned.

[hero_caption] Pumpkins, lanterns, and small knights and dragons — Halloween week opens merry across the Holds.

[weather] Overcast high 69 low 48 rain 0% sunrise 6:41 AM sunset 5:35 PM tomorrow Overcast, 70/50

[weather_caption] Gandy and Maevy lounge contentedly on the deck under the grey skies, one paw stretched out in case adventure passes.

[today Payson] Bible Study at Juanita’s — this morning at 9, at 139 Hash Knife Drive in Payson. A small, weekly, come-as-you-are study group, warm and unhurried — a quiet, friendly local morning rather than a big event. Guests who like to start a grey day in good company will feel right at home. No fuss, no fanfare — just neighbors, coffee weather, and an open door.

[today Camp Verde] “We Are Live!” — Hillside Canine adoptable dogs, live online — tonight at 6, on Hillside Canine’s Facebook page (the kennel stands at 874 North Industrial Drive in Camp Verde). The handlers introduce their adoptable dogs live — meet each dog, hear its story and its quirks, and ask questions as you watch. It is a fine fireside doing for dog lovers, and for any traveler quietly thinking a dog might join the household. No road trip needed — the pack comes to you.

[today Sedona] Sirsy Concert — tonight from 7 to 8:30 at the Mary D. Fisher Theatre, 2030 West State Route 89A in Sedona, presented by the Sedona International Film Festival. Sirsy is an award-winning duo from upstate New York — just two musicians making a sound the Boston Globe called a “little band with the big sound.” Expect catchy, soulful songs, stories, and jokes between the tunes in an intimate theatre. A splendid evening road-trip for music lovers under the red rocks.

[today Prescott] High Altitude Baking Workshop — tonight from 5 to 7 at 840 Rodeo Drive, Building C, in Prescott. Why do cakes fall flat above 3,000 feet, and how do you fix them? This hands-on class covers the fixes — time, temperature, and ingredient changes that make high-country baking behave. It costs $5 to cover materials, seats are limited to 30, and registration is required. Home bakers, this one was made for you. | Musicians with Heart Open Mic — tonight from 7 to 10 at the Jersey Lilly Saloon in Prescott. Local singers and pickers take their turns in a Whiskey Row saloon while the crowd settles in — and every donation goes to local charity. Part concert, part town gathering with better tunes. Drop in for one song or stay for the whole merry evening. | Beginning Line Dance with Beth Raber — tonight at 6 at The Center on Rosser, 1280 East Rosser Street, Suite B, in Prescott. A beginner-friendly line-dance session — easy steps, good music, and a social floor where first-timers are the honored guests. A joyful way to shake off a grey day and earn your supper. Wear shoes you can slide in, and bring your best two left feet.

[week Thu, Oct. 29] Marigold Mural Project begins at Tlaquepaque in Sedona, 336 State Route 179, running 11 to 5 each day through the weekend. Visitors paint a tribute to a loved one on a 26-foot community remembrance wall, guided by the artist Lovejoy, with brushes and paints supplied and earlier years’ murals standing nearby for heart. You need only bring a name and a memory. One note, told plainly: the venue’s Día de los Muertos celebration on Sunday is canceled — the mural project itself still opens Thursday as planned. | Windmill Park Farmers Market in Cornville, just outside Camp Verde, from 2 to 6 in the afternoon at 9950 East Cornville Road. A small-town creekside market, rain or shine — fresh produce, sourdough and baked goods, farm eggs, local honey, goat-milk soaps, jams, pickles, and handmade crafts from local makers. A fine guest outing for anyone who shops with their stomach. Come hungry and bring a bag with room to spare. | Show Low Public Library Halloween Carnival — at 3 in the afternoon at the library, 181 North 9th Street in Show Low, with a costume contest at 4. Games, activities, prizes, and treats for everyone — a family Halloween stop run by the city library itself. One honest note: the city’s own post mixes its weekday words, so a quick call to the library before you set out is a wise traveler’s move. Costumes are very much welcome.

[week Fri, Oct. 30] Prescott — The Rough Rider opens at Courthouse Square in Prescott, a brand-new three-day gravel bike race running Friday, Oct. 30 through Sunday, Nov. 1. Riders take on three stages of high-desert roads based in historic downtown — Stage 1 starts Friday at 9 in the morning at Camp Wood, and the weekend stages finish right on North Cortez Street. Spectators get the best of it: fast starts, dusty finishes, and a square full of food and cheer. Come wave the riders home like bards greeting heroes.

[week Sat, Oct. 31] Camp Verde Trunk or Treat takes over Main Street in Camp Verde from 5 to 7 in the evening. Businesses, groups, and neighbors line the street with decorated cars and booths, handing out candy to crowds the town counts in the thousands. There are haunted houses, games, music, and a Haunted Jail for the brave, plus a decorating contest. Costumes are the order of the night — bring a bag with room to spare. | Uptown Trick or Treat in Sedona, 5 to 8 in the evening along Uptown’s main street on State Route 89A. Shops stay open late handing out candy as costumed families wander door to door under the red rocks. Look for the “Thriller” flash-mob dance at Sinagua Plaza and the Fire Department’s Haunted Ambulance nearby. It is Sedona’s biggest Halloween gathering — joyful, glowing, and full of tiny dragons and knights. | Show Low Main Street Trunk or Treat — from 3 to 8 in the evening at Hatch Toyota, 1051 North Auto Mall Parkway in Show Low. Trunk-or-treating, music, food, a haunted house, and a Kids Zone, with a trunk-decorating contest offering cash prizes. Presented by Show Low Main Street, it is the town’s main Halloween gathering. Families from across the White Mountains make the trip for this one.

[week Tue, Nov. 3] Trail Day Volunteer Build in Pine — from 7 in the morning to noon, off Highway 87 just before Pine. Pine Strawberry Fuel Reduction calls hikers, bikers, runners, and neighbors to help clear brush, move rocks, and shape a trail the whole community will use for years. The work also opens better access for fire crews, so every hour given does double duty. Tools are provided and no experience is needed — bring water, gloves if you have them, and sturdy shoes, and sign up at trails@psfuelreduction.org.

[merchant name] The Copper Needle

[merchant town] Payson

[merchant blurb] A true maker’s hall on Payson’s Main Street — a BERNINA sewing and embroidery machine dealership with its own service bench, owned and run by Gina Perkes, and stocked with high-quality fabrics, threads, patterns, and notions. By a touch of loom-magic worthy of a court enchanter, the popular BERNINA Q24 seems to hum a quilt into being while you watch. Their signature stop is a quilting class — technique and project classes for every level and age — or an hour lost happily among the fabric bolts and Gina Perkes Designs ruler templates.

[merchant review] Beautiful and cute store!

[merchant review_src] Google review

[merchant why] Every mead hall needs quilts on its benches, and this is the Hold’s finest place to start one — or to find the cloth, the thread, and the teacher all under one roof.

[merchant visit] 201 Suite B West Main Street, Payson. Open Monday to Friday 10 to 4, Saturday 10 to 3, closed Sunday. Phone 928-363-4036. Prices are moderate. Good to know: it holds a 5.0-star rating from its Google reviewers — small shop, mighty welcome.

[tale title] The Great Pumpkin-Seed Count

[tale] Middas dawned grey and mild, so Mabel (a wood elf) spread a flat stone in the Hearth clearing and set about sorting pumpkin seeds for winter planting — one pile to plant, one pile to roast, one pile for the birds.

Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) helpfully breathed a frosty puff over the planting pile to keep it safe and fresh, and landed beside it in a proud zigzag. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) inspected the bird pile, found it met her standards, and began eating the count down, one seed at a time, like a clerk striking names off a list.

Every time Mabel finished counting, she had a different number, and every time, Henny looked deeply innocent. At last Mabel sighed — her professional sigh — moved the roast pile to the far side of the stone, and paid Henny three seeds up front as a counting fee. The count held steady after that. Flurry still guards the frosted pile, and tells anyone who asks that he saved the whole harvest single-winged.

[tale image caption] Mabel counts, Henny un-counts, and Flurry keeps the harvest on ice.

[dateline] Tuesday, October 27, 2026

[lead] Hail, wayfarer, and good Tirdas morning to you — the sun is up over the Rim, the pines stand bright and still, and Mogollon’s Hearth sends warm greetings on a sunny day that tops out at 68 degrees. The Payson Roundup reports it opened to crowds through its opening weekend — folks stopped in Friday, Oct. 9 and came right back Saturday, Oct. 10, rainy weather and all. The pub’s own page promises premium craft beers, superior cocktails, gourmet plates, and every screen a window to the game. Beyond the pub, Halloween week is upon us: trail work in Pine today, music in Prescott tonight, and a Saturday full of trunk-or-treats, haunted forts, and costumed fun from Camp Verde to Sedona.

[hero_caption] Pumpkins take their places on the tables as Halloween week opens across the Holds.
