[weather_caption] Gandy basks half-asleep in the sun while Maevy chases a butterfly clean across the deck.

[today Payson] Payson Public Library day — Tai Chi at 9 in the morning and Sit and Stitch from 2 to 5 in the afternoon, at the library on North McLane Road. Tai Chi is a gentle way to start a sunny Tirdas, all slow moves and deep breaths under the pines. Sit and Stitch brings the needleworkers together for an afternoon of yarn, talk, and steady progress. Call the library at 928-474-9260 to register. A fine, calm pair of doings for guests who like their days unhurried.

[today Pine-Strawberry] Trail Day Volunteer Build in Pine — today from 7 in the morning to noon, off Highway 87 just before Pine. Pine Strawberry Fuel Reduction calls hikers, bikers, runners, and neighbors to help clear brush, move rocks, and shape a trail the whole community will use for years. The work also opens better access for fire crews, so every hour given does double duty. Bring water, sunscreen, gloves if you have them, and sturdy shoes — tools are provided and no experience is needed. Email trails@psfuelreduction.org for directions and details.

[today Prescott] Open Mic hosted by Greystone — tonight from 5:30 to 8:30 in Prescott. Local singers, pickers, and poets take their turn in the spotlight while the crowd settles in with supper and something warm. Open mics are where a Hold hears itself think out loud — part concert, part town meeting with better tunes. Arrive early if you mean to perform, and stay late for the surprises. A merry way to close a sunny day on the road.

[week Wed, Oct. 28] Wednesday Music at Back Alley Wine Bar in Prescott, 5:30 to 8:30 in the evening, with Wednesday karaoke following at 7. Midweek music is a fine excuse for Valley Dwellers to linger one more night under the pines. Expect an easy crowd, local voices, and songs everybody half-knows and fully enjoys. Sing along or simply listen — both are honored customs of the mead hall.

[week Thu, Oct. 29] Marigold Mural Project begins at Tlaquepaque in Sedona, running 11 to 5 each day through the weekend on Calle Independencia. Visitors paint a tribute to a loved one on a long community remembrance wall, with murals from earlier years standing nearby for heart and inspiration. Brushes and paints are supplied, so you need only bring a name and a memory. It is one of the gentlest, kindest doings of the whole season.

[week Fri, Oct. 30] Prescott — The Rough Rider opens at Courthouse Square in Prescott, a three-day gravel bike race running Oct. 30 through Nov. 1. Riders take on three stages of high-desert roads based in historic downtown, all grit, grind, and glory. Spectators get the best of it — fast starts, dusty finishes, and a square full of food and cheer. Come wave the riders home like bards greeting heroes.

[week Sat, Oct. 31] Camp Verde Trunk or Treat takes over Main Street in Camp Verde from 5 to 7 in the evening. Businesses, groups, and neighbors line the street with decorated cars, trucks, and booths, handing out candy to a crowd the town counts in the thousands. There is a decorating contest, haunted houses, games, music, and a haunted jail for the brave. Costumes are very much the order of the night. Bring a bag with room to spare. | A Haunting at the Fort at Fort Verde State Historic Park, 6 to 8 in the evening. This lantern-lit walk lets you glimpse the old fort after hours, hear ghost stories, and visit with those who still call the fort home after 150 years. There is no extra cost beyond regular park admission. It is spooky in the friendly, storyteller way — perfect after the trunk-or-treat crowds thin. | Uptown Trick or Treat in Sedona, 5 to 8 in the evening along Uptown’s main street. Shops hand out candy as costumed families wander from door to door under the red rocks. It is Sedona’s biggest Halloween gathering and a joyful one, all glow and giggles. Come early for parking and stay for the parade of tiny dragons and knights. | Witch Way to the Spring? A Halloween Cleanup at See Spring Trail in Christopher Creek, 10:30 in the morning to 3:30 in the afternoon. The Women’s Wine Hiking Society leads a spooky-season cleanup hike to keep the trail from looking like a graveyard. Costumes are welcome, good deeds are the point, and the spring rewards the walk at the end. A fine way to earn your evening candy.

[week Sun, Nov. 1] Día de los Muertos at Tlaquepaque in Sedona, with altars, music, and cultural performances honoring loved ones who have died. The courtyards fill with marigolds, candles, and families remembering together in the open air. It follows the Marigold Mural Project’s remembrance wall, so the weekend reads as one long, kind act of memory. Guests who go will come home with full hearts.

[merchant name] White Mountain Books

[merchant town] Show Low

[merchant blurb] A great vault of pre-owned books in Show Low — thousands of used titles, vinyl records, and DVDs, plus local honey, jewelry, art, and handmade goods from mountain artisans. By a touch of shelf-magic worthy of the Arcanaeum, a Tolkien tale or a vintage prayer book seems to surface just when a traveler asks for it. Their signature treasure is the deep used-book hunt itself: come for one paperback, leave with a stack and a story.

[merchant review] Visitors praise the shop as far bigger than it looks, with a most amazing selection of books and staff who know their shelves well — the kind of place you could happily spend all day in.

[merchant review_src] Places reviews for White Mountain Books

[merchant why] Every guest hall needs a book for a quiet night by the hearth, and this is the Hold’s finest place to find one.

[merchant visit] 1150 E Deuce of Clubs, Show Low. Open Monday to Thursday 10 to 5, Friday and Saturday 10 to 6. Phone 928-532-5533. Prices are inexpensive. Good to know: give yourself time — the aisles reward slow browsing, and the shop also does fingerprinting by appointment.

[merchant image caption] Inside White Mountain Books, where the shelves run deep and the hours run short.

[tale title] The Great Pumpkin-Carving Judgment

[tale] Tirdas dawned sunny and mild, so Mabel (a wood elf) declared a pumpkin-carving contest on the Hearth clearing, and Earl (an elk) appointed himself judge before anyone could object.

Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) carved his pumpkin with a grin so wide it needed a second pumpkin to finish the smile. Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) helpfully chilled every finished face so the edges stayed crisp, though his zigzag landing knocked one entry gently into the leaf pile. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) entered herself by sitting inside a hollow pumpkin wearing the lid as a hat, and refused all judging on grounds of already winning.

Earl paced the row three times, antlers high, dignity higher. Then he sneezed at a drifting leaf, crowned every pumpkin at once with one nod, and declared a tie. Mabel sighed like it was her job — because it is — and served pie to all hands. That dang ol’ Jethro is still telling folks his pumpkin smiled first.

[tale image caption] Earl judges, Henny enters herself, and every pumpkin wins.

text:
[headline] Halloween Week Opens With Music, Pumpkins, and Grey Skies

[dateline] Monday, October 26, 2026

[lead] PAYSON — Hail, wayfarer, and good Morndas to you! Grey clouds ride over the Rim this morning, yet the Holds are merry: bards tune up in Pine tonight, the library in Payson keeps its doors wide, story time rings out in Show Low, and Sedona hangs fresh paintings still smelling of pine air. All week the road runs toward Halloween — trail work, murals, gravel racers, and a lantern-lit fort await. Draw up a chair, pour something warm, and plan your week by the Nine.

[hero_caption] A bard tunes up in a timber village square as Halloween week opens across the Holds.

[weather] Overcast high 68 low 44 rain 0% sunrise 6:40 AM sunset 5:37 PM tomorrow Overcast, 69/47

[weather_caption] Gandy dozes through the grey morning while Maevy stalks one brave leaf.

[today Payson] Payson Public Library — Tai Chi and Sit & Stitch — The library at 328 N. McLane Road opens the week in its usual kindly way, with Tai Chi in the morning and the Sit & Stitch circle later in the day. Bring a project, borrow a book, or simply sit a spell among neighbors. It is the quiet, friendly start to a busy Halloween week, and the staff are glad to point guests toward more doings about town. To register for library events, call 928-474-9260.

[today Pine-Strawberry] Open Mic Night: Music with a Purpose — THAT Brewery & Pub, Pine — Tonight from 4 o’clock at 3270 N. Highway 87, the microphones open and the whole village is the band. Rotating members of the Pine Strawberry Fuel Reduction team host the evening, and tips go to their work keeping the forest safer for everyone. Sing a song, tell a tale, or just cheer the brave — a mead-hall night in the pines, with a good cause in every cup.

[today Sedona] Sedona Plein Air Exhibition Opens — Fresh from the festival fields, the paintings made outdoors among the red rocks go on show today, running through November 22. Artists spent the festival chasing desert light, and now guests can walk the walls at leisure and see the canyons as a painter’s eye caught them. A fine, unhurried stop paired with a stroll through Sedona’s galleries and courtyards.

[today Show Low] Story Time — Show Low Public Library — Mondays at 10:00 to 10:30 in the morning, the Kids Room fills with picture books, songs, and small happy chaos. The free drop-in session is made for ages 0 to 5 and builds the first steps toward reading, one story at a time. No sign-up is needed — just bring your smallest traveler. For word, call the library at 928-532-4070.

[week Tue, Oct. 27] Trail Day Volunteer Build — Pine — From 7 in the morning to noon off Highway 87 in Pine, volunteers clear brush, move rocks, and shape a trail built to serve the Hold for years. The work also opens better access for firefighters, so every armful of brush does double duty. Tools are provided; bring water, sunscreen, gloves, and sturdy shoes. To volunteer, write to trails@psfuelreduction.org for directions.

[week Thu, Oct. 29] Halloween Spooktacular Carnival — Show Low Public Library — The library turns carnival at 3 o’clock, with games, activities, treats for everyone, and a costume contest at 4 o’clock with fun prizes. Ghosts, goblins, and one very serious small dragon or two are all welcome. It is free family fun in the heart of Show Low, and a fine warm-up for the big night itself. | Marigold Mural Project Begins — Tlaquepaque, Sedona — From today through November 1, visitors are invited to paint a tribute to a loved one on the community remembrance wall at Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village. The mural grows flower by flower all week, bright marigolds against the courtyards and sycamores. Come add a name, a color, and a memory — the village supplies the wall, you supply the heart.

[week Fri, Oct. 30] Prescott — The Rough Rider Gravel Race Begins — Three days of wild riding open today at Prescott Courthouse Square, 120 South Cortez Street, and run through Sunday, November 1. This bold new three-stage gravel race sends riders out over high-desert roads and brings them home to historic downtown each day. Not riding? The square itself is the show — cheer the starts, watch the finishes, and enjoy Prescott at its autumn best.

[week Sat, Oct. 31] A Haunting at the Fort — Fort Verde State Historic Park, Camp Verde — From 6 to 8 in the evening at 125 E. Hollamon Street, the old fort opens after hours for a ghostly lantern-lit walk. Hear the ghost stories, wander the parade ground by lantern glow, and visit with those who, the rangers say, still call the fort home after 150 years. Spooky, merry, and made for Halloween night itself. | Uptown Trick or Treat — Sedona — From 5 to 8 in the evening along Uptown Sedona, 200 N. State Route 89A, the shops open their doors to costumed travelers great and small. Bring a bag, mind the ghouls, and gather sweets beneath the red rocks as the light fades. A beloved Sedona Halloween custom, right in the heart of town. | Morning Café — Unity of Payson — Start Halloween morning gently at 9:30, in person at 110 E. Bonita Street in Payson or by Zoom from your own fireside. Morning Café is an inspirational hour of talk and good company to open the day. Costumes are not required — but by the Nine, nobody will stop you.

[week Sun, Nov. 1] Día de los Muertos — Tlaquepaque, Sedona — Sedona closes the week in remembrance and celebration, with altars, music, and cultural performances honoring loved ones who have died. The Marigold Mural, painted by visitors all week, stands at the heart of it. Go gently, go gladly — this is one of the most beautiful days of the Sedona year.

[merchant name] Persnikkity’s Cafe

[merchant town] Show Low

[merchant blurb] An eclectic cafe-bakery with a full espresso bar, fruit smoothies, baked-from-scratch sweet treats, sandwiches, wraps, bountiful salads, and stacked-up burgers — as if a kindly alchemist had enchanted a diner. The signature bite is the Famous Brown Sugar French Toast, made with thick-cut brioche; regulars also swear by the Cowboy Burger and the Banana Pecan Waffles.

[merchant review] Coffee and pastries, sandwiches for lunch, yummy sides - and TWO locations, the second featuring even more desserts. The cupcakes are beyond epic. 100% recommend!

[merchant review_src] Google review

[merchant why] Great Praise is Great! The Hearth sends guests east to Persnikkity’s when the road calls for French toast worth crossing a Hold for — Valley Dwellers trading lowland heat for White Mountain air will find it a merry stop.

[merchant visit] 161 E. Deuce of Clubs, Show Low. Open Monday–Thursday 9 AM–3 PM and Friday–Saturday 9 AM–8 PM (closed Sundays). Phone (928) 251-1965. Moderate prices. Good to know: the cupcakes and baked treats go fast — arrive before the lunch crowd if your heart is set on one.

[merchant image caption] Persnikkity’s, as the bards picture it: an alchemist’s espresso bench and a counter of wonders.

[quest] Print the torch sconces Print two torches plus the socket test piece and test-fit before finishing.

[quest] Finish & install the torches Paint, UV-seal, and wire the sockets with the breaker off.

[quest] Mount the shield by the front door Hang it on a French cleat beside the front door, facing the walkway.

[quest] Doors — Mogollon Hearth Front and side door work for the guest house.

[quest caption] The shield takes its place by the door while the torch sconces wait their turn on the bench.

[tale title] The Pumpkin Boat Parade

[tale] Morndas dawned grey over the Hearth, and Mabel (a wood elf) declared the clearing wanted a pumpkin garland before Halloween. She strung the little pumpkins stem to stem along the porch rail while Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) breathed a careful frost on every stem to keep the whole chain stiff and straight. It was, for nearly a minute, the finest garland in the Hold.

Then Henny (the Hearth’s plump chicken) found the one hollow pumpkin Mabel had set aside for a lantern. Henny climbed in, settled herself like a jarl launching a longship, and refused every order to disembark. Flurry, delighted, frosted a tiny prow. Mabel sighed her longest sigh, tied the garland’s end to the pumpkin, and led the slowest parade in Rim Country history twice around the clearing — one frosted dragon marching, one elf conducting, and Henny, unbothered and magnificent, sailing six inches above the pine needles in her pumpkin boat.

[tale image caption] Henny launches the pumpkin boat while Mabel conducts and Flurry frosts the prow.

headline: Sunshine, Markets, and Music Fill a Fine Sundas
greeting: PAYSON — Hail, wayfarer, and a bright good morning to you, under a clear sky and a kind sun over the pines! Today the Hold offers a farmers market in Sedona, a thoughtful discussion circle here in Payson, the last hours of a river retreat in Camp Verde, and live music in Prescott. The days ahead bring an open mic in Pine, a trail-building morning, and Halloween doings on Saturday, Oct. 31 — by the Nine, a merry week for every traveler on the Rim road.
text:
[headline] Sunshine, Markets, and Music Fill a Fine Sundas

[tale title] The Great Acorn Necklace Parade

[tale] Sundas dawned warm and golden, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) announced a parade. Not for any reason, mind — the acorns were falling, the sun was out, and that dang ol’ Jethro has never once let a good morning go uncelebrated.

All morning he sat in the clearing stringing fallen acorns onto twine, making necklace after necklace. Earl (an elk) received the longest one and wore it with enormous dignity, holding his head high so it would not slide down his neck. Henny (the Hearth’s plump chicken) refused a necklace outright, climbed onto the biggest pumpkin by the porch instead, and led the whole parade from up there like a queen on a very round throne.

Round the clearing they went, three times, Jethro waving at nobody, Earl stepping slow and stately, Henny clucking the beat. Mabel sighed, said it was the finest parade the Hold had seen all week, and went back to her garden. She was not wrong.

[tale image caption] Henny leads the parade from the finest seat in the Hold.

[tale title] The Great Monster Mash Costume Fitting

[tale] Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) woke under a partly cloudy Loredas sky with a grand notion: Earl (an elk) should go to tonight’s Monster Mash in costume, and Jethro would fit him himself. Out came pine boughs, a coil of twine, and a hollow pumpkin saved for just such an emergency.

Earl stood very still and very dignified while Jethro tied boughs along his back like a forest come to life. The pumpkin hat, though, would not sit straight between those enormous antlers — left, right, left again, until it settled at a jaunty angle that Jethro declared ‘terrifying, probably.’ Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) walked one slow circle as judge, pecked the twine once, and gave a single approving cluck.

Then a butterfly crossed the clearing, Earl turned his head to watch it, and the whole costume turned with him — boughs, pumpkin, and all — like a small woodland revolving door. Jethro clapped anyway. If you see a pine forest dancing at the Mash tonight, traveler, that is not a forest. That is Earl, and he would like you to know he is a monster now.

[tale image caption] Earl’s Monster Mash fitting — boughs, pumpkin, and one approving cluck.

[tale title] Gus’s Pie-Delivery Service

[tale] Gus (an orc baker) woke with a grand notion: the whole forest should have pie before breakfast, and he would deliver it himself — except his enormous hands were needed at the oven. So he promoted Earl (an elk) to delivery cart, balanced a tray of six tiny pies across Earl’s antlers, and sent him down the path at a dignified walk.

Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) rode on Earl’s back as inspector, pecking nothing, judging everything. Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) took the airmail route with one pie in a cloth sling, zigzagging as his kinked tail demands, and set it down — gently, miraculously — right in the middle of Mabel’s (a wood elf’s) herb garden, on the one flat stone.

Earl delivered five pies without a crumb lost, which Mabel called the most respectable thing to happen all Frostfall. The sixth pie is still unaccounted for. Henny has crumbs on her beak and no comment.

[tale image caption] Gus’s Pie-Delivery Service — five pies delivered, one under investigation.

[hero_caption] Painters at their easels in the red rocks and a disc sailing over Rumsey Park — all under a stormy Rim sky.

[weather_caption] Gandy endures the rain under the eaves while Maevy bats at the raindrops.

[today Payson] Rumsey Park Battle — Disc Golf League, 4:15 to 6:30 p.m. at the Rumsey Park Disc Golf Course in Payson. This evening league round is listed on UDisc as a singles round in the general division, run by league director David, and it throws the park’s course in the cool of the late afternoon under the pines. It is a good, low-key way for guests to get outdoors and meet local players, with a friendly league feel rather than a big tournament show. Bring discs if you have them, check the UDisc listing for check-in details, and watch the stormy sky before you set out.

[today Camp Verde] Camp Carpe Diem Verde Valley 2026 — Opening Day, starting 10:00 a.m. today and running October 22–25 at Verde River RV Resort & Cottages, 1472 West Horseshoe Bend Drive, Camp Verde. This hosted RV-and-camping weekend uses Camp Verde as its base for exploring the whole Verde Valley, with hiking, biking, breweries, wineries, and ghost towns by day and campfire gatherings by night. It is a social, ticketed gathering rather than a drop-in town fair, so guests already in the valley with an RV will get the most from it. Expect a ready-made company of fellow travelers and a planned menu of outings. | Windmill Park Farmers Market, 2:00 p.m. in Windmill Park, 9950 E. Cornville Rd., Cornville, the wine-country village between Camp Verde and Sedona. Local growers and makers set up in the park for the afternoon, and the market pairs naturally with a Page Springs and Cornville tasting-room run. It is good for guests who want a short, scenic drive and something local to bring back for supper. Check the Facebook listing before going, as no end time was shown, and mind the storms on the road.

[today Sedona] Sedona Plein Air Festival — Lights On Afterschool Paint-Out, 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. at West Sedona Elementary in Sedona, free. Part of the 22nd Sedona Plein Air Festival, running October 16–24, this paint-out puts festival artists to work outdoors in the afternoon light — plein air means painting outside, on the spot, so visitors watch a red-rock scene become a canvas in real time. It is a relaxed, family-friendly stop where you can wander, watch, and talk with painters between brushstrokes. No ticket was mentioned for this session in the listing checked. | Sedona Plein Air Festival — Festival Week, all week through October 24 at the Sedona Arts Center, 15 Art Barn Road, Sedona. Now in its 22nd year, the festival brings about 26 invited artists to paint Sedona’s landscape outdoors, and visitors can watch master painters work, attend demonstrations, and see fresh paintings of views they stood in that same morning. It is one of Sedona’s signature fall weeks and an easy wander for Hearth guests. The week builds to Awards Night on Friday and a final sale on Saturday — check the Arts Center for the day’s demonstration schedule before driving over.

[today Show Low] Book vs Movie — Northland Pioneer College, today at the NPC Show Low Learning Center Library, 1001 W. Deuce of Clubs, Show Low; the college calendar lists the program as free and open to everyone, with no start time printed, so check the calendar before you go. The format compares a story on the page with its screen version — a bookish, conversational session rather than a lecture. It suits readers and film fans looking for a quiet stop in Show Low on a stormy day. Bring your own favorite example and join the argument, kindly kept.

[today Prescott] Gabriel Iglesias: The 1976 Tour, 8:00 p.m. at the Findlay Toyota Center in Prescott Valley, just east of Prescott. Stand-up star Gabriel “Fluffy” Iglesias brings his tour to the arena for one night only, with the storytelling, voices, and sound effects he is famous for rather than bite. This is the biggest single ticket in the Prescott area tonight by a wide margin, and arena crowds are expected. Buy through Ticketmaster ahead rather than hoping at the door, and check the ticket page for doors and entry details. | Pickleball Challenge Play at Pioneer Park, 8:00 a.m. at the Pioneer Park Pickleball Complex, 1200 Commerce Dr., Prescott; no end time was stated in the listing. This is morning challenge play — structured, competitive games rather than a first-timers’ clinic — at one of the local homes of the paddle sport half of Rim Country seems to play now. It is best for guests who already play and travel with a paddle. Arrive early, for Prescott mornings in late October are crisp and the courts fill with regulars — and watch the weather before heading out.

[week Fri, Oct. 23] Payson — Noley’s Kids Club, 1:00 to 2:30 p.m. at Noley’s, 103 E. State Highway 260, Payson. Michelle Guerrero reads her book The Christmas Witch — a little Christmas in October — and there will be crafts, free books, and a giveaway, thanks to sponsor Time Out, Inc. A sweet, easy afternoon for young guests and their grown-ups, right in the heart of town. Expect a small, friendly bookstore-style gathering, not a big production. | Sedona — Plein Air Festival Awards Night, 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. at the Sedona Arts Center, 15 Art Barn Road, Sedona, with free admission per the festival guide. After a week of artists painting the red rocks outdoors, the festival gathers for its awards reception, with light refreshments and the week’s work fresh off the easel. It is the best night to see the strongest paintings in one room, meet the painters, and hear which canvases the judges chose. Paintings are for sale, so collectors get first pick — arrive at the start, for this is the festival’s most social evening. | Show Low — Paint & Sip: Three Ghosts, 6:00 p.m. at Kittle’s Fine Art, 100 N. White Mountain Rd., Suite 101, Show Low. A guided evening painting session with a Halloween theme — three ghosts, painted step by step, in a working art studio. It is made for beginners and merry dabblers alike, and you take your canvas home at the end of the night. Register through the studio’s Upcoming Classes page at Kittlesfineart.com, per the listing. A fine, cozy way to spend a fall Friday evening in the White Mountains.

[week Sat, Oct. 24] Payson — Monster Mash, 4:00 to 9:30 p.m. in Payson. Payson’s big family Halloween evening starts earlier this year so families have more room to come and go across the night, with costumes, crowds, and a fall evening in the park. Bring chairs and blankets for the outdoor Halloween movie, The Nightmare Before Christmas, and enjoy the fun as Valley Dwellers trade the lowland heat for Rim Country air. Expect a long, festive evening rather than a quick trick-or-treat stop. Check Adventure Payson for the venue details before you go. | Sedona — Fall Arts & Crafts Show, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. at the Sedona Heritage Museum, 735 Jordan Road, Sedona. The museum’s annual fall fair is timed for early holiday shopping, with handmade jewelry, ceramics, fine art, home décor, cards, woodcarvings, glass, candles, and lotions from local and regional makers. Many of these artisans do only this show or a handful of others, so the goods are genuinely hard to find elsewhere. The museum grounds in Jordan Historical Park make it a pleasant browse, not a mall run. | Prescott — Prescott Regional Airport AirFest, starting 11:00 a.m. at Prescott Regional Airport, Prescott, and free per the City page. The airport’s second annual AirFest is a family-friendly celebration of aviation, with aircraft and military displays, food trucks, and a Prescott Fire Department Touch-a-Truck so kids can climb on real fire equipment. It is an open-air, wander-at-your-own-pace day rather than a seated airshow. A good all-ages outing and an easy drive for guests already headed to Prescott.

[tale title] Earl’s Rainy-Day Walk

[tale] Earl (an elk) takes his daily walk at the same hour every day, storm or shine, and a little thing like a Turdas downpour was not going to move him. So when the rain came hammering down, Earl stepped out with his chin high and his antlers proud, exactly as planned.

Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) could not stand the sight. He tore a pine bough the size of a barn door off the windfall pile and trotted along beside Earl, holding it over them both like a walking roof. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken), who had no intention of getting wet either, fluttered up and rode dry between Earl’s antlers, looking very pleased with her arrangements.

Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) tried to help by chilling the raindrops over Earl’s head, and succeeded only in giving him a hat of small, tinkling hail. Earl endured the whole parade — the bough, the chicken, the hail hat — with perfect dignity, finished his walk at the usual fence post, and shook himself like a great wet dog all over Jethro. Mabel (a wood elf) watched from the porch and said it was the finest roof she had ever seen walk.

[tale image caption] Earl’s Rainy-Day Walk — the finest roof Mabel ever saw walk.

[tale title] The Puddle Mirror Fair

[tale] The storms rolled over the Rim all Middas morning, and by noon the Hearth clearing was a shining quilt of rain puddles. Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) had an idea, as Flurry does: one careful, frosty breath across each puddle, and every puddle turned into a perfect little mirror.

Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) found hers first and admired herself for a full minute, turning this way and that like a queen at court. Earl (an elk) bent to inspect his reflection with great dignity, and a raindrop off his antler cracked his mirror into a hundred Earls, which he declared an improvement.

Then Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) tried to step daintily from mirror to mirror, as Mabel (a wood elf) had warned him not to. He landed sitting down in the one puddle Flurry had missed, soaked to the shag, grinning like the sun. Mabel sighed, handed him a towel, and declared the Puddle Mirror Fair open — admission one dry sock, which nobody in the clearing could pay.

[tale image caption] The Puddle Mirror Fair — admission one dry sock, and nobody could pay.

[headline] Volleyballs, Paint Brushes, and a Trail to Build

[dateline] Tuesday, October 20, 2026

[lead] Hail, wayfarer, and good Tirdas morning from under the Rim — the pines are cool, the sky is partly cloudy over Payson, and the Holds are busy in the best way. In Payson the Longhorn girls take on Blue Ridge at volleyball tonight, in Pine-Strawberry neighbors gather this morning to build trail, and in Sedona painters are out catching red-rock light for the Plein Air Festival. Later this week comes the Monster Mash at Green Valley Park, awards night in Sedona, and an open mic in Pine, so fill your mug, mind the late storms tomorrow, and plan a fine week.

[hero_caption] Volleyball in Payson, painters in Sedona, and trail builders in Pine — one busy morning across the Holds.

[weather] Partly Cloudy high 71 low 57 rain 20% sunrise 6:35 AM sunset 5:44 PM tomorrow Scattered thunderstorms, 69/57

[weather_caption] Gandy naps through the clouds while Maevy bats at a falling leaf.

[today Payson] Varsity Volleyball — Blue Ridge vs. Payson, 6:30 p.m. at Payson High School, 301 S. McLane Rd. The Longhorn girls host Blue Ridge in an evening match that should draw a good home crowd. Come cheer loud, support the home side, and enjoy a classic small-town night in the gym. It is a fine, easy outing for guests who want a taste of real Payson life.

[today Pine-Strawberry] Trail Day Volunteer Build in Pine, 7:00 a.m. to noon off Highway 87 just before Pine. Volunteers help clear brush, move rocks, and shape a trail that will serve hikers, bikers, and runners for years, and that also helps fire crews reach the forest when needed. Tools are provided, no experience is needed, and you should bring water, sunscreen, gloves if you have them, and sturdy shoes.

[today Sedona] Sedona Plein Air Festival — Artist Demonstration, 1:00 to 3:00 p.m. at the Sedona Arts Center. The festival runs October 16–24, with master painters working outdoors all week to catch the red rocks in real light. Today’s free demonstration is a chance to watch a painting come together, ask how the artist chooses a scene, and then wander the gallery to see work made this week.

[week Wed, Oct. 21] Show Low — Trick or Treat Trail. The City of Show Low’s live feed lists the Trick or Treat Trail for Wednesday, October 21. It is a family Halloween outing on the trail, made for costumes, candy, and an easy evening walk. Check the city’s page before you go for the latest start details, and bring a bag for treats and a light for the walk back.

[week Thu, Oct. 22] Monthly Meeting in Payson, 6:00 to 7:00 p.m. at the American Legion, 709 E. Hwy. 260, Payson. Listed as a monthly meeting to discuss runs and events, this is a neighborly evening stop for folks who follow local rides and gatherings. Arrive a little early if you want to meet people before the meeting starts.

[week Fri, Oct. 23] Sedona Plein Air Festival — Awards Night, 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. at the Sedona Arts Center, 15 Art Barn Road. After a week of painting the red rocks outdoors, the festival artists gather for awards and a reception. It is the best night to see the week’s strongest work in one room, meet painters, and hear which canvases the judges chose. The festival closes the next day. | Truckload Meat Sale in Payson, 10:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. in the Tractor Supply parking lot, 510 SR-260, Payson. The listing advertises 20 ribeyes for $50, family packs of beef, chicken, seafood, and pork, and discounts for first responders, military, and seniors on some items. It runs again Saturday, October 24, 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., while stock lasts.

[week Sat, Oct. 24] Monster Mash in Payson, 4:00 to 9:30 p.m. at Green Valley Park. Payson’s big Halloween evening returns earlier this year so families have more time to come and go. Bring chairs and blankets for the Halloween movie, The Nightmare Before Christmas, and enjoy costumes, crowds, and a fall night in the park with Valley Dwellers up for the cool Rim air. | Fall Arts & Crafts Show in Sedona, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. at the Sedona Heritage Museum. The annual show brings makers and crafts back to the museum grounds for a day of browsing. Pair it with the Plein Air Festival’s closing community paint-out and final art sale, 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Sedona Arts Center, for a full art day among the red rocks. | Costumes for Kids 5K & Halloween Fest in Prescott, from 9:00 a.m. at Prescott Courthouse Square downtown. A costume-friendly run and Halloween festival in the heart of Prescott, made for families who like their fall fun active. Come in costume, cheer the runners, and spend the rest of the morning around the square’s shops and cafes.

[week Mon, Oct. 26] Open Mic Night at THAT Brewery & Pub in Pine, 4:00 to 7:00 p.m., 3270 AZ-87, Pine. Singers, poets, storytellers, and first-timers are all welcome, hosted by rotating members of the Fuel Reduction Team, with tips benefiting Fuel Reduction. Share a song, bring a guitar, or just cheer on your neighbors with a pint in the pines.

[merchant name] The Hike House

[merchant town] Sedona

[merchant blurb] Sedona’s premier hiking shop is part gear store, part trail guide, and part refueling stop — a little enchantment in the Trail Finder lets you match over 100 Sedona trails to your legs and your time, as if by a friendly spell. Shop sturdy footwear, hiking and athletic apparel, maps and Sedona’s well-loved hiking book, then grab a smoothie, cookie, or coffee at the Energy Cafe before you head out. The signature thing to try is the Trail Finder help itself: tell them what you hope to see, and let the staff point you to the right red-rock trail.

[merchant review] We had a great experience here, Ian helped us out and he is very knowledgeable. He even took the time to answer questions about hike trails and showed us in a map. The store was stocked with a variety of things, worth stopping by.

[merchant review_src] Google review via Wanderlog

[merchant why] Because a good trail, well chosen, is half the Sedona visit — and these folks send you out fitted, fed, and pointed the right way, every time. Great praise is great, and this shop has earned it!

[merchant visit] 431 AZ-179 Ste B1, Sedona, AZ 86336. Hours: Mon.–Sat. 9 a.m.–6 p.m., Sun. 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Phone: (928) 282-5820. Price range: moderate. Good to know: go before your hike, not after — the trail advice is the real treasure, and weekends can be busy.

[merchant image caption] The Hike House in Sedona — boots, maps, and wise trail counsel before the red rocks.

[quest] Build the Mogollon’s Hearth shield Overdue — was due Oct. 17. Finalize the size, cut and engrave the layered plywood, mount the 3D-printed troll relief, and finish with spar urethane.

[quest] Mount the shield by the front door Due Oct. 24. Hang it on a French cleat beside the front door, placed for best sight from the walkway.

[quest] Finish & install the torches Overdue — was due Oct. 10. Paint, seal for sun, wire the sockets with the breaker off, mount both torches, and test at dusk.

[quest] Print the torch sconces Overdue — was due Oct. 3. Print two torches plus the socket test piece and test-fit the bulb and socket.

[quest] Design & prep the torch sconces Overdue — was due Sept. 26. Measure the bulb and socket, scale the sconce model, check the door-light wiring, and slice in PETG.

[quest] Doors — Mogollon Hearth Due Oct. 24. The front and side door work for the guest house.

[due soon] Due Saturday, Oct. 24: mount the shield by the front door, and the doors quest comes due the same day — the workshop will be busy, by the Nine!

[quest caption] The shield, the torches, and the doors — the Hearth’s workshop quests await.

[tale title] The Great Acorn Tower

[tale] That dang ol’ Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) woke up under a partly cloudy sky with a grand plan: he would stack acorns into a tower tall enough, he said, to wave at the Rim.

Earl (an elk) agreed to judge, which mostly meant standing very still and looking dignified while acorns rolled off his hooves. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) supervised from a stump, unbothered, as always. Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) tried to help by chilling the bottom acorns together, which worked beautifully until the sun warmed them and the whole tower sighed down in one soft clatter.

Jethro did not mind. He built it again, shorter and wider, and crowned it with one perfect acorn. Earl nodded once, very seriously, and the acorn fell off. Everyone agreed it was the finest tower the clearing had ever seen, for the full nine seconds it stood.

[tale image caption] Jethro’s acorn tower — finest in the Hold, for nine whole seconds.

text:
[headline] Painters Take the Valley While the Holds Keep a Merry Morndas

[dateline] Monday, October 19, 2026

[lead] Hail, wayfarer, and good Morndas morning — the Rim wakes under soft travelling clouds, bound for 68 degrees after a 52-degree dawn, with the pines standing tall and the roads dry for wandering. The art holds the day: painters gather at D.A. Ranch in Cornville for the Sedona Plein Air Festival’s golden-hour Paint Out, Prescott opens its own Plein Air Festival, and Camp Verde spreads its farmers market on Hollamon Street. By the Nine, friend of the Hearth, take a light cloak and go watch the valley turn into pictures.

[hero_caption] Painters at their easels in the Verde Valley, turning red rocks and ranch light into pictures.

[weather] Partly Cloudy high 68 low 52 rain 20% sunrise 6:34 AM sunset 5:45 PM tomorrow Partly Cloudy, 71/57

[weather_caption] Gandy dozes on the deck while Maevy watches the clouds go by.

[today Camp Verde] Verde Valley Farmers Market — 9 AM–1 PM, 75 E Hollamon St, Camp Verde. The valley’s Monday market fills the street with farm produce, baked goods, and handmade wares from local growers and makers. It is a friendly, walkable browse — the sort of morning where you arrive for tomatoes and leave with honey, bread, and a neighbor’s whole life story. Stock the Hearth kitchen, chat with the farmers, and enjoy small-town Camp Verde at its merriest.

[today Sedona] D.A. Ranch Paint Out — Sedona Plein Air Festival — 4–7 PM, D.A. Ranch, Cornville; $45 per guest, limited tickets. Festival artists paint across the ranch grounds from 4–6 PM, among the historic red barn, pastures, ponds, orchards, and vineyards, while you wander and watch the canvases grow. Awards and an exclusive sale of the works created that very afternoon follow at 6:30 PM. D.A. Ranch wines are for sale, with a grazing table and live music besides. Golden-hour art, wine, and music in the Verde Valley — a painter’s quest with refreshments.

[today Prescott] Prescott Plein Air Art Festival — opening day — today through Saturday, Oct. 24, at venues and outdoor painting spots around Prescott. Artists set up their easels across the old capital all week, painting its courthouse square, pines, and granite country in the open air while passersby watch the work take shape. It is a wandering sort of festival: stroll, find an artist, and see Prescott turned into pictures one canvas at a time. A fine excuse for a day trip over the hills, Valley Dwellers included.

[week Tue, Oct. 20] Trail Day Volunteer Build — 7 AM–noon, on Hwy 87 just before Pine, with PINE Strawberry Fuel Reduction. “Don’t just use the trail — help build it”: volunteers clear brush, move rocks, break roots, and shape a trail the community will use for years, and the work also creates better access routes for firefighters and emergency crews. Tools are provided; bring water, sunscreen, gloves if you have them, and sturdy shoes. Email trails@psfuelreduction.org for directions. | Sedona Plein Air Festival — artist demonstration — 1–3 PM, free, Sedona Arts Center, 15 Art Barn Rd, Sedona. A festival artist demonstrates the plein air craft live, turning red-rock light into a finished canvas in two hours while you watch. The festival runs through Saturday, Oct. 24, with 26 artists painting across Sedona and the Verde Valley. This free demonstration is the easiest way in — no ticket, just curiosity. Arrive a little early for a good spot.

[week Wed, Oct. 21] Paint Out at a Private Sedona Residence — 4–7 PM, private Sedona residence, address with ticket; $60 per guest, limited tickets. The Plein Air Festival’s most intimate evening: a small audience watches artists paint from 4–6 PM amid sweeping red-rock views. Awards and an exclusive sale of the afternoon’s works begin at 6:30 PM. Wine, beer, and Southwest BBQ are served as the sun sets. Part art show, part garden party, part treasure hunt. | Long-Term Water Management Plan Community Meeting — 1–3 PM, Prescott Public Library, 215 E Goodwin St, Prescott. City staff open with a presentation on Prescott’s water supplies, current and future needs, and strategies for conservation and efficiency. Information stations follow, where residents can talk one-to-one with City representatives and take a community survey. Can’t attend? The survey is online, and your input still feeds the plan’s first draft. Dry-country homework that truly matters.

[week Thu, Oct. 22] Camp Carpe Diem Verde Valley 2026 opens — Oct. 22–25, basecamp at Verde River RV Resort & Cottages, Camp Verde; ticketed. A grown-up camp and “UnRally” for RVers, van-lifers, tent campers, and travellers: four days exploring the valley’s hiking, biking, breweries, wineries, and ghost towns. The organisers handle the details; campers pick how much or how little to do, with community dinners along the way. This year’s edition lands at peak fall colour. Come for the adventure; stay for the company.

[week Fri, Oct. 23] Paint & Sip “Three Ghosts” — 6 PM, 100 N White Mountain Rd, Ste 101, Show Low. A Halloween-week paint night: settle in with a brush and a sip to create “Three Ghosts,” a seasonal canvas to take home. The listing points painters to Kittles Fine Art for full information and registration under “Upcoming Classes.” A relaxed Fredas-evening way to start the last weekend before Halloween. The ghosts, we are assured, are friendly ones.

[week Sat, Oct. 24] Morning Café — Unity of Payson — 9:30 AM–12:30 PM, 110 E Bonita, Payson, and on Zoom every Saturday. A gentle, coffee-hour start to Loredas: good company and an uplifting talk to open the day. It runs every Saturday, so guests can join from the Hearth by Zoom without driving anywhere. Check unityofpayson.org for the blue Zoom link. | Sedona Plein Air Festival — closing day — 10 AM–2 PM, Sedona. The festival’s last day brings artist pumpkin painting, a community paint-out with a $15 registration — your own brushes welcome — and a final sale of the week’s fresh paintings. Nine days of red-rock canvases come down to one morning: watch, paint, or carry a piece of Sedona home. A fine Loredas finale for art lovers, Valley Dwellers included.

[merchant name] Noley’s Books, Art & Whatnot

[merchant town] Payson

[merchant blurb] A bookshop, art gallery, and coffee bar all in one cozy room on Highway 260 — shelves of books, walls of local art, locally made goods and gifts, and a counter serving good coffee, baked goods, and fresh bites. Guests can browse, play a game of chess, take tea or a pastry, and lose a happy hour among the whatnot. Some small kindly enchantment — call it the Whatnot Charm — keeps the coffee hot, the shelves curious, and every visit a little longer than planned.

[merchant review] Hands down the best coffee and coolest spot in Payson. Love the atmosphere and friendly baristas.

[merchant review_src] Google review

[merchant why] Books, local art, and the best coffee in the Hold in one warm room — the Hearth’s favorite refuge for guests who love to browse.

[merchant visit] 103 E Highway 260, Payson, AZ 85541 · Closed Mon; Tue–Thu 6:30 AM–5 PM; Fri 6:30 AM–7 PM; Sat 8 AM–5 PM; Sun 10 AM–4 PM · (928) 478-8998 · $ (inexpensive) · Good to know: closed on Mondays, so plan for Tuesday through Sunday — and leave time to browse, because nobody leaves in five minutes.

[merchant image caption] Books, art, coffee, and whatnot — all under one cozy roof.

[quest] Design & prep the torch sconces Overdue since Sept. 26 — draw the sconces and ready them before a single torch can burn.

[quest] Print the torch sconces Overdue since Oct. 3 — the printers stand ready; give them their orders.

[quest] Finish & install the torches Overdue since Oct. 10 — hang the finished torches and light the way.

[quest] Build the Mogollon’s Hearth shield Overdue since Oct. 17 — the Hearth’s arms take shape at last.

[quest] Mount the shield by the front door Due Oct. 24 — hang it on a French cleat where every guest can see it.

[quest] Doors — Mogollon Hearth Due Oct. 24 — the Hearth’s doors are next on the quest board.

[due soon] The shield build is overdue since Saturday, Oct. 17 — and the torches still wait, wanting their sconces printed and hung.

[quest caption] The Hearth shield on the workbench, with the torch sconces lined up beside it.

[tale title] The Morning Jethro Jarred the Fog

[tale] Morndas dawned grey and drippy, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) announced that the low cloud over the Hearth was far too good to waste. He fetched a row of Mabel’s canning jars and set about catching the fog to water her garden later, one jar at a time, waving each lid like a butterfly net.

Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) helped the only way he knows how, breathing a careful little ice-mist over each jar so the fog would stay put. It worked beautifully. The rims frosted, the fog settled, and Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) supervised from the deck rail like a harbor master counting cargo.

Then Henny knocked the fullest jar off the rail. It did not break — it sighed. One small, perfect cloud rolled across the deck, and Earl (an elk) stepped into it up to his knees and stood there, very dignified, wearing the weather. Mabel (a wood elf) sighed her longest sigh, poured the other jars over her sage, and declared the garden officially watered by cloud. Jethro calls it a success. By the Nine, so does the sage.

[tale image caption] One jar down — and Earl wears the weather with dignity.

[today Payson] Sunday Brunch with Guest Chef Bee — 10 AM–2 PM, Bruzzi Vineyard, 47209 N Highway 288, Young, down the scenic road southeast of Payson; $34.99 per person plus tax and gratuity. A vineyard brunch in full autumn dress — call 928-462-3314 or write BruzziVineyard@aol.com for reservations.

A slow Sunday browse under the red rocks. | Tee Up for Tails — Verde Valley Humane Society Golf Outing — registration 7:30 AM, 9 AM shotgun start, scramble format, at Sedona Golf Resort, 35 Ridge Trail Dr, Sedona; $160 per golfer including 18 holes, a cart, lunch, balls, and tees. This fourth annual outing raises funds for shelter animals, with raffles, closest-to-the-pin and longest-drive prizes, and a $25,000 hole-in-one prize waiting on one lucky swing. Golfers of any level may sign up alone or in pairs and be teamed in fours.

Filmmakers and movie lovers have filled the theatre since Thursday with film blocks and workshops on screenwriting, music in film, and pitching. Come catch the last pictures before the credits roll on this year.

The parade steps off first, the costume competition follows, and winners are named from about 3 PM. All ages welcome, and the spectacle alone is worth the drive — bring the family and cheer the finery. | Prescott Valley Community Market — 11 AM–3 PM, Prescott Valley. A family-friendly Sunday market built to support local artisans, small businesses, and food creators, with handmade goods and good things to eat spread across the stalls. It pairs neatly with the Catrina Parade nearby in the afternoon — browse the market late morning, take lunch from a vendor, then wander over for the parade at two. A full, easy Sundas outing in one town. | CrafTea Time: Ghost Garland — 2–3 PM, Prescott Public Library, Prescott. [tale title] The Pancake That Would Not Land

[tale] Sundas dawned drizzly, and Gus (an orc baker) marked it the only proper way: one enormous pumpkin pancake on the Hearth deck, wide as a cartwheel, flipped high enough to need a witness. Mabel (a wood elf) appointed herself witness, mostly to say she had warned him.

The flip was perfect. The landing was not. A gust off the Rim took the pancake sideways, and Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) zigzagged after it with a tray, tail kink and all, while Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) ran the deck below like a one-bird ground crew.

That dang pancake sailed clean over the tray, over Henny, and settled — soft as you please — square on Earl’s antlers, where it sat like a grand golden beret. Earl (an elk) stood very still, wearing his breakfast with complete dignity, and declared it the finest hat in the Hold. Gus agreed, and served the next one on a plate, like a coward.

[tale image caption] The great flip — one pancake, one gust, one very dignified hat.

[headline] Pumpkins, Painters, and Great Drums Fill a Showery Loredas

[dateline] Saturday, October 17, 2026

[lead] Hail, wayfarer, and good Loredas morning — the Rim wakes cool at 50 degrees, the pines stand grey-green under a sky bound for 63 with showers promised by afternoon, so take the morning while it is dry. Sedona throws its Fest of Fall at noon with pumpkins splashing in the pool beside it, painters spread their easels for the Plein Air Festival, great taiko drums sound in Prescott, and a caravan of fine cars climbs the Beeline to breakfast in Payson. By the Nine, friend of the Hearth, it is a day to wander early and find a warm hall when the rain comes.

[hero_caption] Painters, drummers, and pumpkin stalls — Loredas lays out its best before the afternoon showers.

[weather] PM showers high 63 low 50 rain 40% sunrise 6:32 AM sunset 5:48 PM tomorrow AM showers, 63/50

[weather_caption] Gandy keeps dry under the eaves while Maevy bats at the afternoon raindrops.

[today Payson] Payson Drive ’n Dine to Crosswinds Restaurant — cars leave Mesa at 9 AM and reach Payson before 10:30 AM for breakfast and lunch at Crosswinds, by Payson Airport. The Audi Club of Arizona’s mountain run up the Beeline ends where model planes hang from the ceiling and real ones sit outside the windows. The listing invites non-members to take a test drive with the club, and non-Audi cars are welcome too. Watch for the caravan rolling into town mid-morning. | Morning Café — Unity of Payson — 9:30 AM–12:30 PM, 110 E Bonita, Payson, and on Zoom every Saturday. A gentle, coffee-hour start to Loredas: good company and an uplifting talk to open the day. It runs every Saturday, so guests can join from the Hearth by Zoom without driving anywhere. Check unityofpayson.org for the blue Zoom link.

[today Camp Verde] Beaver Creek School Reunion — from 9 AM, Beaver Creek School, Beaver Creek School Rd, Rimrock, just south of Camp Verde. A full day of reconnecting and reminiscing for the school’s friends and faculty, with a Flag Assembly at 10 AM, an assembly at 11 AM, lunch at noon, and activities into the afternoon. A true small-school homecoming — old classmates, old teachers, and stories from the Beaver Creek valley. The listing asks folks to register ahead of time. | The Blue Canyon Band Residency — 8 PM–midnight, Cliff Castle Casino and Hotel, Camp Verde. Two nights of live band music close out the week, and tonight is the second show of the band’s weekend residency. Expect a party crowd, dancing energy, and casino-hall entertainment right off I-17. A good after-dinner option once the sun drops behind the red rocks. Guests in the Verde Valley can make an easy night of it. | Saturday Starlight Train — Verde Canyon Railroad — 3:30 PM departure, 300 N Broadway, Clarkdale, about 25 minutes from Camp Verde. The popular Starlight run rides four hours through Verde Canyon — daylight first, then sunset colour on the cliff walls, then twilight and starlight under wide skies. Romantic, unhurried, and one of the Verde Valley’s signature evenings. These Saturday trips run on select Saturdays through Nov. 21.

[today Sedona] Fest of Fall — 12–6 PM, Posse Grounds Park, 525 Posse Ground Rd, Sedona. The City of Sedona’s big fall party packs food trucks, craft and community vendors, a Kids’ Zone, a Gaming Center, and a Ride Jam at the skate park into one afternoon, with pickleball and cornhole tournaments and live music all day. It aims to be low- or zero-waste — bring a reusable water bottle for a raffle entry. A free shuttle runs from the West SR 89A Park & Ride. | The Great Pumpkin Splash — 11 AM–1 PM, free, Sedona Community Pool, 570 Posse Ground Rd, Sedona. Halloween starts in a swimming pool: families jump in to pick their very own floating pumpkin from the water. After the splash, kids decorate their pumpkin at a no-mess sticker station and take home a goodie bag. Registration secures a pumpkin and a raffle ticket. It ends just as Fest of Fall opens next door, so families can stay all afternoon. | Sedona Plein Air Festival — artist demonstrations today — festival runs Oct. 16–24, based at Sedona Arts Center, 15 Art Barn Rd, Sedona; free demo today 10 AM–noon at the Outbound Sedona Hotel, and painter Liam Matthew Dye demonstrates 11 AM–3 PM at Mountain Trails Gallery, Tlaquepaque. Twenty-six artists from across the country paint the red rocks outdoors and in real time for nine days. Watch a canvas catch the very light you are standing in. A perfect pairing with Fest of Fall for an art-filled Loredas.

[today Show Low] Third Annual Autumn Bazaar — 9 AM–2 PM, White Mountain United Methodist Church, 261 N 5th St, Show Low. A proper fall bazaar: handmade crafts from local artisans, a bake sale of sweet treats, and special activities for the kids. Spend a crisp autumn morning browsing while supporting local vendors. All proceeds support the church’s projects, including its food pantry and the Thanksgiving Turkey Dinner Drive. Family-friendly and community-run — a Show Low Loredas tradition in the making. | Show Low Film Festival — today is a full festival day, WME Village 8, 1501 W White Mountain Blvd, Pinetop-Lakeside; day pass $75, block tickets $15. Independent filmmakers and movie lovers gather in the White Mountains for this eight-years-running festival, with about 100 selected projects. Today’s programme adds workshops on screenwriting, music in film, and learning to pitch, alongside film blocks through the day. Sunday closes with a free showcase block.

[today Prescott] Taiko Drumming Workshop and Taiko Extravaganza — workshops 9 AM–1 PM and evening show 7 PM, Elks Performing Arts Center, 117 E Gurley St, Prescott. World-class taiko artist Ken Koshio leads a beginner-friendly, hands-on workshop in ancient Japanese drumming — all drums provided, no experience needed. The day crescendos with the evening Taiko Extravaganza, fusing Japanese drumming and world music with World Hoop Dance Champion Derrick Suwaima Davis. Taiko is heard with the whole body — feel it in your chest. | OktoberMarket with Holly Ridge — 12–8 PM, The Grand Highland Hotel, 154 S Montezuma St, Prescott. Prescott’s fall market season kicks off inside the hotel ballroom and out in its courtyard, with artisan vendors offering organic skincare, baked goods, jewellery, apparel, woodwork, and soaps. There are pumpkins and spooky treats for kids and kids at heart. Come for coffee, stay for lunch, or wander in after dinner — this year they are testing longer hours. | Free Garden Class: Effortless Plants for Busy Gardeners — 9:30–10:30 AM, 1815 W Iron Springs Rd, Prescott. Want a gorgeous garden without spending every weekend on upkeep? This free morning class dives into low-maintenance plants that actually thrive in the Arizona climate. Expect practical picks and care tips aimed at busy gardeners who would rather relax in their yard than labour in it. Arrive curious; leave with a planting list.

[week Sun, Oct. 18] Howl-O-Ween Dog Costume Parade — 10 AM–noon, check-in 9–9:30 AM, Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village, Sedona; registration $20, benefiting the Humane Society of Sedona. Costumed canines parade through the courtyards for $100 prizes as Doggone Cutest, Craziest Canine, and Leaders of the Pack, with a 50/50 raffle and swag bags besides. Dress up your dog, yourself, or the whole family. Spectators line the route — pure Sedona charm with wagging tails. | Sedona Community Farmers Market — winter hours — 11 AM–3 PM, Wells Fargo Bank parking lot, 2201 W State Route 89A, West Sedona. The market settles into its Sunday winter hours with live music and vendors offering pastured chicken, grass-fed beef, artisan bakery goods, fish, honey, eggs, and pot pies. Seasonal produce, specialty foods, and handmade crafts fill out the stalls. Leashed, well-behaved dogs are welcome. A slow Sunday browse under the red rocks.

[week Mon, Oct. 19] D.A. Ranch Paint Out — Sedona Plein Air Festival — 4–7 PM, D.A. Ranch, Cornville; $45 per guest, limited tickets. Watch festival artists paint across the ranch grounds from 4–6 PM, among the historic red barn, pastures, ponds, orchards, and vineyards. Awards and an exclusive sale of the works created that very afternoon follow at 6:30 PM. D.A. Ranch wines are for sale, with a grazing table and live music. Golden-hour art, wine, and music in the Verde Valley.

[week Tue, Oct. 20] Trail Day Volunteer Build — 7 AM–noon, on Hwy 87 just before Pine, with PINE Strawberry Fuel Reduction. “Don’t just use the trail — help build it”: volunteers clear brush, move rocks, break roots, and shape a trail the community will use for years. The work also creates better access routes for firefighters and emergency crews. Tools are provided; bring water, sunscreen, gloves if you have them, and sturdy shoes. Email trails@psfuelreduction.org for directions.

[week Wed, Oct. 21] Long-Term Water Management Plan Community Meeting — 1–3 PM, Prescott Public Library, 215 E Goodwin St, Prescott. City staff open with a 45-minute presentation on Prescott’s water supplies, current and future needs, and strategies for conservation and efficiency. Information stations follow, where residents can talk one-to-one with City representatives and take a community survey. Can’t attend? The survey is online, and your input still feeds the plan’s first draft. Dry-country homework that truly matters. | Paint Out at a Private Sedona Residence — 4–7 PM, private Sedona residence, address with ticket; $60 per guest, limited tickets. The Plein Air Festival’s most intimate evening: a small audience watches artists paint from 4–6 PM amid sweeping red-rock views. Awards and an exclusive sale of the afternoon’s works begin at 6:30 PM. Wine, beer, and Southwest BBQ are served as the sun sets. Part art show, part garden party, part treasure hunt.

[week Thu, Oct. 22] Camp Carpe Diem Verde Valley 2026 opens — Oct. 22–25, basecamp at Verde River RV Resort & Cottages, Camp Verde; ticketed. A grown-up camp and “UnRally” for RVers, van-lifers, tent campers, and travellers: four days exploring the valley’s hiking, biking, breweries, wineries, and ghost towns. Organisers handle the details; campers pick how much or how little to do, with community dinners along the way. This year’s edition lands at peak fall colour. Come for the adventure; stay for the company.

[week Fri, Oct. 23] Paint & Sip “Three Ghosts” — 6 PM, 100 N White Mountain Rd, Ste 101, Show Low. A Halloween-week paint night: settle in with a brush and a sip to create “Three Ghosts,” a seasonal canvas to take home. The listing points painters to Kittles Fine Art for full information and registration under “Upcoming Classes.” A relaxed Fredas-evening way to start the last weekend before Halloween. The ghosts, we are assured, are friendly ones.

[merchant name] Oak Creek Brewing Company

[merchant town] Sedona

[merchant blurb] Sedona’s own working craft brewery and brewpub, handcrafting brews for more than 30 years right where you drink them — Sedona’s oldest craft brewery, pouring since 1995. The signature pour is the Nut Brown Ale — rich, nutty, with a hint of spice — with the Hefeweizen close behind, and Zen Dough’s inside turns out fresh pizza, pretzels, and cod fish and chips to go with your pint in the outdoor beer garden. Some small kindly enchantment keeps every tankard cool and every crust crisp, or so the regulars swear.

[merchant review] Great chill atmosphere! The beer is really good.

[merchant review_src] Google review

[merchant why] A true mead-hall in spirit — beer brewed on the spot, bards playing on the weekend, and a garden to sit in after a day on the red-rock trails.

[merchant visit] 2050 Yavapai Dr, Sedona, AZ 86336 · Sat noon–10 PM, Fri noon–10 PM, Mon/Wed/Thu 2–8 PM, Tue 2–11 PM (karaoke 8–11 PM), Sun noon–8 PM · 928-204-1300 · $ (easy on the purse) · Good to know: live music Fri–Sat nights and Hoppy Hour daily 4–7 PM; dogs are not permitted, and the Tlaquepaque Grill with the same beers is a different place — head for Yavapai Drive for the brewery itself.

[merchant image caption] The brewers of Oak Creek at their kettle, tankards raised in the garden beyond.

[tale title] The First Pinecone Bowling Championship

[tale] Loredas stayed dry all morning, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) declared the Hearth clearing open for the First Pinecone Bowling Championship. The pins were ten proud acorns in a row. The ball was the roundest pinecone in the forest. Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) kept score by clucking once for every pin down, which made her the busiest official in the Hold.

Earl (an elk) rolled first, with great dignity and no aim at all — his pinecone veered into Mabel’s herb basket and he declared it a practice throw. Then Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) breathed one careful ribbon of ice-mist down the lane to make it properly slick, and Jethro took his run-up just as the afternoon showers arrived.

That dang ol’ Jethro hit the slick lane at full trot, slid past the acorns, past Henny, and clean into the rain barrel, taking all ten pins down with the splash. Henny clucked ten times without stopping. The championship trophy — a shiny bottle cap from Flurry’s hoard — is still in the barrel, and Jethro says that is exactly where champions keep them.

[tale image caption] The championship roll — ten pins, one splash.

[headline] Drums, Easels, and Friday-Night Lights Fill the Holds

[dateline] Friday, October 16, 2026

[lead] Good Fredas morning, friend of the Hearth — the sun is up over the Rim, the pines stand bright in cool, clear air bound for 71 degrees, and every hold from Payson to Prescott has laid out its best for the start of the weekend. Painters carry their easels to the red rocks as Sedona’s Plein Air Festival opens, great drums thunder tonight in Prescott’s old opera house, artists stroll Camp Verde’s Main Street, and the Longhorns take the field under the lights. Tomorrow brings a bike poker run under the Rim, fall fests, and film screens — by the Nine, traveler, no one need sit idle this weekend.

[hero_caption] Painters take their easels to the red rocks while the drums sound — Fredas opens the festival weekend.

[weather] Sunny high 71 low 48 rain 0% sunrise 6:31 AM sunset 5:49 PM tomorrow Mostly cloudy, 65/50

[weather_caption] Gandy basks in the Fredas sun while Maevy hunts her butterfly.

[today Payson] October Chamber Mixer — 5 PM, The Rim Golf Club, 2000 E Rim Club Dr, Payson. The Rim Country Chamber’s monthly mixer gathers the Hold’s shopkeepers, makers, and hosts for an easy evening of handshakes and news in a handsome club setting. It is the friendliest room in town for a newcomer to learn who runs what in Rim Country. Come meet the neighbors the Hearth trades with all year. | Thatcher vs. Payson — Varsity Football — 7 PM, Payson High School field, Payson. Friday-night lights, Rim Country style: the Payson Longhorns host the Thatcher Eagles in a non-conference home game. Expect the band, the concessions, and half the Hold in the stands cheering the home boys on. A classic fall Fredas for families and football hearts alike.

[today Camp Verde] 3rd Friday Art Walk — 4–6 PM, free, around 646 S 1st St, Camp Verde. The town’s monthly third-Friday stroll returns for a relaxed early evening among local artists and downtown stops. It runs just two hours, so arrive on time and take it at a wanderer’s pace. Pair it with dinner in Camp Verde or nearby Old Town Cottonwood for a gentle Fredas outing. | Scottsdale Christian Academy vs. Camp Verde — Varsity Football — 7 PM, Camp Verde. The Camp Verde Cowboys defend their home field in a conference game under the Friday lights. Small-town football at its warmest — a hometown crowd, a cool desert evening, and a team the whole valley turns out for. Guests who love the game will feel right at home.

[today Sedona] Sedona Plein Air Festival — opening day — runs Oct. 16–24, opening at D.A. Ranch Vineyards, Cornville; tickets through Sedona Arts Center, 15 Art Barn Rd, Sedona. Accomplished outdoor painters from across the country set up their easels around Sedona and the Verde Valley to paint the red rocks live, in the very light you are standing in. Watch canvases take shape, catch demonstrations and exhibitions, and buy original paintings fresh off the easel. The festival runs nine days, so there is time to return. | “Bernstein’s Wall” — Northern Arizona premiere — showing Oct. 16–22, Mary D. Fisher Theatre, 2030 W State Route 89A, Sedona. The Sedona International Film Festival presents the Northern Arizona premiere of this film at its arthouse theatre in West Sedona. It is a fine pick for film lovers wanting something beyond the multiplex during a red-rock stay. Check the Visit Sedona calendar for the day’s showtimes before you ride over. | Friday Nights at the Theater — 7–8:30 PM, The New Room at Sedona United Methodist Church, 110 Indian Cliffs Rd, Sedona. The Arts Academy of Sedona’s monthly third-Friday showcase is a cabaret-style evening of local music, dance, poetry, comedy, and short dramatic pieces, with light refreshments. Intimate and friendly, it is a low-key way to sample Sedona’s own talent in a single evening. Valley Dwellers up for the weekend are most welcome.

[today Prescott] Taiko Extravaganza: Prayer for Peace — 7 PM, Prescott Elks Theater, 117 E Gurley St, Prescott. A thunderous evening of traditional Japanese taiko drumming inside Prescott’s historic 1905 opera house, themed as a prayer for peace. Great drums, choreographed movement, and a room built for sound — it will rattle pleasantly in your ribs. A striking night out for music lovers, and the week’s most unusual concert in any hold. | Autumn Bazaar and Bake Sale — Fri Oct. 16–Sat Oct. 17, 8 AM–3 PM, Prescott. More than twenty artisan vendors bring handmade gifts, with a bake sale, grand drawings, and a silent auction besides. All proceeds benefit local charities, so every septim spent does double duty. An easy early stop for fall and holiday gift hunting that supports the town it sits in. | Third Friday Chamber Music — 3–4 PM, Prescott. The Third Friday Chamber Music Series holds its monthly concert, this month featuring a flute quartet organized by Leanne Lawhead alongside local chamber musicians and special guests. One short, civilized hour of music — easy to pair with the bazaar beforehand and dinner downtown after. A gentle way to ease into the weekend.

[week Sat, Oct. 17] Highline Hold’em Mountain Bike Poker Run — from 9 AM, Landmark at The Creek, 1177 Christopher Creek Loop, Payson. The Rim Country Mountain Biking Association’s sixth annual nine-mile poker run on the Highline Trail beneath the Rim. Riders collect seven cards along the trail to build a five-card hand, and the best hands pick prizes back at the Landmark. Paid entry includes a 2026 T-shirt, and proceeds fund signage and care for the Highline’s 63 miles. | Fest of Fall — 12–6 PM, Posse Grounds Park, 525 Posse Ground Rd, Sedona. The City of Sedona’s big fall gathering fills one park with food trucks, craft and community vendors, pickleball and cornhole tournaments, a Kids’ Zone, a skate-park Ride Jam, a gaming center, and live music. It is run as a low- and zero-waste event, and families can wander it free. Bring a reusable water bottle — it enters you in a raffle. | Third Annual Autumn Craft Bazaar — 9 AM–2 PM, White Mountain United Methodist Church, Show Low. Local White Mountain artisans offer handmade crafts, with children’s activities and a bake sale on the side. Proceeds support church projects, the local food pantry, and the Thanksgiving Turkey Dinner Drive. Fall shopping with a community payoff — worth the ride up the mountain. | Show Low Film Festival — Sat Oct. 17–Mon Oct. 19, WME Village 8, 1501 W White Mountain Blvd, Pinetop-Lakeside. In its eighth year, the festival screens roughly a hundred selected independent films across three days, from shorts to features and documentaries. Filmmakers attend in person, with workshops on pitching, entertainment law, and more. Day passes and single-block tickets are on sale; note the films are not yet rated, and the festival says it is not suggested for children. | Arizona Blues Hall of Fame Showcase — 6 PM, Prescott Elks Theater, 117 E Gurley St, Prescott. A showcase concert celebrating Arizona Blues Hall of Fame talent in the historic Elks opera house — the same room that hosts tonight’s taiko drums. An evening of blues for fans of the genre, performed by the state’s honored players. A strong Loredas-night ticket for the Prescott hold.

[week Mon, Oct. 19] Music in the Stacks — Open Mic Night — 4–6:30 PM, free, Camp Verde Community Library, 130 Black Bridge Rd, Camp Verde. The library’s open-mic night among the shelves: local musicians and performers take turns in an informal, supportive setting. Come to play a song or simply to listen with a cup of something warm. A cozy Morndas-evening staple for the Verde Valley.

[week Tue, Oct. 20] Trail Day Volunteer Build — from 7 AM, Pine, with Pine-Strawberry Fuel Reduction. “Don’t just use the trail — help build it”: volunteers clear brush, move rocks, break roots, and shape new trail alongside the crew. The work doubles as fire-safety work, improving access routes for firefighters and emergency crews. Open to hikers, bikers, runners, and any traveler who wants to give the forest a morning.

[week Wed, Oct. 21] Long-Term Water Management Plan Community Meeting — 1–3 PM, Prescott Public Library, Prescott. City staff present Prescott’s developing Long-Term Water Management Plan — current and future water supplies, conservation, and efficiency — in a 45-minute presentation. Informal stations follow, where residents can talk with City representatives and take a community survey. For Prescott folk who want a voice in the town’s water future.

[merchant name] Smashley’s Coffee Company

[merchant town] Payson

[merchant blurb] A locally owned coffee house tucked inside the Payson Olive Oil Company shop on the Beeline, pouring specialty coffees, Americanos, lattes, and cortados, plus energy drinks and hot chocolate for the road. The signature pour is the Nutty Ex — with the Carrot Cake and Churro Americanos close behind — and the counter carries homemade bakes, from cinnamon buns and cookies to a gluten-free brownie reviewers praise by name. Some small morning enchantment keeps every foam standing tall and every bun warm, or so the regulars swear.

[merchant review] Delicious!!! My husband and I loved our drinks! He got a vanilla latte and I tried the Nutty Ex.

[merchant review_src] Tracie O. on Yelp (via Roadtrippers)

[merchant why] The Hold’s happiest morning stop — creative lattes, homemade bakes, and a patio made for slow starts before a day on the Rim.

[merchant visit] 614 N Beeline Hwy, Payson · Mon–Sat 7 AM–3 PM, Sun 8 AM–2 PM · (928) 978-6613 · $ (easy on the purse) · Good to know: it sits inside the Payson Olive Oil Company, with a back patio — browse the oils and local goods while your latte is poured.

[merchant image caption] Lattes, cinnamon buns, and olive oils under one timber roof.

[quest caption] The Hearth shield on the workbench, with the torch sconces lined up beside it.

[tale title] The Great Pumpkin Weigh-In

[tale] Fredas dawned bright and clear, and Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) declared the First Great Pumpkin Weigh-In open before breakfast. His pumpkin — raised in Mabel’s compost corner and proud of it — sat on the Hearth’s scale like a small orange hill, while Mabel (a wood elf) read the tally board and sighed in an official capacity.

Earl (an elk) had been appointed judge, mostly because he owns the steadiest face in the forest. He inspected the pumpkin from every side, nodded once with great dignity, and stepped onto the scale himself to check it was honest — at which point the needle spun clean off its pin and the pumpkin took the prize by default.

Henny (the Hearth’s chicken) rode the champion pumpkin back to the porch in state, one foot planted like a ship’s captain. Gus has already claimed the seeds, Jethro has claimed the glory, and Earl has claimed he was never on the scale at all.

[tale image caption] The champion pumpkin, its judge, and its captain.

[today Payson] Lanterns on the Lake — 6th Annual — 4 PM to sundown, Green Valley Park, 1000 W Country Club Dr. Time Out Shelter hosts this beloved gathering to raise awareness of domestic violence, and the whole Hold turns out for it. Food trucks and family activities run from 4 to 5:30 PM, with lantern decorating, face painting, and police and fire displays. The awareness walk steps off at 5:30 PM, and at sunset the decorated lanterns are launched across Green Valley Lake — a sight worth the whole trip. | A Band Called Honalee — 7 PM, 301 S McLane Rd, Payson. This modern-day folk trio relives the timeless magic of Peter, Paul and Mary, bringing classics the whole hall knows by heart to life with stirring vocal harmonies. The show also honors Dylan, Joni Mitchell, and other legends of the age. A warm Turdas evening of songs carried the way traveling bards once carried news between holds. Come ready to sing along under your breath.

[today Camp Verde] Windmill Park Farmers Market in Cornville — until 6 PM, 9950 E Cornville Rd, Cornville, a short ride from Camp Verde. This small-town market spreads through a creekside park with fresh produce, sourdough breads and baked goods, farm eggs and local honey. Look also for goat-milk soaps, jams, pickled vegetables, mushrooms, flowers, herbs, and handmade crafts. Listed rain or shine, it is an easy, tasty stop for guests bound for Sedona or Camp Verde.

[today Sedona] Sacred Qi Acupuncture Healing with Margarita Alcantara — 11 AM–5 PM, Shine Sanctuary Sedona, 162 Coffee Pot Dr, Unit D. A full daytime healing session on the sanctuary’s own October calendar, part of Shine’s regular rotation of acupuncture, energy, and sound-healing offerings. It is a calm, wellness-minded way to spend a red-rock day between hikes and galleries. Check the Shine calendar for booking details before you go, as sessions fill. | Renee Taylor Jewelry Buying Event — until 5:30 PM today, 313 AZ-179, Suite B14, Sedona. [week Fri, Oct. 16] October Chamber Mixer — 5 PM, The Rim Golf Club, 2000 E Rim Club Dr, Payson. The Rim Country Chamber’s October mixer moves to the golf club for a business-and-neighbors social on Friday evening. Meet local shopkeepers, makers, and hosts over drinks in a handsome club setting. Check the Chamber calendar for ticket and RSVP details before heading up the hill. | 3rd Friday Art Walk — 4–6 PM, free, around 646 S 1st St, Camp Verde. A gentle Friday outing for art-loving travelers. | Sedona Plein Air Festival — 22nd Annual — opens Friday and runs through Oct. 24, Sedona Arts Center, 15 Art Barn Rd, Sedona. Twenty-six invited artists paint the red rocks outdoors, in real time, across nine days. Watch canvases take shape in the very light you are standing in, at paint-out sites across the Verde Valley. [week Sat, Oct. 17] Highline Hold’em Mountain Bike Poker Run — from 9 AM, Landmark at The Creek, 1177 Christopher Creek Loop, Payson. The sixth annual nine-mile poker run on the Highline Trail is run by the Rim Country Mountain Biking Association. Riders collect seven cards along the trail to make a five-card hand, and the best hands pick prizes back at the Landmark.
