[week Fredas, 9th of Frostfall (Fri, Oct. 9)] Sky Rock Sedona — Live Music — weekend live music returns to Sky Rock Sedona, 6–9 PM, with sunset skies over the red rocks. A reliable Friday evening out in West Sedona.

[merchant name] Wild Iris Coffee House

[merchant town] Prescott

[merchant blurb] Wild Iris Coffee House is a locally owned coffee house and café on South Granite Street in Prescott, pouring espresso drinks brewed to wake the sleepiest traveler and serving pastries baked from scratch on the premises, plus light lunch fare — quiche, paninis, and sandwiches. The signature pour is the 'Bee's Knees,' a cappuccino with Arizona honey and lavender; the thing to order is the homemade breakfast sandwich on a scratch-baked biscuit. The secluded dog-friendly courtyard, with its fountain overlooking Granite Creek, is a fine spot to linger over a cup.

[merchant review] It's so nice to get away from the national chains and relax at a homegrown establishment. Plus it was toasty warm which was great after standing in the chilly afternoon overcast during the parade. But better than that was the tasty drinks and relaxed setting.

[merchant review_src] a TripAdvisor review

[merchant why] Prescott's own homegrown coffee hall — where Valley Dwellers trade the lowland heat for a cool courtyard, a honey-lavender cappuccino, and pastries still warm from the oven. On the drive from the Hearth, Montezuma Castle's cliff dwelling rises just off the trail near Camp Verde — worth a rein-pull and a likeness snared in thy pocket-glass (other travelers have called it a 'celliephone').

[merchant visit] 124 S Granite St (Ste E), Prescott, AZ 86303 — open daily 6 AM–6 PM; (928) 778-5155; $ (~$10–25 per person); the dog-friendly courtyard overlooks Granite Creek, and free Wi-Fi makes it a popular work spot — it can get crowded on busy days.

[merchant image caption] Wild Iris Coffee House, where the courtyard overlooks the creek.

[due soon] Due Loredas: the torch sconces must print today — the Hearth's torchlight waits on thee.

[quest caption] The craftsman's bench: torch sconces on the rise, tools at the ready.

[tale title] Flight School

[tale] On a blazing Loredas morning, the kind of bright where the shadows themselves squinted, Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) announced that Flurry needed landing lessons.

Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) flies in a fine straight line, Jethro explained, which is the easy part. The hard part is the arriving. Ever since the rain-barrel incident his tail has had a kink, so he flies in zigzags and lands wherever the wind argues him into — last week that was Gus the orc baker's pie-cooling rack, and the week before, Mabel's herb bed, which is still not over it.

So Jethro laid out a landing strip of pine needles in the sunny clearing, planted two tiny signal flags, and waved Flurry in. Earl (an elk) stood by as the tower, enormous antlers held high, calling the altitude in his most official voice. "Two tail-lengths! One! Flare!"

Flurry flared. Flurry zigged. Flurry zagged — and set down neat as you please in the middle of the strip, wings folded, looking enormously pleased with himself.

Jethro wept with pride. Earl logged it in the bark ledger: one good landing. Then the wind shifted, and Flurry's victory lap ended in Gus's pie rack again.

One out of two, the forest agreed, is a personal best.

[tale image caption] Flurry comes in for a landing — Jethro waves him down.

greeting: HAIL and well met, friends of the Hearth — Sundas rises over the Rim in a wash of gold, and the faire's last day is upon us: the North Inch village throws its gates open one final time, nine of the morning clock to five of the evening, for one last caber toss, one last song on the pipes, and one last stroll through the artisans' row before the tents come down. Frostfall has settled over the Hold proper now, and the week ahead runs rich: a classic car show rolls into Payson, the fort at Camp Verde celebrates its seventieth homecoming, and Sedona fills the red rocks with wings, wheels, and art. Fill thy cup, traveler — the Hold is wide awake.
headline: The Faire's Final Day — and the Week Rolls On

[headline] The Faire's Final Day — and the Week Rolls On

[dateline] Sunday, October 4, 2026

[lead] HAIL and well met, friends of the Hearth — Sundas rises over the Rim in a wash of gold, and the faire's last day is upon us: the North Inch village throws its gates open one final time, nine of the morning clock to five of the evening, for one last caber toss, one last song on the pipes, and one last stroll through the artisans' row before the tents come down. Frostfall has settled over the Hold proper now, and the week ahead runs rich: a classic car show rolls into Payson, the fort at Camp Verde celebrates its seventieth homecoming, and Sedona fills the red rocks with wings, wheels, and art. Fill thy cup, traveler — the Hold is wide awake.

[hero_caption] The faire's last day: one final caber toss, one last round of the village — Sundas, nine of the morning clock to five of the evening.

[weather] Sunny high 82 low 57 rain 1% sunrise 6:22 AM sunset 6:05 PM tomorrow Sunny, 79/58

[weather_caption] Henny claims the sunniest plank of the deck and basks like a thane on holiday, daring the sky to cloud over.

[weather_overheard] Overheard Last Night — The garlic braid sold out at the market Saturday — the vendor swears she never saw the buyers, only a neat stack of coins left on her counter. The barkeep only shrugged: “Aye. They only ever shop when the nights run long.”

[today Payson] North Inch Renaissance Faire — the inaugural Scottish faire's last day: artisans, combat demonstrations, Highland games, and the court of Mary Queen of Scots, 9 AM–5 PM at the Payson Golf Course, 1504 W Country Club Dr | The Sketch Mob – Renaissance Style — a sketching meetup in faire garb, 10 AM at Fairways Dining in the Payson Golf Club

[today Pine-Strawberry] 36th Annual Pine-Strawberry Craft Fair — vendors galore beneath the Rim, 8 AM–4 PM at the Pine-Strawberry Community Center ramada, 3886 N Hwy 87, Pine

[today Sedona] Sedona Community Farmers Market — the Sunday market runs 8 AM–noon at the Wells Fargo lot, 2201 W State Route 89A, per the market's own site | “Love & Laughter” Comedy Night — ninety minutes of stand-up from the Sedona International Film Festival, 7–8:30 PM at the Mary D. Fisher Theatre | Sedona Yoga Festival — last day of the four-day wellness gathering among the red rocks

[today Show Low] White Mountain Church Group disc golf — a casual Sunday round, 9 AM–noon

[today Prescott] Dogtoberfest and Adopt-a-Thon — pet adoptions and four-legged merriment, 10 AM at 3101 Watson Lake Rd | Prescott Fall Arts & Crafts Show — last day: artists, craftsmen, and food vendors on the Yavapai County Courthouse Plaza | Arizona Philharmonic: Beethoven and Mozart — the Violin Concerto and the Jupiter Symphony, 3 PM at the Ruth Street Theater, 1050 Ruth St; tickets $28–69

[week Tue, Oct. 6] Trail Day Volunteer Build — lend thy hands to the trails: a volunteer trail-build day along Highway 87 in Pine, starting 7 AM. Bring work gloves and a stout heart; the forest thanks its tenders. | Nursing & Allied Health Job Fair — Northland Pioneer College opens its Show Low Campus Learning Center lobby, noon–1:30 PM, to job seekers. Health-care employers with open positions will be on hand, and the public is welcome.

[week Wed, Oct. 7] Brit Floyd — the world-touring Pink Floyd tribute brings its full spectacle to the Findlay Toyota Center in Prescott Valley, 7 PM. A night of classic rock under the arena lights.

[week Fri, Oct. 9] 33rd Annual Beeline Cruise-In Classic Car Show — the weekend roars to life Friday with a classic car cruise around town and the “Burger Burn” cookout at Rumsey Park. Saturday brings the main show on the grass at Green Valley Park — 2001-and-older cars, trucks, low riders, and rat rods. | Prescott Antique Show & Vintage Market — treasure-hunting at the Prescott Rodeo Grounds, starting noon Friday. Antiques and vintage wares for every purse.

[week Sat, Oct. 10] 70th Annual Fort Verde Days — Camp Verde's homecoming weekend at Fort Verde State Historic Park, Saturday and Sunday: flag ceremonies, cannon demonstrations, living-history re-enactors, Dutch oven cooking, a people's-choice chili cook-off, and a parade down Main Street Saturday at 10 AM. Free fort entry both days. | Wings & Wheels — static aircraft displays, vintage warbirds, and airplane and helicopter rides at the Sedona Airport, 9 AM, alongside the Sedona Car Club show. Admission is a non-perishable food item or $2. | 34th Annual Sedona Arts Festival — more than a hundred juried artists gather at Sedona Red Rock High School, Saturday 9 AM–5 PM and Sunday 10 AM–4 PM. Live music, food trucks, and a beer and wine garden round out the red-rocks weekend.

[merchant name] Red Rose Thriftique

[merchant town] Sedona

[merchant blurb] A thrift store and artist boutique in Bell Rock Plaza, in the Village of Oak Creek — home decor, clothing, books, jewelry, and a steady rotation of secondhand treasures. Every single coin of profit flows to Red Rose Inspiration For Animals, funding free spay-and-neuter, emergency vet bills, and rescue work across the Verde Valley. The signature hunt: dig the racks for that one perfect find, then feel twice as good about the price — the beasts eat because thou didst shop.

[merchant review] Red Rose Thriftique is a beautiful and unique store whose proceeds benefit animal rescue groups. All items are of quality and you can't beat the prices.

[merchant review_src] a Birdeye review

[merchant why] The Hearth sends its guests to shop where every purchase feeds a rescue beast — treasure-hunting with a warm heart.

[tale title] The Guest Book

[tale] Sundas dawned warm as a fresh honey-cake, and the road past the Hearth filled with faire-folk and Valley Dwellers trading the lowland heat for Rim Country air — which put Jethro (the Mogollon Monster) in a welcoming frame of mind.

“The Hearth needs a guest book,” he announced, and dragged a hollow log up to the front door.

Being a monster of few letters, Jethro's guest book required no writing: each traveler dropped one shiny thing into the log. Flurry (a young ice-breathing dragon) appointed himself curator, rejecting three pinecones and a lost button before Mabel (a wood elf) ruled that sentiment counted.

Henny (the Hearth's plump Skyrim-style chicken) inspected each offering for edibility, and found them all wanting.

When a little girl dropped in a bottle cap polished to mirror-bright, Jethro was so moved he tried to hug the whole log — and tipped it clean over. Forty-seven shinies rolled down the sunlit deck in every direction. Flurry zigzagged after them on his kinked tail, collecting them twice as fast as they rolled, while Earl (an elk) stood very still in the middle of it all, dignity intact, pretending with great success that nothing was happening.

Mabel righted the log, declared it a guest log in the most literal sense, and Gus (an orc baker) arrived with honey-cakes — which Jethro entered into the book the only way he knew how: he drew a picture of a chicken judging a pinecone.

[tale image caption] The guest log's first entry: one bottle cap, mirror-bright.
